143// Environment-describing macros
144// -----------------------------
145//
146// Google Test can be used in many different environments. Macros in
147// this section tell Google Test what kind of environment it is being
148// used in, such that Google Test can provide environment-specific
149// features and implementations.
150//
151// Google Test tries to automatically detect the properties of its
152// environment, so users usually don't need to worry about these
153// macros. However, the automatic detection is not perfect.
154// Sometimes it's necessary for a user to define some of the following
155// macros in the build script to override Google Test's decisions.
156//
157// If the user doesn't define a macro in the list, Google Test will
158// provide a default definition. After this header is #included, all
159// macros in this list will be defined to either 1 or 0.
160//
161// Notes to maintainers:
162// - Each macro here is a user-tweakable knob; do not grow the list
163// lightly.
164// - Use #if to key off these macros. Don't use #ifdef or "#if
165// defined(...)", which will not work as these macros are ALWAYS
166// defined.
167//
168// GTEST_HAS_CLONE - Define it to 1/0 to indicate that clone(2)
169// is/isn't available.
170// GTEST_HAS_EXCEPTIONS - Define it to 1/0 to indicate that exceptions
171// are enabled.
172// GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_STRING - Define it to 1/0 to indicate that ::string
173// is/isn't available
174// GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_WSTRING - Define it to 1/0 to indicate that ::wstring
175// is/isn't available
176// GTEST_HAS_POSIX_RE - Define it to 1/0 to indicate that POSIX regular
177// expressions are/aren't available.
178// GTEST_HAS_PTHREAD - Define it to 1/0 to indicate that <pthread.h>
179// is/isn't available.
180// GTEST_HAS_RTTI - Define it to 1/0 to indicate that RTTI is/isn't
181// enabled.
182// GTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING - Define it to 1/0 to indicate that
183// std::wstring does/doesn't work (Google Test can
184// be used where std::wstring is unavailable).
185// GTEST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE - Define it to 1/0 to indicate tr1::tuple
186// is/isn't available.
187// GTEST_HAS_SEH - Define it to 1/0 to indicate whether the
188// compiler supports Microsoft's "Structured
189// Exception Handling".
190// GTEST_HAS_STREAM_REDIRECTION
191// - Define it to 1/0 to indicate whether the
192// platform supports I/O stream redirection using
193// dup() and dup2().
194// GTEST_USE_OWN_TR1_TUPLE - Define it to 1/0 to indicate whether Google
195// Test's own tr1 tuple implementation should be
196// used. Unused when the user sets
197// GTEST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE to 0.
198// GTEST_LANG_CXX11 - Define it to 1/0 to indicate that Google Test
199// is building in C++11/C++98 mode.
200// GTEST_LINKED_AS_SHARED_LIBRARY
201// - Define to 1 when compiling tests that use
202// Google Test as a shared library (known as
203// DLL on Windows).
204// GTEST_CREATE_SHARED_LIBRARY
205// - Define to 1 when compiling Google Test itself
206// as a shared library.
207// GTEST_DEFAULT_DEATH_TEST_STYLE
208// - The default value of --gtest_death_test_style.
209// The legacy default has been "fast" in the open
210// source version since 2008. The recommended value
211// is "threadsafe", and can be set in
212// custom/gtest-port.h.
213
214// Platform-indicating macros
215// --------------------------
216//
217// Macros indicating the platform on which Google Test is being used
218// (a macro is defined to 1 if compiled on the given platform;
219// otherwise UNDEFINED -- it's never defined to 0.). Google Test
220// defines these macros automatically. Code outside Google Test MUST
221// NOT define them.
222//
223// GTEST_OS_AIX - IBM AIX
224// GTEST_OS_CYGWIN - Cygwin
225// GTEST_OS_FREEBSD - FreeBSD
226// GTEST_OS_FUCHSIA - Fuchsia
227// GTEST_OS_HPUX - HP-UX
228// GTEST_OS_LINUX - Linux
229// GTEST_OS_LINUX_ANDROID - Google Android
230// GTEST_OS_MAC - Mac OS X
231// GTEST_OS_IOS - iOS
232// GTEST_OS_NACL - Google Native Client (NaCl)
233// GTEST_OS_NETBSD - NetBSD
234// GTEST_OS_OPENBSD - OpenBSD
235// GTEST_OS_QNX - QNX
236// GTEST_OS_SOLARIS - Sun Solaris
237// GTEST_OS_SYMBIAN - Symbian
238// GTEST_OS_WINDOWS - Windows (Desktop, MinGW, or Mobile)
239// GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_DESKTOP - Windows Desktop
240// GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MINGW - MinGW
241// GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE - Windows Mobile
242// GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE - Windows Phone
243// GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT - Windows Store App/WinRT
244// GTEST_OS_ZOS - z/OS
245//
246// Among the platforms, Cygwin, Linux, Max OS X, and Windows have the
247// most stable support. Since core members of the Google Test project
248// don't have access to other platforms, support for them may be less
249// stable. If you notice any problems on your platform, please notify
250// googletestframework@googlegroups.com (patches for fixing them are
251// even more welcome!).
252//
253// It is possible that none of the GTEST_OS_* macros are defined.
254
255// Feature-indicating macros
256// -------------------------
257//
258// Macros indicating which Google Test features are available (a macro
259// is defined to 1 if the corresponding feature is supported;
260// otherwise UNDEFINED -- it's never defined to 0.). Google Test
261// defines these macros automatically. Code outside Google Test MUST
262// NOT define them.
263//
264// These macros are public so that portable tests can be written.
265// Such tests typically surround code using a feature with an #if
266// which controls that code. For example:
267//
268// #if GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
269// EXPECT_DEATH(DoSomethingDeadly());
270// #endif
271//
272// GTEST_HAS_COMBINE - the Combine() function (for value-parameterized
273// tests)
274// GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST - death tests
275// GTEST_HAS_TYPED_TEST - typed tests
276// GTEST_HAS_TYPED_TEST_P - type-parameterized tests
277// GTEST_IS_THREADSAFE - Google Test is thread-safe.
278// GOOGLETEST_CM0007 DO NOT DELETE
279// GTEST_USES_POSIX_RE - enhanced POSIX regex is used. Do not confuse with
280// GTEST_HAS_POSIX_RE (see above) which users can
281// define themselves.
282// GTEST_USES_SIMPLE_RE - our own simple regex is used;
283// the above RE\b(s) are mutually exclusive.
284// GTEST_CAN_COMPARE_NULL - accepts untyped NULL in EXPECT_EQ().
285
286// Misc public macros
287// ------------------
288//
289// GTEST_FLAG(flag_name) - references the variable corresponding to
290// the given Google Test flag.
291
292// Internal utilities
293// ------------------
294//
295// The following macros and utilities are for Google Test's INTERNAL
296// use only. Code outside Google Test MUST NOT USE THEM DIRECTLY.
297//
298// Macros for basic C++ coding:
299// GTEST_AMBIGUOUS_ELSE_BLOCKER_ - for disabling a gcc warning.
300// GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_ - declares that a class' instances or a
301// variable don't have to be used.
302// GTEST_DISALLOW_ASSIGN_ - disables operator=.
303// GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_ - disables copy ctor and operator=.
304// GTEST_MUST_USE_RESULT_ - declares that a function's result must be used.
305// GTEST_INTENTIONAL_CONST_COND_PUSH_ - start code section where MSVC C4127 is
306// suppressed (constant conditional).
307// GTEST_INTENTIONAL_CONST_COND_POP_ - finish code section where MSVC C4127
308// is suppressed.
309//
310// C++11 feature wrappers:
311//
312// testing::internal::forward - portability wrapper for std::forward.
313// testing::internal::move - portability wrapper for std::move.
314//
315// Synchronization:
316// Mutex, MutexLock, ThreadLocal, GetThreadCount()
317// - synchronization primitives.
318//
319// Template meta programming:
320// is_pointer - as in TR1; needed on Symbian and IBM XL C/C++ only.
321// IteratorTraits - partial implementation of std::iterator_traits, which
322// is not available in libCstd when compiled with Sun C++.
323//
324// Smart pointers:
325// scoped_ptr - as in TR2.
326//
327// Regular expressions:
328// RE - a simple regular expression class using the POSIX
329// Extended Regular Expression syntax on UNIX-like platforms
330// GOOGLETEST_CM0008 DO NOT DELETE
331// or a reduced regular exception syntax on other
332// platforms, including Windows.
333// Logging:
334// GTEST_LOG_() - logs messages at the specified severity level.
335// LogToStderr() - directs all log messages to stderr.
336// FlushInfoLog() - flushes informational log messages.
337//
338// Stdout and stderr capturing:
339// CaptureStdout() - starts capturing stdout.
340// GetCapturedStdout() - stops capturing stdout and returns the captured
341// string.
342// CaptureStderr() - starts capturing stderr.
343// GetCapturedStderr() - stops capturing stderr and returns the captured
344// string.
345//
346// Integer types:
347// TypeWithSize - maps an integer to a int type.
348// Int32, UInt32, Int64, UInt64, TimeInMillis
349// - integers of known sizes.
350// BiggestInt - the biggest signed integer type.
351//
352// Command-line utilities:
353// GTEST_DECLARE_*() - declares a flag.
354// GTEST_DEFINE_*() - defines a flag.
355// GetInjectableArgvs() - returns the command line as a vector of strings.
356//
357// Environment variable utilities:
358// GetEnv() - gets the value of an environment variable.
359// BoolFromGTestEnv() - parses a bool environment variable.
360// Int32FromGTestEnv() - parses an Int32 environment variable.
361// StringFromGTestEnv() - parses a string environment variable.

427#define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS 0
428#define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE 0

430#define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_DESKTOP 0
431#define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE 0
432#define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_TV_TITLE 0
433#define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT 0
434#define GTEST_OS_MAC 0
435#define GTEST_OS_LINUX 0
436#define GTEST_OS_LINUX_ANDROID 0
437#define GTEST_OS_ZOS 0
438#define GTEST_OS_SOLARIS 0
439#define GTEST_OS_AIX 0
440#define GTEST_OS_HPUX 0
441#define GTEST_OS_NACL 0
442#define GTEST_OS_OPENBSD 0
443#define GTEST_OS_QNX 0
444#define GTEST_OS_IOS 0

446#define GTEST_OS_FREEBSD 0

450#ifdef __CYGWIN__
451# undef GTEST_OS_CYGWIN
452# define GTEST_OS_CYGWIN 1
453#elif defined __SYMBIAN32__
454# undef GTEST_OS_SYMBIAN
455# define GTEST_OS_SYMBIAN 1
456#elif defined _WIN32
457# undef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
458# define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS 1
459# ifdef _WIN32_WCE
460# undef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
461# define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE 1
462# elif defined(__MINGW__) || defined(__MINGW32__)
463# undef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MINGW
464# define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MINGW 1
465# elif defined(WINAPI_FAMILY)
466# include <winapifamily.h>
467# if WINAPI_FAMILY_PARTITION(WINAPI_PARTITION_DESKTOP)
468# undef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_DESKTOP
469# define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_DESKTOP 1
470# elif WINAPI_FAMILY_PARTITION(WINAPI_PARTITION_PHONE_APP)
471# undef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE
472# define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE 1
473# elif WINAPI_FAMILY_PARTITION(WINAPI_PARTITION_APP)
474# undef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT
475# define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT 1
476# elif WINAPI_FAMILY_PARTITION(WINAPI_PARTITION_TV_TITLE)
477# undef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE
478# undef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_TV_TITLE
479# define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE 1
480# define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_TV_TITLE 1
481# else
482 // WINAPI_FAMILY defined but no known partition matched.
483 // Default to desktop.
484# undef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_DESKTOP
485# define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_DESKTOP 1
486# endif
487# else
488# undef GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_DESKTOP
489# define GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_DESKTOP 1
490# endif // _WIN32_WCE
491#elif defined __APPLE__
492# undef GTEST_OS_MAC
493# define GTEST_OS_MAC 1
494# if TARGET_OS_IPHONE
495# undef GTEST_OS_IOS
496# define GTEST_OS_IOS 1
497# if TARGET_IPHONE_SIMULATOR
498# undef GTEST_OS_IOS_SIMULATOR
499# define GTEST_OS_IOS_SIMULATOR 1
500# endif
501# endif
502#elif defined __FreeBSD__
503# undef GTEST_OS_FREEBSD
504# define GTEST_OS_FREEBSD 1
505#elif defined __Fuchsia__
506# undef GTEST_OS_FUCHSIA
507# define GTEST_OS_FUCHSIA 1
508#elif defined __linux__
509# undef GTEST_OS_LINUX
510# define GTEST_OS_LINUX 1
511# if defined __ANDROID__
512# undef GTEST_OS_LINUX_ANDROID
513# define GTEST_OS_LINUX_ANDROID 1
514# endif
515#elif defined __MVS__
516# undef GTEST_OS_ZOS
517# define GTEST_OS_ZOS 1
518#elif defined(__sun) && defined(__SVR4)
519# undef GTEST_OS_SOLARIS
520# define GTEST_OS_SOLARIS 1
521#elif defined(_AIX)
522# undef GTEST_OS_AIX
523# define GTEST_OS_AIX 1
524#elif defined(__hpux)
525# undef GTEST_OS_HPUX
526# define GTEST_OS_HPUX 1
527#elif defined __native_client__
528# undef GTEST_OS_NACL
529# define GTEST_OS_NACL 1
530#elif defined __NetBSD__
531# undef GTEST_OS_NETBSD
532# define GTEST_OS_NETBSD 1
533#elif defined __OpenBSD__
534# undef GTEST_OS_OPENBSD
535# define GTEST_OS_OPENBSD 1
536#elif defined __QNX__
537# undef GTEST_OS_QNX
538# define GTEST_OS_QNX 1
539#endif // __CYGWIN__

600// Determines the version of gcc that is used to compile this.
601#ifdef __GNUC__

1169// In theory, defining stuff in the ::std namespace is undefined
1170// behavior. We can do this as we are playing the role of a standard
1171// library vendor.

1176 typename T3 = void, typename T4 = void, typename T5 = void,

1181// Anything in namespace gtest_internal is Google Test's INTERNAL
1182// IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL and MUST NOT BE USED DIRECTLY in user code.
1183namespace gtest_internal {

1185// ByRef<T>::type is T if T is a reference; otherwise it's const T&.
1186template <typename T>
1187struct ByRef { typedef const T& type; }; // NOLINT
1188template <typename T>
1189struct ByRef<T&> { typedef T& type; }; // NOLINT
1190
1191// A handy wrapper for ByRef.
1192#define GTEST_BY_REF_(T) typename ::std::tr1::gtest_internal::ByRef<T>::type
1193
1194// AddRef<T>::type is T if T is a reference; otherwise it's T&. This
1195// is the same as tr1::add_reference<T>::type.
1196template <typename T>
1197struct AddRef { typedef T& type; }; // NOLINT
1198template <typename T>
1199struct AddRef<T&> { typedef T& type; }; // NOLINT
1200
1201// A handy wrapper for AddRef.
1202#define GTEST_ADD_REF_(T) typename ::std::tr1::gtest_internal::AddRef<T>::type
1203
1204// A helper for implementing get<k>().
1205template <int k> class Get;
1206
1207// A helper for implementing tuple_element<k, T>. kIndexValid is true
1208// iff k < the number of fields in tuple type T.
1209template <bool kIndexValid, int kIndex, class Tuple>
1210struct TupleElement;

1679 explicit tuple(GTEST_BY_REF_(T0) f0, GTEST_BY_REF_(T1) f1,
1680 GTEST_BY_REF_(T2) f2, GTEST_BY_REF_(T3) f3, GTEST_BY_REF_(T4) f4,
1681 GTEST_BY_REF_(T5) f5, GTEST_BY_REF_(T6) f6, GTEST_BY_REF_(T7) f7,
1682 GTEST_BY_REF_(T8) f8, GTEST_BY_REF_(T9) f9) : f0_(f0), f1_(f1), f2_(f2),
1683 f3_(f3), f4_(f4), f5_(f5), f6_(f6), f7_(f7), f8_(f8), f9_(f9) {}
1684
1685 tuple(const tuple& t) : f0_(t.f0_), f1_(t.f1_), f2_(t.f2_), f3_(t.f3_),
1686 f4_(t.f4_), f5_(t.f5_), f6_(t.f6_), f7_(t.f7_), f8_(t.f8_), f9_(t.f9_) {}
1687
1688 template <GTEST_10_TYPENAMES_(U)>
1689 tuple(const GTEST_10_TUPLE_(U)& t) : f0_(t.f0_), f1_(t.f1_), f2_(t.f2_),
1690 f3_(t.f3_), f4_(t.f4_), f5_(t.f5_), f6_(t.f6_), f7_(t.f7_), f8_(t.f8_),
1691 f9_(t.f9_) {}
1692
1693 tuple& operator=(const tuple& t) { return CopyFrom(t); }
1694
1695 template <GTEST_10_TYPENAMES_(U)>
1696 tuple& operator=(const GTEST_10_TUPLE_(U)& t) {
1697 return CopyFrom(t);
1698 }

1702 template <GTEST_10_TYPENAMES_(U)>
1703 tuple& CopyFrom(const GTEST_10_TUPLE_(U)& t) {
1704 f0_ = t.f0_;
1705 f1_ = t.f1_;
1706 f2_ = t.f2_;
1707 f3_ = t.f3_;
1708 f4_ = t.f4_;
1709 f5_ = t.f5_;
1710 f6_ = t.f6_;
1711 f7_ = t.f7_;
1712 f8_ = t.f8_;
1713 f9_ = t.f9_;
1714 return *this;
1715 }
1716
1717 T0 f0_;
1718 T1 f1_;
1719 T2 f2_;
1720 T3 f3_;
1721 T4 f4_;
1722 T5 f5_;
1723 T6 f6_;
1724 T7 f7_;
1725 T8 f8_;
1726 T9 f9_;
1727};

2001// 6.1.3.5 Relational operators
2002
2003// We only implement == and !=, as we don't have a need for the rest yet.
2004
2005namespace gtest_internal {
2006
2007// SameSizeTuplePrefixComparator<k, k>::Eq(t1, t2) returns true if the
2008// first k fields of t1 equals the first k fields of t2.
2009// SameSizeTuplePrefixComparator(k1, k2) would be a compiler error if
2010// k1 != k2.
2011template <int kSize1, int kSize2>
2012struct SameSizeTuplePrefixComparator;
2013
2014template <>
2015struct SameSizeTuplePrefixComparator<0, 0> {
2016 template <class Tuple1, class Tuple2>
2017 static bool Eq(const Tuple1& /* t1 */, const Tuple2& /* t2 */) {
2018 return true;
2019 }
2020};
2021
2022template <int k>
2023struct SameSizeTuplePrefixComparator<k, k> {
2024 template <class Tuple1, class Tuple2>
2025 static bool Eq(const Tuple1& t1, const Tuple2& t2) {
2026 return SameSizeTuplePrefixComparator<k - 1, k - 1>::Eq(t1, t2) &&
2027 ::std::tr1::get<k - 1>(t1) == ::std::tr1::get<k - 1>(t2);
2028 }
2029};
2030
2031} // namespace gtest_internal
2032
2033template <GTEST_10_TYPENAMES_(T), GTEST_10_TYPENAMES_(U)>
2034inline bool operator==(const GTEST_10_TUPLE_(T)& t,
2035 const GTEST_10_TUPLE_(U)& u) {
2036 return gtest_internal::SameSizeTuplePrefixComparator<
2037 tuple_size<GTEST_10_TUPLE_(T) >::value,
2038 tuple_size<GTEST_10_TUPLE_(U) >::value>::Eq(t, u);
2039}
2040
2041template <GTEST_10_TYPENAMES_(T), GTEST_10_TYPENAMES_(U)>
2042inline bool operator!=(const GTEST_10_TUPLE_(T)& t,
2043 const GTEST_10_TUPLE_(U)& u) { return !(t == u); }

2083// On Symbian, BOOST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE causes Boost's TR1 tuple library to
2084// use STLport's tuple implementation, which unfortunately doesn't
2085// work as the copy of STLport distributed with Symbian is incomplete.
2086// By making sure BOOST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE is undefined, we force Boost to
2087// use its own tuple implementation.

2089# undef BOOST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE
2090# endif // BOOST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE
2091
2092// This prevents <boost/tr1/detail/config.hpp>, which defines
2093// BOOST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE, from being #included by Boost's <tuple>.
2094# define BOOST_TR1_DETAIL_CONFIG_HPP_INCLUDED
2095# include <tuple> // IWYU pragma: export // NOLINT
2096
2097# elif defined(__GNUC__) && (GTEST_GCC_VER_ >= 40000)
2098// GCC 4.0+ implements tr1/tuple in the <tr1/tuple> header. This does
2099// not conform to the TR1 spec, which requires the header to be <tuple>.
2100
2101# if !GTEST_HAS_RTTI && GTEST_GCC_VER_ < 40302
2102// Until version 4.3.2, gcc has a bug that causes <tr1/functional>,
2103// which is #included by <tr1/tuple>, to not compile when RTTI is
2104// disabled. _TR1_FUNCTIONAL is the header guard for
2105// <tr1/functional>. Hence the following #define is used to prevent
2106// <tr1/functional> from being included.
2107# define _TR1_FUNCTIONAL 1
2108# include <tr1/tuple>
2109# undef _TR1_FUNCTIONAL // Allows the user to #include
2110 // <tr1/functional> if they choose to.
2111# else
2112# include <tr1/tuple> // NOLINT
2113# endif // !GTEST_HAS_RTTI && GTEST_GCC_VER_ < 40302
2114
2115// VS 2010 now has tr1 support.
2116# elif defined(_MSC_VER) && _MSC_VER >= 1600
2117# include <tuple> // IWYU pragma: export // NOLINT
2118
2119# else // GTEST_USE_OWN_TR1_TUPLE
2120# include <tr1/tuple> // IWYU pragma: export // NOLINT
2121# endif // GTEST_USE_OWN_TR1_TUPLE
2122
2123#endif // GTEST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE

2141# else

2144# else

2211// Defines some utility macros.
2212
2213// The GNU compiler emits a warning if nested "if" statements are followed by
2214// an "else" statement and braces are not used to explicitly disambiguate the
2215// "else" binding. This leads to problems with code like:
2216//
2217// if (gate)
2218// ASSERT_*(condition) << "Some message";
2219//
2220// The "switch (0) case 0:" idiom is used to suppress this.
2221#ifdef __INTEL_COMPILER
2222# define GTEST_AMBIGUOUS_ELSE_BLOCKER_
2223#else
2224# define GTEST_AMBIGUOUS_ELSE_BLOCKER_ switch (0) case 0: default: // NOLINT
2225#endif
2226
2227// Use this annotation at the end of a struct/class definition to
2228// prevent the compiler from optimizing away instances that are never
2229// used. This is useful when all interesting logic happens inside the
2230// c'tor and / or d'tor. Example:
2231//
2232// struct Foo {
2233// Foo() { ... }
2234// } GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_;
2235//

2429// The GTEST_COMPILE_ASSERT_ macro can be used to verify that a compile time
2430// expression is true. For example, you could use it to verify the
2431// size of a static array:
2432//
2433// GTEST_COMPILE_ASSERT_(GTEST_ARRAY_SIZE_(names) == NUM_NAMES,
2434// names_incorrect_size);
2435//
2436// or to make sure a struct is smaller than a certain size:
2437//
2438// GTEST_COMPILE_ASSERT_(sizeof(foo) < 128, foo_too_large);
2439//
2440// The second argument to the macro is the name of the variable. If
2441// the expression is false, most compilers will issue a warning/error
2442// containing the name of the variable.
2443
2444#if GTEST_LANG_CXX11
2445# define GTEST_COMPILE_ASSERT_(expr, msg) static_assert(expr, #msg)
2446#else // !GTEST_LANG_CXX11
2447template <bool>
2448 struct CompileAssert {
2449};
2450
2451# define GTEST_COMPILE_ASSERT_(expr, msg) \
2452 typedef ::testing::internal::CompileAssert<(static_cast<bool>(expr))> \
2453 msg[static_cast<bool>(expr) ? 1 : -1] GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_
2454#endif // !GTEST_LANG_CXX11
2455
2456// Implementation details of GTEST_COMPILE_ASSERT_:
2457//
2458// (In C++11, we simply use static_assert instead of the following)
2459//
2460// - GTEST_COMPILE_ASSERT_ works by defining an array type that has -1
2461// elements (and thus is invalid) when the expression is false.
2462//
2463// - The simpler definition
2464//
2465// #define GTEST_COMPILE_ASSERT_(expr, msg) typedef char msg[(expr) ? 1 : -1]
2466//
2467// does not work, as gcc supports variable-length arrays whose sizes
2468// are determined at run-time (this is gcc's extension and not part
2469// of the C++ standard). As a result, gcc fails to reject the
2470// following code with the simple definition:
2471//
2472// int foo;
2473// GTEST_COMPILE_ASSERT_(foo, msg); // not supposed to compile as foo is
2474// // not a compile-time constant.
2475//
2476// - By using the type CompileAssert<(bool(expr))>, we ensures that
2477// expr is a compile-time constant. (Template arguments must be
2478// determined at compile-time.)
2479//
2480// - The outter parentheses in CompileAssert<(bool(expr))> are necessary
2481// to work around a bug in gcc 3.4.4 and 4.0.1. If we had written
2482//
2483// CompileAssert<bool(expr)>
2484//
2485// instead, these compilers will refuse to compile
2486//
2487// GTEST_COMPILE_ASSERT_(5 > 0, some_message);
2488//
2489// (They seem to think the ">" in "5 > 0" marks the end of the
2490// template argument list.)
2491//
2492// - The array size is (bool(expr) ? 1 : -1), instead of simply
2493//
2494// ((expr) ? 1 : -1).
2495//
2496// This is to avoid running into a bug in MS VC 7.1, which
2497// causes ((0.0) ? 1 : -1) to incorrectly evaluate to 1.
2498

2539template <typename T> class scoped_ptr;
2540template <typename T> static void swap(scoped_ptr<T>& a, scoped_ptr<T>& b);
2541
2542// Defines scoped_ptr.
2543
2544// This implementation of scoped_ptr is PARTIAL - it only contains
2545// enough stuff to satisfy Google Test's need.
2546template <typename T>
2547class scoped_ptr {
2548 public:
2549 typedef T element_type;
2550
2551 explicit scoped_ptr(T* p = NULL) : ptr_(p) {}
2552 ~scoped_ptr() { reset(); }
2553
2554 T& operator*() const { return *ptr_; }
2555 T* operator->() const { return ptr_; }
2556 T* get() const { return ptr_; }
2557
2558 T* release() {
2559 T* const ptr = ptr_;
2560 ptr_ = NULL;
2561 return ptr;
2562 }
2563
2564 void reset(T* p = NULL) {
2565 if (p != ptr_) {
2566 if (IsTrue(sizeof(T) > 0)) { // Makes sure T is a complete type.
2567 delete ptr_;
2568 }
2569 ptr_ = p;
2570 }
2571 }
2572
2573 friend void swap<T>(scoped_ptr<T>& a, scoped_ptr<T>& b);
2574
2575 private:
2576 T* ptr_;
2577
2578 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(scoped_ptr);
2579};
2580
2581template <typename T>
2582static void swap(scoped_ptr<T>& a, scoped_ptr<T>& b) {
2583 using std::swap;
2584 swap(a.ptr_, b.ptr_);
2585}

2593// A simple C++ wrapper for <regex.h>. It uses the POSIX Extended
2594// Regular Expression syntax.
2595class GTEST_API_ RE {
2596 public:
2597 // A copy constructor is required by the Standard to initialize object
2598 // references from r-values.
2599 RE(const RE& other) { Init(other.pattern()); }
2600
2601 // Constructs an RE from a string.
2602 RE(const ::std::string& regex) { Init(regex.c_str()); } // NOLINT
2603
2604# if GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_STRING
2605
2606 RE(const ::string& regex) { Init(regex.c_str()); } // NOLINT
2607
2608# endif // GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_STRING
2609
2610 RE(const char* regex) { Init(regex); } // NOLINT
2611 ~RE();
2612
2613 // Returns the string representation of the regex.
2614 const char* pattern() const { return pattern_; }
2615
2616 // FullMatch(str, re) returns true iff regular expression re matches
2617 // the entire str.
2618 // PartialMatch(str, re) returns true iff regular expression re
2619 // matches a substring of str (including str itself).
2620 //
2621 // FIXME: make FullMatch() and PartialMatch() work
2622 // when str contains NUL characters.
2623 static bool FullMatch(const ::std::string& str, const RE& re) {
2624 return FullMatch(str.c_str(), re);
2625 }
2626 static bool PartialMatch(const ::std::string& str, const RE& re) {
2627 return PartialMatch(str.c_str(), re);
2628 }
2629
2630# if GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_STRING
2631
2632 static bool FullMatch(const ::string& str, const RE& re) {
2633 return FullMatch(str.c_str(), re);
2634 }
2635 static bool PartialMatch(const ::string& str, const RE& re) {
2636 return PartialMatch(str.c_str(), re);
2637 }
2638
2639# endif // GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_STRING
2640
2641 static bool FullMatch(const char* str, const RE& re);
2642 static bool PartialMatch(const char* str, const RE& re);
2643
2644 private:
2645 void Init(const char* regex);
2646
2647 // We use a const char* instead of an std::string, as Google Test used to be
2648 // used where std::string is not available. FIXME: change to
2649 // std::string.
2650 const char* pattern_;
2651 bool is_valid_;
2652
2653# if GTEST_USES_POSIX_RE
2654
2655 regex_t full_regex_; // For FullMatch().
2656 regex_t partial_regex_; // For PartialMatch().
2657
2658# else // GTEST_USES_SIMPLE_RE
2659
2660 const char* full_pattern_; // For FullMatch();
2661
2662# endif
2663
2664 GTEST_DISALLOW_ASSIGN_(RE);
2665};

2722// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE.
2723//
2724// GTEST_CHECK_ is an all-mode assert. It aborts the program if the condition
2725// is not satisfied.
2726// Synopsis:
2727// GTEST_CHECK_(boolean_condition);
2728// or
2729// GTEST_CHECK_(boolean_condition) << "Additional message";
2730//
2731// This checks the condition and if the condition is not satisfied
2732// it prints message about the condition violation, including the
2733// condition itself, plus additional message streamed into it, if any,
2734// and then it aborts the program. It aborts the program irrespective of
2735// whether it is built in the debug mode or not.
2736# define GTEST_CHECK_(condition) \
2737 GTEST_AMBIGUOUS_ELSE_BLOCKER_ \
2738 if (::testing::internal::IsTrue(condition)) \
2739 ; \
2740 else \
2741 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << "Condition " #condition " failed. "
2742#endif // !defined(GTEST_CHECK_)

2744// An all-mode assert to verify that the given POSIX-style function
2745// call returns 0 (indicating success). Known limitation: this
2746// doesn't expand to a balanced 'if' statement, so enclose the macro
2747// in {} if you need to use it as the only statement in an 'if'
2748// branch.
2749#define GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(posix_call) \
2750 if (const int gtest_error = (posix_call)) \
2751 GTEST_LOG_(FATAL) << #posix_call << "failed with error " \
2752 << gtest_error

2754// Adds reference to a type if it is not a reference type,
2755// otherwise leaves it unchanged. This is the same as
2756// tr1::add_reference, which is not widely available yet.
2757template <typename T>
2758struct AddReference { typedef T& type; }; // NOLINT
2759template <typename T>
2760struct AddReference<T&> { typedef T& type; }; // NOLINT
2761
2762// A handy wrapper around AddReference that works when the argument T
2763// depends on template parameters.
2764#define GTEST_ADD_REFERENCE_(T) \
2765 typename ::testing::internal::AddReference<T>::type
2766
2767// Transforms "T" into "const T&" according to standard reference collapsing
2768// rules (this is only needed as a backport for C++98 compilers that do not
2769// support reference collapsing). Specifically, it transforms:
2770//
2771// char ==> const char&
2772// const char ==> const char&
2773// char& ==> char&
2774// const char& ==> const char&
2775//
2776// Note that the non-const reference will not have "const" added. This is
2777// standard, and necessary so that "T" can always bind to "const T&".
2778template <typename T>
2779struct ConstRef { typedef const T& type; };
2780template <typename T>
2781struct ConstRef<T&> { typedef T& type; };
2782
2783// The argument T must depend on some template parameters.
2784#define GTEST_REFERENCE_TO_CONST_(T) \
2785 typename ::testing::internal::ConstRef<T>::type
2786
2787#if GTEST_HAS_STD_MOVE_
2788using std::forward;
2789using std::move;
2790
2791template <typename T>
2792struct RvalueRef {
2793 typedef T&& type;
2794};
2795#else // GTEST_HAS_STD_MOVE_
2796template <typename T>
2797const T& move(const T& t) {
2798 return t;
2799}
2800template <typename T>
2801GTEST_ADD_REFERENCE_(T) forward(GTEST_ADD_REFERENCE_(T) t) { return t; }
2802
2803template <typename T>
2804struct RvalueRef {
2805 typedef const T& type;
2806};
2807#endif // GTEST_HAS_STD_MOVE_

2809// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN USER CODE.
2810//
2811// Use ImplicitCast_ as a safe version of static_cast for upcasting in
2812// the type hierarchy (e.g. casting a Foo* to a SuperclassOfFoo* or a
2813// const Foo*). When you use ImplicitCast_, the compiler checks that
2814// the cast is safe. Such explicit ImplicitCast_s are necessary in
2815// surprisingly many situations where C++ demands an exact type match
2816// instead of an argument type convertible to a target type.
2817//
2818// The syntax for using ImplicitCast_ is the same as for static_cast:
2819//
2820// ImplicitCast_<ToType>(expr)
2821//
2822// ImplicitCast_ would have been part of the C++ standard library,
2823// but the proposal was submitted too late. It will probably make
2824// its way into the language in the future.
2825//
2826// This relatively ugly name is intentional. It prevents clashes with
2827// similar functions users may have (e.g., implicit_cast). The internal
2828// namespace alone is not enough because the function can be found by ADL.
2829template<typename To>
2830inline To ImplicitCast_(To x) { return x; }
2831
2832// When you upcast (that is, cast a pointer from type Foo to type
2833// SuperclassOfFoo), it's fine to use ImplicitCast_<>, since upcasts
2834// always succeed. When you downcast (that is, cast a pointer from
2835// type Foo to type SubclassOfFoo), static_cast<> isn't safe, because
2836// how do you know the pointer is really of type SubclassOfFoo? It
2837// could be a bare Foo, or of type DifferentSubclassOfFoo. Thus,
2838// when you downcast, you should use this macro. In debug mode, we
2839// use dynamic_cast<> to double-check the downcast is legal (we die
2840// if it's not). In normal mode, we do the efficient static_cast<>
2841// instead. Thus, it's important to test in debug mode to make sure
2842// the cast is legal!
2843// This is the only place in the code we should use dynamic_cast<>.
2844// In particular, you SHOULDN'T be using dynamic_cast<> in order to
2845// do RTTI (eg code like this:
2846// if (dynamic_cast<Subclass1>(foo)) HandleASubclass1Object(foo);
2847// if (dynamic_cast<Subclass2>(foo)) HandleASubclass2Object(foo);
2848// You should design the code some other way not to need this.
2849//
2850// This relatively ugly name is intentional. It prevents clashes with
2851// similar functions users may have (e.g., down_cast). The internal
2852// namespace alone is not enough because the function can be found by ADL.
2853template<typename To, typename From> // use like this: DownCast_<T*>(foo);
2854inline To DownCast_(From* f) { // so we only accept pointers
2855 // Ensures that To is a sub-type of From *. This test is here only
2856 // for compile-time type checking, and has no overhead in an
2857 // optimized build at run-time, as it will be optimized away
2858 // completely.
2859 GTEST_INTENTIONAL_CONST_COND_PUSH_()
2860 if (false) {
2861 GTEST_INTENTIONAL_CONST_COND_POP_()
2862 const To to = NULL;
2863 ::testing::internal::ImplicitCast_<From*>(to);
2864 }
2865
2866#if GTEST_HAS_RTTI
2867 // RTTI: debug mode only!
2868 GTEST_CHECK_(f == NULL || dynamic_cast<To>(f) != NULL);
2869#endif
2870 return static_cast<To>(f);
2871}
2872
2873// Downcasts the pointer of type Base to Derived.
2874// Derived must be a subclass of Base. The parameter MUST
2875// point to a class of type Derived, not any subclass of it.
2876// When RTTI is available, the function performs a runtime
2877// check to enforce this.
2878template <class Derived, class Base>
2879Derived* CheckedDowncastToActualType(Base* base) {
2880#if GTEST_HAS_RTTI
2881 GTEST_CHECK_(typeid(*base) == typeid(Derived));
2882#endif
2883
2884#if defined(GTEST_HAS_DOWNCAST_) && GTEST_HAS_DOWNCAST_
2885 return ::down_cast<Derived*>(base);
2886#elif GTEST_HAS_RTTI
2887 return dynamic_cast<Derived*>(base); // NOLINT
2888#else
2889 return static_cast<Derived*>(base); // Poor man's downcast.
2890#endif
2891}

2932// Sleeps for (roughly) n milliseconds. This function is only for testing
2933// Google Test's own constructs. Don't use it in user tests, either
2934// directly or indirectly.
2935inline void SleepMilliseconds(int n) {
2936 const timespec time = {
2937 0, // 0 seconds.
2938 n * 1000L * 1000L, // And n ms.
2939 };
2940 nanosleep(&time, NULL);
2941}

2949// Allows a controller thread to pause execution of newly created
2950// threads until notified. Instances of this class must be created
2951// and destroyed in the controller thread.
2952//
2953// This class is only for testing Google Test's own constructs. Do not
2954// use it in user tests, either directly or indirectly.
2955class Notification {
2956 public:
2957 Notification() : notified_(false) {
2958 GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(pthread_mutex_init(&mutex_, NULL));
2959 }
2960 ~Notification() {
2961 pthread_mutex_destroy(&mutex_);
2962 }
2963
2964 // Notifies all threads created with this notification to start. Must
2965 // be called from the controller thread.
2966 void Notify() {
2967 pthread_mutex_lock(&mutex_);
2968 notified_ = true;
2969 pthread_mutex_unlock(&mutex_);
2970 }
2971
2972 // Blocks until the controller thread notifies. Must be called from a test
2973 // thread.
2974 void WaitForNotification() {
2975 for (;;) {
2976 pthread_mutex_lock(&mutex_);
2977 const bool notified = notified_;
2978 pthread_mutex_unlock(&mutex_);
2979 if (notified)
2980 break;
2981 SleepMilliseconds(10);
2982 }
2983 }
2984
2985 private:
2986 pthread_mutex_t mutex_;
2987 bool notified_;
2988
2989 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(Notification);
2990};

3048// As a C-function, ThreadFuncWithCLinkage cannot be templated itself.
3049// Consequently, it cannot select a correct instantiation of ThreadWithParam
3050// in order to call its Run(). Introducing ThreadWithParamBase as a
3051// non-templated base class for ThreadWithParam allows us to bypass this
3052// problem.
3053class ThreadWithParamBase {
3054 public:

3059// pthread_create() accepts a pointer to a function type with the C linkage.
3060// According to the Standard (7.5/1), function types with different linkages
3061// are different even if they are otherwise identical. Some compilers (for
3062// example, SunStudio) treat them as different types. Since class methods
3063// cannot be defined with C-linkage we need to define a free C-function to
3064// pass into pthread_create().
3065extern "C" inline void* ThreadFuncWithCLinkage(void* thread) {
3066 static_cast<ThreadWithParamBase*>(thread)->Run();
3067 return NULL;
3068}

3070// Helper class for testing Google Test's multi-threading constructs.
3071// To use it, write:
3072//
3073// void ThreadFunc(int param) { /* Do things with param */ }
3074// Notification thread_can_start;
3075// ...
3076// // The thread_can_start parameter is optional; you can supply NULL.
3077// ThreadWithParam<int> thread(&ThreadFunc, 5, &thread_can_start);
3078// thread_can_start.Notify();
3079//
3080// These classes are only for testing Google Test's own constructs. Do
3081// not use them in user tests, either directly or indirectly.
3082template <typename T>
3083class ThreadWithParam : public ThreadWithParamBase {
3084 public:
3085 typedef void UserThreadFunc(T);
3086
3087 ThreadWithParam(UserThreadFunc* func, T param, Notification* thread_can_start)
3088 : func_(func),
3089 param_(param),
3090 thread_can_start_(thread_can_start),
3091 finished_(false) {
3092 ThreadWithParamBase* const base = this;
3093 // The thread can be created only after all fields except thread_
3094 // have been initialized.
3095 GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(
3096 pthread_create(&thread_, 0, &ThreadFuncWithCLinkage, base));
3097 }
3098 ~ThreadWithParam() { Join(); }
3099
3100 void Join() {
3101 if (!finished_) {
3102 GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(pthread_join(thread_, 0));
3103 finished_ = true;
3104 }
3105 }
3106
3107 virtual void Run() {
3108 if (thread_can_start_ != NULL)
3109 thread_can_start_->WaitForNotification();
3110 func_(param_);
3111 }
3112
3113 private:
3114 UserThreadFunc* const func_; // User-supplied thread function.
3115 const T param_; // User-supplied parameter to the thread function.
3116 // When non-NULL, used to block execution until the controller thread
3117 // notifies.
3118 Notification* const thread_can_start_;
3119 bool finished_; // true iff we know that the thread function has finished.
3120 pthread_t thread_; // The native thread object.
3121
3122 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ThreadWithParam);
3123};

3133// Mutex implements mutex on Windows platforms. It is used in conjunction
3134// with class MutexLock:
3135//
3136// Mutex mutex;
3137// ...
3138// MutexLock lock(&mutex); // Acquires the mutex and releases it at the
3139// // end of the current scope.
3140//
3141// A static Mutex *must* be defined or declared using one of the following
3142// macros:
3143// GTEST_DEFINE_STATIC_MUTEX_(g_some_mutex);
3144// GTEST_DECLARE_STATIC_MUTEX_(g_some_mutex);
3145//
3146// (A non-static Mutex is defined/declared in the usual way).
3147class GTEST_API_ Mutex {
3148 public:
3149 enum MutexType { kStatic = 0, kDynamic = 1 };
3150 // We rely on kStaticMutex being 0 as it is to what the linker initializes
3151 // type_ in static mutexes. critical_section_ will be initialized lazily
3152 // in ThreadSafeLazyInit().
3153 enum StaticConstructorSelector { kStaticMutex = 0 };
3154
3155 // This constructor intentionally does nothing. It relies on type_ being
3156 // statically initialized to 0 (effectively setting it to kStatic) and on
3157 // ThreadSafeLazyInit() to lazily initialize the rest of the members.
3158 explicit Mutex(StaticConstructorSelector /*dummy*/) {}
3159
3160 Mutex();
3161 ~Mutex();
3162
3163 void Lock();
3164
3165 void Unlock();
3166
3167 // Does nothing if the current thread holds the mutex. Otherwise, crashes
3168 // with high probability.
3169 void AssertHeld();
3170
3171 private:
3172 // Initializes owner_thread_id_ and critical_section_ in static mutexes.
3173 void ThreadSafeLazyInit();
3174
3175 // Per https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20040223-00/?p=40503,
3176 // we assume that 0 is an invalid value for thread IDs.
3177 unsigned int owner_thread_id_;
3178
3179 // For static mutexes, we rely on these members being initialized to zeros
3180 // by the linker.
3181 MutexType type_;
3182 long critical_section_init_phase_; // NOLINT
3183 GTEST_CRITICAL_SECTION* critical_section_;
3184
3185 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(Mutex);
3186};

3305// Implements thread-local storage on Windows systems.
3306//
3307// // Thread 1
3308// ThreadLocal<int> tl(100); // 100 is the default value for each thread.
3309//
3310// // Thread 2
3311// tl.set(150); // Changes the value for thread 2 only.
3312// EXPECT_EQ(150, tl.get());
3313//
3314// // Thread 1
3315// EXPECT_EQ(100, tl.get()); // In thread 1, tl has the original value.
3316// tl.set(200);
3317// EXPECT_EQ(200, tl.get());
3318//
3319// The template type argument T must have a public copy constructor.
3320// In addition, the default ThreadLocal constructor requires T to have
3321// a public default constructor.
3322//
3323// The users of a TheadLocal instance have to make sure that all but one
3324// threads (including the main one) using that instance have exited before
3325// destroying it. Otherwise, the per-thread objects managed for them by the
3326// ThreadLocal instance are not guaranteed to be destroyed on all platforms.
3327//
3328// Google Test only uses global ThreadLocal objects. That means they
3329// will die after main() has returned. Therefore, no per-thread
3330// object managed by Google Test will be leaked as long as all threads
3331// using Google Test have exited when main() returns.
3332template <typename T>
3333class ThreadLocal : public ThreadLocalBase {
3334 public:
3335 ThreadLocal() : default_factory_(new DefaultValueHolderFactory()) {}
3336 explicit ThreadLocal(const T& value)
3337 : default_factory_(new InstanceValueHolderFactory(value)) {}
3338
3339 ~ThreadLocal() { ThreadLocalRegistry::OnThreadLocalDestroyed(this); }
3340
3341 T* pointer() { return GetOrCreateValue(); }
3342 const T* pointer() const { return GetOrCreateValue(); }
3343 const T& get() const { return *pointer(); }
3344 void set(const T& value) { *pointer() = value; }
3345
3346 private:
3347 // Holds a value of T. Can be deleted via its base class without the caller
3348 // knowing the type of T.
3349 class ValueHolder : public ThreadLocalValueHolderBase {
3350 public:
3351 ValueHolder() : value_() {}
3352 explicit ValueHolder(const T& value) : value_(value) {}
3353
3354 T* pointer() { return &value_; }
3355
3356 private:
3357 T value_;
3358 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ValueHolder);
3359 };
3360
3361
3362 T* GetOrCreateValue() const {
3363 return static_cast<ValueHolder*>(
3364 ThreadLocalRegistry::GetValueOnCurrentThread(this))->pointer();
3365 }
3366
3367 virtual ThreadLocalValueHolderBase* NewValueForCurrentThread() const {
3368 return default_factory_->MakeNewHolder();
3369 }
3370
3371 class ValueHolderFactory {
3372 public:
3373 ValueHolderFactory() {}
3374 virtual ~ValueHolderFactory() {}
3375 virtual ValueHolder* MakeNewHolder() const = 0;
3376
3377 private:
3378 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ValueHolderFactory);
3379 };
3380
3381 class DefaultValueHolderFactory : public ValueHolderFactory {
3382 public:
3383 DefaultValueHolderFactory() {}
3384 virtual ValueHolder* MakeNewHolder() const { return new ValueHolder(); }
3385
3386 private:
3387 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(DefaultValueHolderFactory);
3388 };
3389
3390 class InstanceValueHolderFactory : public ValueHolderFactory {
3391 public:
3392 explicit InstanceValueHolderFactory(const T& value) : value_(value) {}
3393 virtual ValueHolder* MakeNewHolder() const {
3394 return new ValueHolder(value_);
3395 }
3396
3397 private:
3398 const T value_; // The value for each thread.
3399
3400 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(InstanceValueHolderFactory);
3401 };
3402
3403 scoped_ptr<ValueHolderFactory> default_factory_;
3404
3405 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ThreadLocal);
3406};

3410// MutexBase and Mutex implement mutex on pthreads-based platforms.
3411class MutexBase {
3412 public:
3413 // Acquires this mutex.
3414 void Lock() {
3415 GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(pthread_mutex_lock(&mutex_));
3416 owner_ = pthread_self();
3417 has_owner_ = true;
3418 }
3419
3420 // Releases this mutex.
3421 void Unlock() {
3422 // Since the lock is being released the owner_ field should no longer be
3423 // considered valid. We don't protect writing to has_owner_ here, as it's
3424 // the caller's responsibility to ensure that the current thread holds the
3425 // mutex when this is called.
3426 has_owner_ = false;
3427 GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(pthread_mutex_unlock(&mutex_));
3428 }
3429
3430 // Does nothing if the current thread holds the mutex. Otherwise, crashes
3431 // with high probability.
3432 void AssertHeld() const {
3433 GTEST_CHECK_(has_owner_ && pthread_equal(owner_, pthread_self()))
3434 << "The current thread is not holding the mutex @" << this;
3435 }
3436
3437 // A static mutex may be used before main() is entered. It may even
3438 // be used before the dynamic initialization stage. Therefore we
3439 // must be able to initialize a static mutex object at link time.
3440 // This means MutexBase has to be a POD and its member variables
3441 // have to be public.
3442 public:
3443 pthread_mutex_t mutex_; // The underlying pthread mutex.
3444 // has_owner_ indicates whether the owner_ field below contains a valid thread
3445 // ID and is therefore safe to inspect (e.g., to use in pthread_equal()). All
3446 // accesses to the owner_ field should be protected by a check of this field.
3447 // An alternative might be to memset() owner_ to all zeros, but there's no
3448 // guarantee that a zero'd pthread_t is necessarily invalid or even different
3449 // from pthread_self().
3450 bool has_owner_;
3451 pthread_t owner_; // The thread holding the mutex.
3452};
3453
3454// Forward-declares a static mutex.
3455# define GTEST_DECLARE_STATIC_MUTEX_(mutex) \
3456 extern ::testing::internal::MutexBase mutex
3457
3458// Defines and statically (i.e. at link time) initializes a static mutex.
3459// The initialization list here does not explicitly initialize each field,
3460// instead relying on default initialization for the unspecified fields. In
3461// particular, the owner_ field (a pthread_t) is not explicitly initialized.
3462// This allows initialization to work whether pthread_t is a scalar or struct.
3463// The flag -Wmissing-field-initializers must not be specified for this to work.
3464#define GTEST_DEFINE_STATIC_MUTEX_(mutex) \
3465 ::testing::internal::MutexBase mutex = {PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER, false, 0}
3466
3467// The Mutex class can only be used for mutexes created at runtime. It
3468// shares its API with MutexBase otherwise.
3469class Mutex : public MutexBase {
3470 public:
3471 Mutex() {
3472 GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(pthread_mutex_init(&mutex_, NULL));
3473 has_owner_ = false;
3474 }
3475 ~Mutex() {
3476 GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(pthread_mutex_destroy(&mutex_));
3477 }
3478
3479 private:
3480 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(Mutex);
3481};
3482
3483// We cannot name this class MutexLock because the ctor declaration would
3484// conflict with a macro named MutexLock, which is defined on some
3485// platforms. That macro is used as a defensive measure to prevent against
3486// inadvertent misuses of MutexLock like "MutexLock(&mu)" rather than
3487// "MutexLock l(&mu)". Hence the typedef trick below.
3488class GTestMutexLock {
3489 public:
3490 explicit GTestMutexLock(MutexBase* mutex)
3491 : mutex_(mutex) { mutex_->Lock(); }
3492
3493 ~GTestMutexLock() { mutex_->Unlock(); }
3494
3495 private:
3496 MutexBase* const mutex_;
3497
3498 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(GTestMutexLock);
3499};

3514// Called by pthread to delete thread-local data stored by
3515// pthread_setspecific().
3516extern "C" inline void DeleteThreadLocalValue(void* value_holder) {
3517 delete static_cast<ThreadLocalValueHolderBase*>(value_holder);
3518}
3519
3520// Implements thread-local storage on pthreads-based systems.
3521template <typename T>
3522class GTEST_API_ ThreadLocal {
3523 public:
3524 ThreadLocal()
3525 : key_(CreateKey()), default_factory_(new DefaultValueHolderFactory()) {}
3526 explicit ThreadLocal(const T& value)
3527 : key_(CreateKey()),
3528 default_factory_(new InstanceValueHolderFactory(value)) {}
3529
3530 ~ThreadLocal() {
3531 // Destroys the managed object for the current thread, if any.
3532 DeleteThreadLocalValue(pthread_getspecific(key_));
3533
3534 // Releases resources associated with the key. This will *not*
3535 // delete managed objects for other threads.
3536 GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(pthread_key_delete(key_));
3537 }
3538
3539 T* pointer() { return GetOrCreateValue(); }
3540 const T* pointer() const { return GetOrCreateValue(); }
3541 const T& get() const { return *pointer(); }
3542 void set(const T& value) { *pointer() = value; }
3543
3544 private:
3545 // Holds a value of type T.
3546 class ValueHolder : public ThreadLocalValueHolderBase {
3547 public:
3548 ValueHolder() : value_() {}
3549 explicit ValueHolder(const T& value) : value_(value) {}
3550
3551 T* pointer() { return &value_; }
3552
3553 private:
3554 T value_;
3555 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ValueHolder);
3556 };
3557
3558 static pthread_key_t CreateKey() {
3559 pthread_key_t key;
3560 // When a thread exits, DeleteThreadLocalValue() will be called on
3561 // the object managed for that thread.
3562 GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(
3563 pthread_key_create(&key, &DeleteThreadLocalValue));
3564 return key;
3565 }
3566
3567 T* GetOrCreateValue() const {
3568 ThreadLocalValueHolderBase* const holder =
3569 static_cast<ThreadLocalValueHolderBase*>(pthread_getspecific(key_));
3570 if (holder != NULL) {
3571 return CheckedDowncastToActualType<ValueHolder>(holder)->pointer();
3572 }
3573
3574 ValueHolder* const new_holder = default_factory_->MakeNewHolder();
3575 ThreadLocalValueHolderBase* const holder_base = new_holder;
3576 GTEST_CHECK_POSIX_SUCCESS_(pthread_setspecific(key_, holder_base));
3577 return new_holder->pointer();
3578 }
3579
3580 class ValueHolderFactory {
3581 public:
3582 ValueHolderFactory() {}
3583 virtual ~ValueHolderFactory() {}
3584 virtual ValueHolder* MakeNewHolder() const = 0;
3585
3586 private:
3587 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ValueHolderFactory);
3588 };
3589
3590 class DefaultValueHolderFactory : public ValueHolderFactory {
3591 public:
3592 DefaultValueHolderFactory() {}
3593 virtual ValueHolder* MakeNewHolder() const { return new ValueHolder(); }
3594
3595 private:
3596 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(DefaultValueHolderFactory);
3597 };
3598
3599 class InstanceValueHolderFactory : public ValueHolderFactory {
3600 public:
3601 explicit InstanceValueHolderFactory(const T& value) : value_(value) {}
3602 virtual ValueHolder* MakeNewHolder() const {
3603 return new ValueHolder(value_);
3604 }
3605
3606 private:
3607 const T value_; // The value for each thread.
3608
3609 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(InstanceValueHolderFactory);
3610 };
3611
3612 // A key pthreads uses for looking up per-thread values.
3613 const pthread_key_t key_;
3614 scoped_ptr<ValueHolderFactory> default_factory_;
3615
3616 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ThreadLocal);
3617};
3618

3672// Passing non-POD classes through ellipsis (...) crashes the ARM
3673// compiler and generates a warning in Sun Studio before 12u4. The Nokia Symbian
3674// and the IBM XL C/C++ compiler try to instantiate a copy constructor
3675// for objects passed through ellipsis (...), failing for uncopyable
3676// objects. We define this to ensure that only POD is passed through
3677// ellipsis on these systems.
3678#if defined(__SYMBIAN32__) || defined(__IBMCPP__) || \
3679 (defined(__SUNPRO_CC) && __SUNPRO_CC < 0x5130)
3680// We lose support for NULL detection where the compiler doesn't like
3681// passing non-POD classes through ellipsis (...).
3682# define GTEST_ELLIPSIS_NEEDS_POD_ 1
3683#else
3684# define GTEST_CAN_COMPARE_NULL 1
3685#endif
3686
3687// The Nokia Symbian and IBM XL C/C++ compilers cannot decide between
3688// const T& and const T* in a function template. These compilers
3689// _can_ decide between class template specializations for T and T*,
3690// so a tr1::type_traits-like is_pointer works.
3691#if defined(__SYMBIAN32__) || defined(__IBMCPP__)
3692# define GTEST_NEEDS_IS_POINTER_ 1
3693#endif

3745// Utilities for char.
3746
3747// isspace(int ch) and friends accept an unsigned char or EOF. char
3748// may be signed, depending on the compiler (or compiler flags).
3749// Therefore we need to cast a char to unsigned char before calling
3750// isspace(), etc.
3751
3752inline bool IsAlpha(char ch) {
3753 return isalpha(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)) != 0;
3754}
3755inline bool IsAlNum(char ch) {
3756 return isalnum(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)) != 0;
3757}
3758inline bool IsDigit(char ch) {
3759 return isdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)) != 0;
3760}
3761inline bool IsLower(char ch) {
3762 return islower(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)) != 0;
3763}
3764inline bool IsSpace(char ch) {
3765 return isspace(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)) != 0;
3766}
3767inline bool IsUpper(char ch) {
3768 return isupper(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)) != 0;
3769}
3770inline bool IsXDigit(char ch) {
3771 return isxdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)) != 0;
3772}
3773inline bool IsXDigit(wchar_t ch) {
3774 const unsigned char low_byte = static_cast<unsigned char>(ch);
3775 return ch == low_byte && isxdigit(low_byte) != 0;
3776}
3777
3778inline char ToLower(char ch) {
3779 return static_cast<char>(tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)));
3780}
3781inline char ToUpper(char ch) {
3782 return static_cast<char>(toupper(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)));
3783}
3784
3785inline std::string StripTrailingSpaces(std::string str) {
3786 std::string::iterator it = str.end();
3787 while (it != str.begin() && IsSpace(*--it))
3788 it = str.erase(it);
3789 return str;
3790}

3888inline const char* GetEnv(const char* name) {
3889#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE || GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_PHONE || GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_RT
3890 // We are on Windows CE, which has no environment variables.
3891 static_cast<void>(name); // To prevent 'unused argument' warning.
3892 return NULL;
3893#elif defined(__BORLANDC__) || defined(__SunOS_5_8) || defined(__SunOS_5_9)
3894 // Environment variables which we programmatically clear will be set to the
3895 // empty string rather than unset (NULL). Handle that case.
3896 const char* const env = getenv(name);
3897 return (env != NULL && env[0] != '\0') ? env : NULL;
3898#else
3899 return getenv(name);
3900#endif

3916// MSVC "deprecates" snprintf and issues warnings wherever it is used. In
3917// order to avoid these warnings, we need to use _snprintf or _snprintf_s on
3918// MSVC-based platforms. We map the GTEST_SNPRINTF_ macro to the appropriate
3919// function in order to achieve that. We use macro definition here because
3920// snprintf is a variadic function.
3921#if defined(_MSC_VER) && _MSC_VER >= 1400 && !GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
3922// MSVC 2005 and above support variadic macros.
3923# define GTEST_SNPRINTF_(buffer, size, format, ...) \
3924 _snprintf_s(buffer, size, size, format, __VA_ARGS__)
3925#elif defined(_MSC_VER)
3926// Windows CE does not define _snprintf_s and MSVC prior to 2005 doesn't
3927// complain about _snprintf.
3928# define GTEST_SNPRINTF_ _snprintf
3929#else
3930# define GTEST_SNPRINTF_ snprintf
3931#endif

3933// The maximum number a BiggestInt can represent. This definition
3934// works no matter BiggestInt is represented in one's complement or
3935// two's complement.
3936//
3937// We cannot rely on numeric_limits in STL, as __int64 and long long
3938// are not part of standard C++ and numeric_limits doesn't need to be
3939// defined for them.
3940const BiggestInt kMaxBiggestInt =
3941 ~(static_cast<BiggestInt>(1) << (8*sizeof(BiggestInt) - 1));

3943// This template class serves as a compile-time function from size to
3944// type. It maps a size in bytes to a primitive type with that
3945// size. e.g.
3946//
3947// TypeWithSize<4>::UInt
3948//
3949// is typedef-ed to be unsigned int (unsigned integer made up of 4
3950// bytes).
3951//
3952// Such functionality should belong to STL, but I cannot find it
3953// there.
3954//
3955// Google Test uses this class in the implementation of floating-point
3956// comparison.
3957//
3958// For now it only handles UInt (unsigned int) as that's all Google Test
3959// needs. Other types can be easily added in the future if need
3960// arises.
3961template <size_t size>
3962class TypeWithSize {
3963 public:
3964 // This prevents the user from using TypeWithSize<N> with incorrect
3965 // values of N.
3966 typedef void UInt;
3967};
3968
3969// The specialization for size 4.
3970template <>
3971class TypeWithSize<4> {
3972 public:
3973 // unsigned int has size 4 in both gcc and MSVC.
3974 //
3975 // As base/basictypes.h doesn't compile on Windows, we cannot use
3976 // uint32, uint64, and etc here.
3977 typedef int Int;
3978 typedef unsigned int UInt;
3979};
3980
3981// The specialization for size 8.
3982template <>
3983class TypeWithSize<8> {
3984 public:
3985#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
3986 typedef __int64 Int;
3987 typedef unsigned __int64 UInt;
3988#else
3989 typedef long long Int; // NOLINT
3990 typedef unsigned long long UInt; // NOLINT
3991#endif // GTEST_OS_WINDOWS
3992};
3993
3994// Integer types of known sizes.
3995typedef TypeWithSize<4>::Int Int32;
3996typedef TypeWithSize<4>::UInt UInt32;
3997typedef TypeWithSize<8>::Int Int64;
3998typedef TypeWithSize<8>::UInt UInt64;
3999typedef TypeWithSize<8>::Int TimeInMillis; // Represents time in milliseconds.

4140// The Message class works like an ostream repeater.
4141//
4142// Typical usage:
4143//
4144// 1. You stream a bunch of values to a Message object.
4145// It will remember the text in a stringstream.
4146// 2. Then you stream the Message object to an ostream.
4147// This causes the text in the Message to be streamed
4148// to the ostream.
4149//
4150// For example;
4151//
4152// testing::Message foo;
4153// foo << 1 << " != " << 2;
4154// std::cout << foo;
4155//
4156// will print "1 != 2".
4157//
4158// Message is not intended to be inherited from. In particular, its
4159// destructor is not virtual.
4160//
4161// Note that stringstream behaves differently in gcc and in MSVC. You
4162// can stream a NULL char pointer to it in the former, but not in the
4163// latter (it causes an access violation if you do). The Message
4164// class hides this difference by treating a NULL char pointer as
4165// "(null)".
4166class GTEST_API_ Message {
4167 private:
4168 // The type of basic IO manipulators (endl, ends, and flush) for
4169 // narrow streams.
4170 typedef std::ostream& (*BasicNarrowIoManip)(std::ostream&);
4171
4172 public:
4173 // Constructs an empty Message.
4174 Message();
4175
4176 // Copy constructor.
4177 Message(const Message& msg) : ss_(new ::std::stringstream) { // NOLINT
4178 *ss_ << msg.GetString();
4179 }
4180
4181 // Constructs a Message from a C-string.
4182 explicit Message(const char* str) : ss_(new ::std::stringstream) {
4183 *ss_ << str;
4184 }
4185
4186#if GTEST_OS_SYMBIAN
4187 // Streams a value (either a pointer or not) to this object.
4188 template <typename T>
4189 inline Message& operator <<(const T& value) {
4190 StreamHelper(typename internal::is_pointer<T>::type(), value);
4191 return *this;
4192 }
4193#else
4194 // Streams a non-pointer value to this object.
4195 template <typename T>
4196 inline Message& operator <<(const T& val) {
4197 // Some libraries overload << for STL containers. These
4198 // overloads are defined in the global namespace instead of ::std.
4199 //
4200 // C++'s symbol lookup rule (i.e. Koenig lookup) says that these
4201 // overloads are visible in either the std namespace or the global
4202 // namespace, but not other namespaces, including the testing
4203 // namespace which Google Test's Message class is in.
4204 //
4205 // To allow STL containers (and other types that has a << operator
4206 // defined in the global namespace) to be used in Google Test
4207 // assertions, testing::Message must access the custom << operator
4208 // from the global namespace. With this using declaration,
4209 // overloads of << defined in the global namespace and those
4210 // visible via Koenig lookup are both exposed in this function.
4211 using ::operator <<;
4212 *ss_ << val;
4213 return *this;
4214 }
4215
4216 // Streams a pointer value to this object.
4217 //
4218 // This function is an overload of the previous one. When you
4219 // stream a pointer to a Message, this definition will be used as it
4220 // is more specialized. (The C++ Standard, section
4221 // [temp.func.order].) If you stream a non-pointer, then the
4222 // previous definition will be used.
4223 //
4224 // The reason for this overload is that streaming a NULL pointer to
4225 // ostream is undefined behavior. Depending on the compiler, you
4226 // may get "0", "(nil)", "(null)", or an access violation. To
4227 // ensure consistent result across compilers, we always treat NULL
4228 // as "(null)".
4229 template <typename T>
4230 inline Message& operator <<(T* const& pointer) { // NOLINT
4231 if (pointer == NULL) {
4232 *ss_ << "(null)";
4233 } else {
4234 *ss_ << pointer;
4235 }
4236 return *this;
4237 }
4238#endif // GTEST_OS_SYMBIAN
4239
4240 // Since the basic IO manipulators are overloaded for both narrow
4241 // and wide streams, we have to provide this specialized definition
4242 // of operator <<, even though its body is the same as the
4243 // templatized version above. Without this definition, streaming
4244 // endl or other basic IO manipulators to Message will confuse the
4245 // compiler.
4246 Message& operator <<(BasicNarrowIoManip val) {
4247 *ss_ << val;
4248 return *this;
4249 }
4250
4251 // Instead of 1/0, we want to see true/false for bool values.
4252 Message& operator <<(bool b) {
4253 return *this << (b ? "true" : "false");
4254 }
4255
4256 // These two overloads allow streaming a wide C string to a Message
4257 // using the UTF-8 encoding.
4258 Message& operator <<(const wchar_t* wide_c_str);
4259 Message& operator <<(wchar_t* wide_c_str);
4260
4261#if GTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING
4262 // Converts the given wide string to a narrow string using the UTF-8
4263 // encoding, and streams the result to this Message object.
4264 Message& operator <<(const ::std::wstring& wstr);
4265#endif // GTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING
4266
4267#if GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_WSTRING
4268 // Converts the given wide string to a narrow string using the UTF-8
4269 // encoding, and streams the result to this Message object.
4270 Message& operator <<(const ::wstring& wstr);
4271#endif // GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_WSTRING
4272
4273 // Gets the text streamed to this object so far as an std::string.
4274 // Each '\0' character in the buffer is replaced with "\\0".
4275 //
4276 // INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN A USER PROGRAM.
4277 std::string GetString() const;
4278
4279 private:
4280#if GTEST_OS_SYMBIAN
4281 // These are needed as the Nokia Symbian Compiler cannot decide between
4282 // const T& and const T* in a function template. The Nokia compiler _can_
4283 // decide between class template specializations for T and T*, so a
4284 // tr1::type_traits-like is_pointer works, and we can overload on that.
4285 template <typename T>
4286 inline void StreamHelper(internal::true_type /*is_pointer*/, T* pointer) {
4287 if (pointer == NULL) {
4288 *ss_ << "(null)";
4289 } else {
4290 *ss_ << pointer;
4291 }
4292 }
4293 template <typename T>
4294 inline void StreamHelper(internal::false_type /*is_pointer*/,
4295 const T& value) {
4296 // See the comments in Message& operator <<(const T&) above for why
4297 // we need this using statement.
4298 using ::operator <<;
4299 *ss_ << value;
4300 }
4301#endif // GTEST_OS_SYMBIAN
4302
4303 // We'll hold the text streamed to this object here.
4304 const internal::scoped_ptr< ::std::stringstream> ss_;
4305
4306 // We declare (but don't implement) this to prevent the compiler
4307 // from implementing the assignment operator.
4308 void operator=(const Message&);
4309};
4310
4311// Streams a Message to an ostream.
4312inline std::ostream& operator <<(std::ostream& os, const Message& sb) {
4313 return os << sb.GetString();
4314}
4315
4316namespace internal {
4317
4318// Converts a streamable value to an std::string. A NULL pointer is
4319// converted to "(null)". When the input value is a ::string,
4320// ::std::string, ::wstring, or ::std::wstring object, each NUL
4321// character in it is replaced with "\\0".
4322template <typename T>
4323std::string StreamableToString(const T& streamable) {
4324 return (Message() << streamable).GetString();
4325}
4326
4327} // namespace internal
4328} // namespace testing

4427namespace testing {

4430// String - an abstract class holding static string utilities.
4431class GTEST_API_ String {
4432 public:
4433 // Static utility methods
4434
4435 // Clones a 0-terminated C string, allocating memory using new. The
4436 // caller is responsible for deleting the return value using
4437 // delete[]. Returns the cloned string, or NULL if the input is
4438 // NULL.
4439 //
4440 // This is different from strdup() in string.h, which allocates
4441 // memory using malloc().
4442 static const char* CloneCString(const char* c_str);
4443
4444#if GTEST_OS_WINDOWS_MOBILE
4445 // Windows CE does not have the 'ANSI' versions of Win32 APIs. To be
4446 // able to pass strings to Win32 APIs on CE we need to convert them
4447 // to 'Unicode', UTF-16.
4448
4449 // Creates a UTF-16 wide string from the given ANSI string, allocating
4450 // memory using new. The caller is responsible for deleting the return
4451 // value using delete[]. Returns the wide string, or NULL if the
4452 // input is NULL.
4453 //
4454 // The wide string is created using the ANSI codepage (CP_ACP) to
4455 // match the behaviour of the ANSI versions of Win32 calls and the
4456 // C runtime.
4457 static LPCWSTR AnsiToUtf16(const char* c_str);
4458
4459 // Creates an ANSI string from the given wide string, allocating
4460 // memory using new. The caller is responsible for deleting the return
4461 // value using delete[]. Returns the ANSI string, or NULL if the
4462 // input is NULL.
4463 //
4464 // The returned string is created using the ANSI codepage (CP_ACP) to
4465 // match the behaviour of the ANSI versions of Win32 calls and the
4466 // C runtime.
4467 static const char* Utf16ToAnsi(LPCWSTR utf16_str);
4468#endif
4469
4470 // Compares two C strings. Returns true iff they have the same content.
4471 //
4472 // Unlike strcmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s). A
4473 // NULL C string is considered different to any non-NULL C string,
4474 // including the empty string.
4475 static bool CStringEquals(const char* lhs, const char* rhs);
4476
4477 // Converts a wide C string to a String using the UTF-8 encoding.
4478 // NULL will be converted to "(null)". If an error occurred during
4479 // the conversion, "(failed to convert from wide string)" is
4480 // returned.
4481 static std::string ShowWideCString(const wchar_t* wide_c_str);
4482
4483 // Compares two wide C strings. Returns true iff they have the same
4484 // content.
4485 //
4486 // Unlike wcscmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s). A
4487 // NULL C string is considered different to any non-NULL C string,
4488 // including the empty string.
4489 static bool WideCStringEquals(const wchar_t* lhs, const wchar_t* rhs);
4490
4491 // Compares two C strings, ignoring case. Returns true iff they
4492 // have the same content.
4493 //
4494 // Unlike strcasecmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s).
4495 // A NULL C string is considered different to any non-NULL C string,
4496 // including the empty string.
4497 static bool CaseInsensitiveCStringEquals(const char* lhs,
4498 const char* rhs);
4499
4500 // Compares two wide C strings, ignoring case. Returns true iff they
4501 // have the same content.
4502 //
4503 // Unlike wcscasecmp(), this function can handle NULL argument(s).
4504 // A NULL C string is considered different to any non-NULL wide C string,
4505 // including the empty string.
4506 // NB: The implementations on different platforms slightly differ.
4507 // On windows, this method uses _wcsicmp which compares according to LC_CTYPE
4508 // environment variable. On GNU platform this method uses wcscasecmp
4509 // which compares according to LC_CTYPE category of the current locale.
4510 // On MacOS X, it uses towlower, which also uses LC_CTYPE category of the
4511 // current locale.
4512 static bool CaseInsensitiveWideCStringEquals(const wchar_t* lhs,
4513 const wchar_t* rhs);
4514
4515 // Returns true iff the given string ends with the given suffix, ignoring
4516 // case. Any string is considered to end with an empty suffix.
4517 static bool EndsWithCaseInsensitive(
4518 const std::string& str, const std::string& suffix);
4519
4520 // Formats an int value as "%02d".
4521 static std::string FormatIntWidth2(int value); // "%02d" for width == 2
4522
4523 // Formats an int value as "%X".
4524 static std::string FormatHexInt(int value);
4525
4526 // Formats a byte as "%02X".
4527 static std::string FormatByte(unsigned char value);
4528
4529 private:
4530 String(); // Not meant to be instantiated.
4531}; // class String
4532
4533// Gets the content of the stringstream's buffer as an std::string. Each '\0'
4534// character in the buffer is replaced with "\\0".
4535GTEST_API_ std::string StringStreamToString(::std::stringstream* stream);
4536
4537} // namespace internal
4538} // namespace testing

4548// FilePath - a class for file and directory pathname manipulation which
4549// handles platform-specific conventions (like the pathname separator).
4550// Used for helper functions for naming files in a directory for xml output.
4551// Except for Set methods, all methods are const or static, which provides an
4552// "immutable value object" -- useful for peace of mind.
4553// A FilePath with a value ending in a path separator ("like/this/") represents
4554// a directory, otherwise it is assumed to represent a file. In either case,
4555// it may or may not represent an actual file or directory in the file system.
4556// Names are NOT checked for syntax correctness -- no checking for illegal
4557// characters, malformed paths, etc.
4558
4559class GTEST_API_ FilePath {
4560 public:
4561 FilePath() : pathname_("") { }
4562 FilePath(const FilePath& rhs) : pathname_(rhs.pathname_) { }
4563
4564 explicit FilePath(const std::string& pathname) : pathname_(pathname) {
4565 Normalize();
4566 }
4567
4568 FilePath& operator=(const FilePath& rhs) {
4569 Set(rhs);
4570 return *this;
4571 }
4572
4573 void Set(const FilePath& rhs) {
4574 pathname_ = rhs.pathname_;
4575 }
4576
4577 const std::string& string() const { return pathname_; }
4578 const char* c_str() const { return pathname_.c_str(); }
4579
4580 // Returns the current working directory, or "" if unsuccessful.
4581 static FilePath GetCurrentDir();
4582
4583 // Given directory = "dir", base_name = "test", number = 0,
4584 // extension = "xml", returns "dir/test.xml". If number is greater
4585 // than zero (e.g., 12), returns "dir/test_12.xml".
4586 // On Windows platform, uses \ as the separator rather than /.
4587 static FilePath MakeFileName(const FilePath& directory,
4588 const FilePath& base_name,
4589 int number,
4590 const char* extension);
4591
4592 // Given directory = "dir", relative_path = "test.xml",
4593 // returns "dir/test.xml".
4594 // On Windows, uses \ as the separator rather than /.
4595 static FilePath ConcatPaths(const FilePath& directory,
4596 const FilePath& relative_path);
4597
4598 // Returns a pathname for a file that does not currently exist. The pathname
4599 // will be directory/base_name.extension or
4600 // directory/base_name_<number>.extension if directory/base_name.extension
4601 // already exists. The number will be incremented until a pathname is found
4602 // that does not already exist.
4603 // Examples: 'dir/foo_test.xml' or 'dir/foo_test_1.xml'.
4604 // There could be a race condition if two or more processes are calling this
4605 // function at the same time -- they could both pick the same filename.
4606 static FilePath GenerateUniqueFileName(const FilePath& directory,
4607 const FilePath& base_name,
4608 const char* extension);
4609
4610 // Returns true iff the path is "".
4611 bool IsEmpty() const { return pathname_.empty(); }
4612
4613 // If input name has a trailing separator character, removes it and returns
4614 // the name, otherwise return the name string unmodified.
4615 // On Windows platform, uses \ as the separator, other platforms use /.
4616 FilePath RemoveTrailingPathSeparator() const;
4617
4618 // Returns a copy of the FilePath with the directory part removed.
4619 // Example: FilePath("path/to/file").RemoveDirectoryName() returns
4620 // FilePath("file"). If there is no directory part ("just_a_file"), it returns
4621 // the FilePath unmodified. If there is no file part ("just_a_dir/") it
4622 // returns an empty FilePath ("").
4623 // On Windows platform, '\' is the path separator, otherwise it is '/'.
4624 FilePath RemoveDirectoryName() const;
4625
4626 // RemoveFileName returns the directory path with the filename removed.
4627 // Example: FilePath("path/to/file").RemoveFileName() returns "path/to/".
4628 // If the FilePath is "a_file" or "/a_file", RemoveFileName returns
4629 // FilePath("./") or, on Windows, FilePath(".\\"). If the filepath does
4630 // not have a file, like "just/a/dir/", it returns the FilePath unmodified.
4631 // On Windows platform, '\' is the path separator, otherwise it is '/'.
4632 FilePath RemoveFileName() const;
4633
4634 // Returns a copy of the FilePath with the case-insensitive extension removed.
4635 // Example: FilePath("dir/file.exe").RemoveExtension("EXE") returns
4636 // FilePath("dir/file"). If a case-insensitive extension is not
4637 // found, returns a copy of the original FilePath.
4638 FilePath RemoveExtension(const char* extension) const;
4639
4640 // Creates directories so that path exists. Returns true if successful or if
4641 // the directories already exist; returns false if unable to create
4642 // directories for any reason. Will also return false if the FilePath does
4643 // not represent a directory (that is, it doesn't end with a path separator).
4644 bool CreateDirectoriesRecursively() const;
4645
4646 // Create the directory so that path exists. Returns true if successful or
4647 // if the directory already exists; returns false if unable to create the
4648 // directory for any reason, including if the parent directory does not
4649 // exist. Not named "CreateDirectory" because that's a macro on Windows.
4650 bool CreateFolder() const;
4651
4652 // Returns true if FilePath describes something in the file-system,
4653 // either a file, directory, or whatever, and that something exists.
4654 bool FileOrDirectoryExists() const;
4655
4656 // Returns true if pathname describes a directory in the file-system
4657 // that exists.
4658 bool DirectoryExists() const;
4659
4660 // Returns true if FilePath ends with a path separator, which indicates that
4661 // it is intended to represent a directory. Returns false otherwise.
4662 // This does NOT check that a directory (or file) actually exists.
4663 bool IsDirectory() const;
4664
4665 // Returns true if pathname describes a root directory. (Windows has one
4666 // root directory per disk drive.)
4667 bool IsRootDirectory() const;
4668
4669 // Returns true if pathname describes an absolute path.
4670 bool IsAbsolutePath() const;
4671
4672 private:
4673 // Replaces multiple consecutive separators with a single separator.
4674 // For example, "bar///foo" becomes "bar/foo". Does not eliminate other
4675 // redundancies that might be in a pathname involving "." or "..".
4676 //
4677 // A pathname with multiple consecutive separators may occur either through
4678 // user error or as a result of some scripts or APIs that generate a pathname
4679 // with a trailing separator. On other platforms the same API or script
4680 // may NOT generate a pathname with a trailing "/". Then elsewhere that
4681 // pathname may have another "/" and pathname components added to it,
4682 // without checking for the separator already being there.
4683 // The script language and operating system may allow paths like "foo//bar"
4684 // but some of the functions in FilePath will not handle that correctly. In
4685 // particular, RemoveTrailingPathSeparator() only removes one separator, and
4686 // it is called in CreateDirectoriesRecursively() assuming that it will change
4687 // a pathname from directory syntax (trailing separator) to filename syntax.
4688 //
4689 // On Windows this method also replaces the alternate path separator '/' with
4690 // the primary path separator '\\', so that for example "bar\\/\\foo" becomes
4691 // "bar\\foo".
4692
4693 void Normalize();
4694
4695 // Returns a pointer to the last occurrence of a valid path separator in
4696 // the FilePath. On Windows, for example, both '/' and '\' are valid path
4697 // separators. Returns NULL if no path separator was found.
4698 const char* FindLastPathSeparator() const;
4699
4700 std::string pathname_;
4701}; // class FilePath
4702
4703} // namespace internal
4704} // namespace testing

4768// Canonicalizes a given name with respect to the Standard C++ Library.
4769// This handles removing the inline namespace within `std` that is
4770// used by various standard libraries (e.g., `std::__1`). Names outside
4771// of namespace std are returned unmodified.
4772inline std::string CanonicalizeForStdLibVersioning(std::string s) {
4773 static const char prefix[] = "std::__";
4774 if (s.compare(0, strlen(prefix), prefix) == 0) {
4775 std::string::size_type end = s.find("::", strlen(prefix));
4776 if (end != s.npos) {
4777 // Erase everything between the initial `std` and the second `::`.
4778 s.erase(strlen("std"), end - strlen("std"));
4779 }
4780 }
4781 return s;
4782}

4784// GetTypeName<T>() returns a human-readable name of type T.
4785// NB: This function is also used in Google Mock, so don't move it inside of
4786// the typed-test-only section below.
4787template <typename T>
4788std::string GetTypeName() {
4789# if GTEST_HAS_RTTI
4790
4791 const char* const name = typeid(T).name();
4792# if GTEST_HAS_CXXABI_H_ || defined(__HP_aCC)
4793 int status = 0;
4794 // gcc's implementation of typeid(T).name() mangles the type name,
4795 // so we have to demangle it.
4796# if GTEST_HAS_CXXABI_H_
4797 using abi::__cxa_demangle;
4798# endif // GTEST_HAS_CXXABI_H_
4799 char* const readable_name = __cxa_demangle(name, 0, 0, &status);
4800 const std::string name_str(status == 0 ? readable_name : name);
4801 free(readable_name);
4802 return CanonicalizeForStdLibVersioning(name_str);
4803# else
4804 return name;
4805# endif // GTEST_HAS_CXXABI_H_ || __HP_aCC
4806
4807# else
4808
4809 return "<type>";
4810
4811# endif // GTEST_HAS_RTTI
4812}

4834// The following family of struct and struct templates are used to
4835// represent type lists. In particular, TypesN<T1, T2, ..., TN>
4836// represents a type list with N types (T1, T2, ..., and TN) in it.
4837// Except for Types0, every struct in the family has two member types:
4838// Head for the first type in the list, and Tail for the rest of the
4839// list.
4840
4841// The empty type list.
4842struct Types0 {};
4843
4844// Type lists of length 1, 2, 3, and so on.
4845
4846template <typename T1>
4847struct Types1 {
4848 typedef T1 Head;
4849 typedef Types0 Tail;
4850};
4851template <typename T1, typename T2>
4852struct Types2 {
4853 typedef T1 Head;
4854 typedef Types1<T2> Tail;
4855};

4858struct Types3 {
4859 typedef T1 Head;
4860 typedef Types2<T2, T3> Tail;
4861};

4865 typedef T1 Head;
4866 typedef Types3<T2, T3, T4> Tail;
