10544
10545// Prints the given number of bytes in the given object to the given
10546// ostream.
10547GTEST_API_ void PrintBytesInObjectTo(const unsigned char* obj_bytes,
10548 size_t count,
10549 ::std::ostream* os);
10550
10551// For selecting which printer to use when a given type has neither <<
10552// nor PrintTo().
10553enum TypeKind {
10554 kProtobuf, // a protobuf type
10555 kConvertibleToInteger, // a type implicitly convertible to BiggestInt
10556 // (e.g. a named or unnamed enum type)
10557#if GTEST_HAS_ABSL
10558 kConvertibleToStringView, // a type implicitly convertible to
10559 // absl::string_view
10560#endif
10561 kOtherType // anything else
10562};
10563
10564// TypeWithoutFormatter<T, kTypeKind>::PrintValue(value, os) is called
10565// by the universal printer to print a value of type T when neither
10566// operator<< nor PrintTo() is defined for T, where kTypeKind is the
10567// "kind" of T as defined by enum TypeKind.
10568template <typename T, TypeKind kTypeKind>
10569class TypeWithoutFormatter {
10570 public:
10571 // This default version is called when kTypeKind is kOtherType.
10572 static void PrintValue(const T& value, ::std::ostream* os) {
10573 PrintBytesInObjectTo(static_cast<const unsigned char*>(
10574 reinterpret_cast<const void*>(&value)),
10575 sizeof(value), os);
10576 }
10577};
10578
10579// We print a protobuf using its ShortDebugString() when the string
10580// doesn't exceed this many characters; otherwise we print it using
10581// DebugString() for better readability.
10582const size_t kProtobufOneLinerMaxLength = 50;
10583
10584template <typename T>
10585class TypeWithoutFormatter<T, kProtobuf> {
10586 public:
10587 static void PrintValue(const T& value, ::std::ostream* os) {
10588 std::string pretty_str = value.ShortDebugString();
10589 if (pretty_str.length() > kProtobufOneLinerMaxLength) {
10590 pretty_str = "\n" + value.DebugString();
10591 }
10592 *os << ("<" + pretty_str + ">");
10593 }
10594};
10595
10596template <typename T>
10597class TypeWithoutFormatter<T, kConvertibleToInteger> {
10598 public:
10599 // Since T has no << operator or PrintTo() but can be implicitly
10600 // converted to BiggestInt, we print it as a BiggestInt.
10601 //
10602 // Most likely T is an enum type (either named or unnamed), in which
10603 // case printing it as an integer is the desired behavior. In case
10604 // T is not an enum, printing it as an integer is the best we can do
10605 // given that it has no user-defined printer.
10606 static void PrintValue(const T& value, ::std::ostream* os) {
10607 const internal::BiggestInt kBigInt = static_cast<internal::BiggestInt>(value);
10608 *os << kBigInt;
10609 }
10610};
10611
10612#if GTEST_HAS_ABSL
10613template <typename T>
10614class TypeWithoutFormatter<T, kConvertibleToStringView> {
10615 public:
10616 // Since T has neither operator<< nor PrintTo() but can be implicitly
10617 // converted to absl::string_view, we print it as a absl::string_view.
10618 //
10619 // Note: the implementation is further below, as it depends on
10620 // internal::PrintTo symbol which is defined later in the file.
10621 static void PrintValue(const T& value, ::std::ostream* os);
10622};
10623#endif
10624
10625// Prints the given value to the given ostream. If the value is a
10626// protocol message, its debug string is printed; if it's an enum or
10627// of a type implicitly convertible to BiggestInt, it's printed as an
10628// integer; otherwise the bytes in the value are printed. This is
10629// what UniversalPrinter<T>::Print() does when it knows nothing about
10630// type T and T has neither << operator nor PrintTo().
10631//
10632// A user can override this behavior for a class type Foo by defining
10633// a << operator in the namespace where Foo is defined.
10634//
10635// We put this operator in namespace 'internal2' instead of 'internal'
10636// to simplify the implementation, as much code in 'internal' needs to
10637// use << in STL, which would conflict with our own << were it defined
10638// in 'internal'.
10639//
10640// Note that this operator<< takes a generic std::basic_ostream<Char,
10641// CharTraits> type instead of the more restricted std::ostream. If
10642// we define it to take an std::ostream instead, we'll get an
10643// "ambiguous overloads" compiler error when trying to print a type
10644// Foo that supports streaming to std::basic_ostream<Char,
10645// CharTraits>, as the compiler cannot tell whether
10646// operator<<(std::ostream&, const T&) or
10647// operator<<(std::basic_stream<Char, CharTraits>, const Foo&) is more
10648// specific.
10649template <typename Char, typename CharTraits, typename T>
10650::std::basic_ostream<Char, CharTraits>& operator<<(
10651 ::std::basic_ostream<Char, CharTraits>& os, const T& x) {
10652 TypeWithoutFormatter<T, (internal::IsAProtocolMessage<T>::value
10653 ? kProtobuf
10654 : internal::ImplicitlyConvertible<
10655 const T&, internal::BiggestInt>::value
10656 ? kConvertibleToInteger
10657 :
10658#if GTEST_HAS_ABSL
10659 internal::ImplicitlyConvertible<
10660 const T&, absl::string_view>::value
10661 ? kConvertibleToStringView
10662 :
10663#endif
10664 kOtherType)>::PrintValue(x, &os);
10665 return os;
10666}
10667
10668} // namespace internal2
10669} // namespace testing
10670
10671// This namespace MUST NOT BE NESTED IN ::testing, or the name look-up
10672// magic needed for implementing UniversalPrinter won't work.
10673namespace testing_internal {
10674
10675// Used to print a value that is not an STL-style container when the
10676// user doesn't define PrintTo() for it.
10677template <typename T>
10678void DefaultPrintNonContainerTo(const T& value, ::std::ostream* os) {
10679 // With the following statement, during unqualified name lookup,
10680 // testing::internal2::operator<< appears as if it was declared in
10681 // the nearest enclosing namespace that contains both
10682 // ::testing_internal and ::testing::internal2, i.e. the global
10683 // namespace. For more details, refer to the C++ Standard section
10684 // 7.3.4-1 [namespace.udir]. This allows us to fall back onto
10685 // testing::internal2::operator<< in case T doesn't come with a <<
10686 // operator.
10687 //
10688 // We cannot write 'using ::testing::internal2::operator<<;', which
10689 // gcc 3.3 fails to compile due to a compiler bug.
10690 using namespace ::testing::internal2; // NOLINT
10691
10692 // Assuming T is defined in namespace foo, in the next statement,
10693 // the compiler will consider all of:
10694 //
10695 // 1. foo::operator<< (thanks to Koenig look-up),
10696 // 2. ::operator<< (as the current namespace is enclosed in ::),
10697 // 3. testing::internal2::operator<< (thanks to the using statement above).
10698 //
10699 // The operator<< whose type matches T best will be picked.
10700 //
10701 // We deliberately allow #2 to be a candidate, as sometimes it's
10702 // impossible to define #1 (e.g. when foo is ::std, defining
10703 // anything in it is undefined behavior unless you are a compiler
10704 // vendor.).
10705 *os << value;
10706}
10707
10708} // namespace testing_internal
10709
10710namespace testing {
10711namespace internal {

10713// FormatForComparison<ToPrint, OtherOperand>::Format(value) formats a
10714// value of type ToPrint that is an operand of a comparison assertion
10715// (e.g. ASSERT_EQ). OtherOperand is the type of the other operand in
10716// the comparison, and is used to help determine the best way to
10717// format the value. In particular, when the value is a C string
10718// (char pointer) and the other operand is an STL string object, we
10719// want to format the C string as a string, since we know it is
10720// compared by value with the string object. If the value is a char
10721// pointer but the other operand is not an STL string object, we don't
10722// know whether the pointer is supposed to point to a NUL-terminated
10723// string, and thus want to print it as a pointer to be safe.
10724//
10725// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN A USER PROGRAM.
10726
10727// The default case.
10728template <typename ToPrint, typename OtherOperand>
10729class FormatForComparison {
10730 public:
10731 static ::std::string Format(const ToPrint& value) {
10732 return ::testing::PrintToString(value);
10733 }
10734};
10735
10736// Array.
10737template <typename ToPrint, size_t N, typename OtherOperand>
10738class FormatForComparison<ToPrint[N], OtherOperand> {
10739 public:
10740 static ::std::string Format(const ToPrint* value) {
10741 return FormatForComparison<const ToPrint*, OtherOperand>::Format(value);
10742 }
10743};
10744
10745// By default, print C string as pointers to be safe, as we don't know
10746// whether they actually point to a NUL-terminated string.
10747
10748#define GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_POINTER_(CharType) \
10749 template <typename OtherOperand> \
10750 class FormatForComparison<CharType*, OtherOperand> { \
10751 public: \
10752 static ::std::string Format(CharType* value) { \
10753 return ::testing::PrintToString(static_cast<const void*>(value)); \
10754 } \
10755 }
10756
10757GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_POINTER_(char);
10758GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_POINTER_(const char);
10759GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_POINTER_(wchar_t);
10760GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_POINTER_(const wchar_t);
10761
10762#undef GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_POINTER_
10763
10764// If a C string is compared with an STL string object, we know it's meant
10765// to point to a NUL-terminated string, and thus can print it as a string.
10766
10767#define GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_STRING_(CharType, OtherStringType) \
10768 template <> \
10769 class FormatForComparison<CharType*, OtherStringType> { \
10770 public: \
10771 static ::std::string Format(CharType* value) { \
10772 return ::testing::PrintToString(value); \
10773 } \
10774 }
10775
10776GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_STRING_(char, ::std::string);
10777GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_STRING_(const char, ::std::string);
10778
10779#if GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_STRING
10780GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_STRING_(char, ::string);
10781GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_STRING_(const char, ::string);
10782#endif
10783
10784#if GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_WSTRING
10785GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_STRING_(wchar_t, ::wstring);
10786GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_STRING_(const wchar_t, ::wstring);
10787#endif
10788
10789#if GTEST_HAS_STD_WSTRING
10790GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_STRING_(wchar_t, ::std::wstring);
10791GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_STRING_(const wchar_t, ::std::wstring);
10792#endif
10793
10794#undef GTEST_IMPL_FORMAT_C_STRING_AS_STRING_

10796// Formats a comparison assertion (e.g. ASSERT_EQ, EXPECT_LT, and etc)
10797// operand to be used in a failure message. The type (but not value)
10798// of the other operand may affect the format. This allows us to
10799// print a char* as a raw pointer when it is compared against another
10800// char* or void*, and print it as a C string when it is compared
10801// against an std::string object, for example.
10802//
10803// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN A USER PROGRAM.
10804template <typename T1, typename T2>
10805std::string FormatForComparisonFailureMessage(
10806 const T1& value, const T2& /* other_operand */) {
10807 return FormatForComparison<T1, T2>::Format(value);
10808}

10810// UniversalPrinter<T>::Print(value, ostream_ptr) prints the given
10811// value to the given ostream. The caller must ensure that
10812// 'ostream_ptr' is not NULL, or the behavior is undefined.
10813//
10814// We define UniversalPrinter as a class template (as opposed to a
10815// function template), as we need to partially specialize it for
10816// reference types, which cannot be done with function templates.
10817template <typename T>
10818class UniversalPrinter;
10819
10820template <typename T>
10821void UniversalPrint(const T& value, ::std::ostream* os);
10822
10823enum DefaultPrinterType {
10824 kPrintContainer,
10825 kPrintPointer,
10826 kPrintFunctionPointer,
10827 kPrintOther,
10828};
10829template <DefaultPrinterType type> struct WrapPrinterType {};
10830
10831// Used to print an STL-style container when the user doesn't define
10832// a PrintTo() for it.
10833template <typename C>
10834void DefaultPrintTo(WrapPrinterType<kPrintContainer> /* dummy */,
10835 const C& container, ::std::ostream* os) {
10836 const size_t kMaxCount = 32; // The maximum number of elements to print.
10837 *os << '{';
10838 size_t count = 0;
10839 for (typename C::const_iterator it = container.begin();
10840 it != container.end(); ++it, ++count) {
10841 if (count > 0) {
10842 *os << ',';
10843 if (count == kMaxCount) { // Enough has been printed.
10844 *os << " ...";
10845 break;
10846 }
10847 }
10848 *os << ' ';
10849 // We cannot call PrintTo(*it, os) here as PrintTo() doesn't
10850 // handle *it being a native array.
10851 internal::UniversalPrint(*it, os);
10852 }
10853
10854 if (count > 0) {
10855 *os << ' ';
10856 }
10857 *os << '}';
10858}
10859
10860// Used to print a pointer that is neither a char pointer nor a member
10861// pointer, when the user doesn't define PrintTo() for it. (A member
10862// variable pointer or member function pointer doesn't really point to
10863// a location in the address space. Their representation is
10864// implementation-defined. Therefore they will be printed as raw
10865// bytes.)
10866template <typename T>
10867void DefaultPrintTo(WrapPrinterType<kPrintPointer> /* dummy */,
10868 T* p, ::std::ostream* os) {
10869 if (p == NULL) {
10870 *os << "NULL";
10871 } else {
10872 // T is not a function type. We just call << to print p,
10873 // relying on ADL to pick up user-defined << for their pointer
10874 // types, if any.
10875 *os << p;
10876 }
10877}
10878template <typename T>
10879void DefaultPrintTo(WrapPrinterType<kPrintFunctionPointer> /* dummy */,
10880 T* p, ::std::ostream* os) {
10881 if (p == NULL) {
10882 *os << "NULL";
10883 } else {
10884 // T is a function type, so '*os << p' doesn't do what we want
10885 // (it just prints p as bool). We want to print p as a const
10886 // void*.
10887 *os << reinterpret_cast<const void*>(p);
10888 }
10889}
10890
10891// Used to print a non-container, non-pointer value when the user
10892// doesn't define PrintTo() for it.
10893template <typename T>
10894void DefaultPrintTo(WrapPrinterType<kPrintOther> /* dummy */,
10895 const T& value, ::std::ostream* os) {
10896 ::testing_internal::DefaultPrintNonContainerTo(value, os);
10897}
10898
10899// Prints the given value using the << operator if it has one;
10900// otherwise prints the bytes in it. This is what
10901// UniversalPrinter<T>::Print() does when PrintTo() is not specialized
10902// or overloaded for type T.
10903//
10904// A user can override this behavior for a class type Foo by defining
10905// an overload of PrintTo() in the namespace where Foo is defined. We
10906// give the user this option as sometimes defining a << operator for
10907// Foo is not desirable (e.g. the coding style may prevent doing it,
10908// or there is already a << operator but it doesn't do what the user
10909// wants).
10910template <typename T>
10911void PrintTo(const T& value, ::std::ostream* os) {
10912 // DefaultPrintTo() is overloaded. The type of its first argument
10913 // determines which version will be picked.
10914 //
10915 // Note that we check for container types here, prior to we check
10916 // for protocol message types in our operator<<. The rationale is:
10917 //
10918 // For protocol messages, we want to give people a chance to
10919 // override Google Mock's format by defining a PrintTo() or
10920 // operator<<. For STL containers, other formats can be
10921 // incompatible with Google Mock's format for the container
10922 // elements; therefore we check for container types here to ensure
10923 // that our format is used.
10924 //
10925 // Note that MSVC and clang-cl do allow an implicit conversion from
10926 // pointer-to-function to pointer-to-object, but clang-cl warns on it.
10927 // So don't use ImplicitlyConvertible if it can be helped since it will
10928 // cause this warning, and use a separate overload of DefaultPrintTo for
10929 // function pointers so that the `*os << p` in the object pointer overload
10930 // doesn't cause that warning either.
10931 DefaultPrintTo(
10932 WrapPrinterType <
10933 (sizeof(IsContainerTest<T>(0)) == sizeof(IsContainer)) &&
10934 !IsRecursiveContainer<T>::value
10935 ? kPrintContainer
10936 : !is_pointer<T>::value
10937 ? kPrintOther
10938#if GTEST_LANG_CXX11
10939 : std::is_function<typename std::remove_pointer<T>::type>::value
10940#else
10941 : !internal::ImplicitlyConvertible<T, const void*>::value
10942#endif
10943 ? kPrintFunctionPointer
10944 : kPrintPointer > (),
10945 value, os);
10946}
10947
10948// The following list of PrintTo() overloads tells
10949// UniversalPrinter<T>::Print() how to print standard types (built-in
10950// types, strings, plain arrays, and pointers).
10951
10952// Overloads for various char types.
10953GTEST_API_ void PrintTo(unsigned char c, ::std::ostream* os);
10954GTEST_API_ void PrintTo(signed char c, ::std::ostream* os);
10955inline void PrintTo(char c, ::std::ostream* os) {
10956 // When printing a plain char, we always treat it as unsigned. This
10957 // way, the output won't be affected by whether the compiler thinks
10958 // char is signed or not.
10959 PrintTo(static_cast<unsigned char>(c), os);
10960}

10963inline void PrintTo(bool x, ::std::ostream* os) {
10964 *os << (x ? "true" : "false");
10965}

10967// Overload for wchar_t type.

10969// code otherwise and also as its decimal code (except for L'\0').

10971// as signed integer when wchar_t is implemented by the compiler
10972// as a signed type and is printed as an unsigned integer when wchar_t
10973// is implemented as an unsigned type.
10974GTEST_API_ void PrintTo(wchar_t wc, ::std::ostream* os);

11013// Prints the given number of elements in an array, without printing

11017 UniversalPrint(a[0], os);

11019 *os << ", ";
11020 UniversalPrint(a[i], os);
11021 }

11158 // a reference type. The same for printing value.second.
11159 UniversalPrinter<T1>::Print(value.first, os);

11161 UniversalPrinter<T2>::Print(value.second, os);

11165// Implements printing a non-reference type T by letting the compiler
11166// pick the right overload of PrintTo() for T.
11167template <typename T>
11168class UniversalPrinter {
11169 public:
11170 // MSVC warns about adding const to a function type, so we want to
11171 // disable the warning.
11172 GTEST_DISABLE_MSC_WARNINGS_PUSH_(4180)
11173
11174 // Note: we deliberately don't call this PrintTo(), as that name
11175 // conflicts with ::testing::internal::PrintTo in the body of the
11176 // function.
11177 static void Print(const T& value, ::std::ostream* os) {
11178 // By default, ::testing::internal::PrintTo() is used for printing
11179 // the value.
11180 //
11181 // Thanks to Koenig look-up, if T is a class and has its own
11182 // PrintTo() function defined in its namespace, that function will
11183 // be visible here. Since it is more specific than the generic ones
11184 // in ::testing::internal, it will be picked by the compiler in the
11185 // following statement - exactly what we want.
11186 PrintTo(value, os);
11187 }
11188
11189 GTEST_DISABLE_MSC_WARNINGS_POP_()
11190};

11194// Printer for absl::optional
11195
11196template <typename T>
11197class UniversalPrinter<::absl::optional<T>> {
11198 public:
11199 static void Print(const ::absl::optional<T>& value, ::std::ostream* os) {
11200 *os << '(';
11201 if (!value) {
11202 *os << "nullopt";
11203 } else {
11204 UniversalPrint(*value, os);
11205 }
11206 *os << ')';
11207 }
11208};

11210// Printer for absl::variant
11211
11212template <typename... T>
11213class UniversalPrinter<::absl::variant<T...>> {
11214 public:
11215 static void Print(const ::absl::variant<T...>& value, ::std::ostream* os) {
11216 *os << '(';
11217 absl::visit(Visitor{os}, value);
11218 *os << ')';
11219 }
11220
11221 private:
11222 struct Visitor {
11223 template <typename U>
11224 void operator()(const U& u) const {
11225 *os << "'" << GetTypeName<U>() << "' with value ";
11226 UniversalPrint(u, os);
11227 }
11228 ::std::ostream* os;
11229 };
11230};

11234// UniversalPrintArray(begin, len, os) prints an array of 'len'
11235// elements, starting at address 'begin'.
11236template <typename T>
11237void UniversalPrintArray(const T* begin, size_t len, ::std::ostream* os) {
11238 if (len == 0) {
11239 *os << "{}";
11240 } else {
11241 *os << "{ ";
11242 const size_t kThreshold = 18;
11243 const size_t kChunkSize = 8;
11244 // If the array has more than kThreshold elements, we'll have to
11245 // omit some details by printing only the first and the last
11246 // kChunkSize elements.
11247 // FIXME: let the user control the threshold using a flag.
11248 if (len <= kThreshold) {
11249 PrintRawArrayTo(begin, len, os);
11250 } else {
11251 PrintRawArrayTo(begin, kChunkSize, os);
11252 *os << ", ..., ";
11253 PrintRawArrayTo(begin + len - kChunkSize, kChunkSize, os);
11254 }
11255 *os << " }";
11256 }
11257}

11262// This overload prints a (const) wchar_t array compactly.

11264 const wchar_t* begin, size_t len, ::std::ostream* os);

11266// Implements printing an array type T[N].
11267template <typename T, size_t N>
11268class UniversalPrinter<T[N]> {
11269 public:
11270 // Prints the given array, omitting some elements when there are too
11271 // many.
11272 static void Print(const T (&a)[N], ::std::ostream* os) {
11273 UniversalPrintArray(a, N, os);
11274 }
11275};

11277// Implements printing a reference type T&.
11278template <typename T>
11279class UniversalPrinter<T&> {
11280 public:
11281 // MSVC warns about adding const to a function type, so we want to
11282 // disable the warning.
11283 GTEST_DISABLE_MSC_WARNINGS_PUSH_(4180)
11284
11285 static void Print(const T& value, ::std::ostream* os) {
11286 // Prints the address of the value. We use reinterpret_cast here
11287 // as static_cast doesn't compile when T is a function type.
11288 *os << "@" << reinterpret_cast<const void*>(&value) << " ";
11289
11290 // Then prints the value itself.
11291 UniversalPrint(value, os);
11292 }
11293
11294 GTEST_DISABLE_MSC_WARNINGS_POP_()
11295};

11301template <typename T>
11302class UniversalTersePrinter {

11305 UniversalPrint(value, os);
11306 }

11368// Prints a value using the type inferred by the compiler. The
11369// difference between this and UniversalTersePrint() is that for a
11370// (const) char pointer, this prints both the pointer and the
11371// NUL-terminated string.
11372template <typename T>
11373void UniversalPrint(const T& value, ::std::ostream* os) {

11380typedef ::std::vector< ::std::string> Strings;
11381
11382// TuplePolicy<TupleT> must provide:
11383// - tuple_size
11384// size of tuple TupleT.
11385// - get<size_t I>(const TupleT& t)
11386// static function extracting element I of tuple TupleT.
11387// - tuple_element<size_t I>::type
11388// type of element I of tuple TupleT.
11389template <typename TupleT>
11390struct TuplePolicy;
11391
11392#if GTEST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE
11393template <typename TupleT>
11394struct TuplePolicy {
11395 typedef TupleT Tuple;
11396 static const size_t tuple_size = ::std::tr1::tuple_size<Tuple>::value;
11397
11398 template <size_t I>
11399 struct tuple_element : ::std::tr1::tuple_element<static_cast<int>(I), Tuple> {
11400 };
11401
11402 template <size_t I>
11403 static typename AddReference<const typename ::std::tr1::tuple_element<
11404 I, Tuple>::type>::type
11405 get(const Tuple& tuple) {
11406 return ::std::tr1::get<I>(tuple);
11407 }
11408};
11409template <typename TupleT>
11410const size_t TuplePolicy<TupleT>::tuple_size;
11411#endif // GTEST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE
11412
11413#if GTEST_HAS_STD_TUPLE_
11414template <typename... Types>
11415struct TuplePolicy< ::std::tuple<Types...> > {
11416 typedef ::std::tuple<Types...> Tuple;
11417 static const size_t tuple_size = ::std::tuple_size<Tuple>::value;
11418
11419 template <size_t I>
11420 struct tuple_element : ::std::tuple_element<I, Tuple> {};
11421
11422 template <size_t I>
11423 static const typename ::std::tuple_element<I, Tuple>::type& get(
11424 const Tuple& tuple) {
11425 return ::std::get<I>(tuple);
11426 }
11427};
11428template <typename... Types>
11429const size_t TuplePolicy< ::std::tuple<Types...> >::tuple_size;
11430#endif // GTEST_HAS_STD_TUPLE_
11431
11432#if GTEST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE || GTEST_HAS_STD_TUPLE_
11433// This helper template allows PrintTo() for tuples and
11434// UniversalTersePrintTupleFieldsToStrings() to be defined by
11435// induction on the number of tuple fields. The idea is that
11436// TuplePrefixPrinter<N>::PrintPrefixTo(t, os) prints the first N
11437// fields in tuple t, and can be defined in terms of
11438// TuplePrefixPrinter<N - 1>.
11439//
11440// The inductive case.
11441template <size_t N>
11442struct TuplePrefixPrinter {
11443 // Prints the first N fields of a tuple.
11444 template <typename Tuple>
11445 static void PrintPrefixTo(const Tuple& t, ::std::ostream* os) {
11446 TuplePrefixPrinter<N - 1>::PrintPrefixTo(t, os);
11447 GTEST_INTENTIONAL_CONST_COND_PUSH_()
11448 if (N > 1) {
11449 GTEST_INTENTIONAL_CONST_COND_POP_()
11450 *os << ", ";
11451 }
11452 UniversalPrinter<
11453 typename TuplePolicy<Tuple>::template tuple_element<N - 1>::type>
11454 ::Print(TuplePolicy<Tuple>::template get<N - 1>(t), os);
11455 }
11456
11457 // Tersely prints the first N fields of a tuple to a string vector,
11458 // one element for each field.
11459 template <typename Tuple>
11460 static void TersePrintPrefixToStrings(const Tuple& t, Strings* strings) {
11461 TuplePrefixPrinter<N - 1>::TersePrintPrefixToStrings(t, strings);
11462 ::std::stringstream ss;
11463 UniversalTersePrint(TuplePolicy<Tuple>::template get<N - 1>(t), &ss);
11464 strings->push_back(ss.str());
11465 }
11466};
11467
11468// Base case.
11469template <>
11470struct TuplePrefixPrinter<0> {
11471 template <typename Tuple>
11472 static void PrintPrefixTo(const Tuple&, ::std::ostream*) {}
11473
11474 template <typename Tuple>
11475 static void TersePrintPrefixToStrings(const Tuple&, Strings*) {}
11476};
11477
11478// Helper function for printing a tuple.
11479// Tuple must be either std::tr1::tuple or std::tuple type.
11480template <typename Tuple>
11481void PrintTupleTo(const Tuple& t, ::std::ostream* os) {
11482 *os << "(";
11483 TuplePrefixPrinter<TuplePolicy<Tuple>::tuple_size>::PrintPrefixTo(t, os);
11484 *os << ")";
11485}
11486
11487// Prints the fields of a tuple tersely to a string vector, one
11488// element for each field. See the comment before
11489// UniversalTersePrint() for how we define "tersely".
11490template <typename Tuple>
11491Strings UniversalTersePrintTupleFieldsToStrings(const Tuple& value) {
11492 Strings result;
11493 TuplePrefixPrinter<TuplePolicy<Tuple>::tuple_size>::
11494 TersePrintPrefixToStrings(value, &result);
11495 return result;
11496}
11497#endif // GTEST_HAS_TR1_TUPLE || GTEST_HAS_STD_TUPLE_
11498

11601template <typename> class ParamGeneratorInterface;
11602template <typename> class ParamGenerator;
11603
11604// Interface for iterating over elements provided by an implementation
11605// of ParamGeneratorInterface<T>.
11606template <typename T>
11607class ParamIteratorInterface {
11608 public:
11609 virtual ~ParamIteratorInterface() {}
11610 // A pointer to the base generator instance.
11611 // Used only for the purposes of iterator comparison
11612 // to make sure that two iterators belong to the same generator.
11613 virtual const ParamGeneratorInterface<T>* BaseGenerator() const = 0;
11614 // Advances iterator to point to the next element
11615 // provided by the generator. The caller is responsible
11616 // for not calling Advance() on an iterator equal to
11617 // BaseGenerator()->End().
11618 virtual void Advance() = 0;
11619 // Clones the iterator object. Used for implementing copy semantics
11620 // of ParamIterator<T>.
11621 virtual ParamIteratorInterface* Clone() const = 0;
11622 // Dereferences the current iterator and provides (read-only) access
11623 // to the pointed value. It is the caller's responsibility not to call
11624 // Current() on an iterator equal to BaseGenerator()->End().
11625 // Used for implementing ParamGenerator<T>::operator*().
11626 virtual const T* Current() const = 0;
11627 // Determines whether the given iterator and other point to the same
11628 // element in the sequence generated by the generator.
11629 // Used for implementing ParamGenerator<T>::operator==().
11630 virtual bool Equals(const ParamIteratorInterface& other) const = 0;
11631};
11632
11633// Class iterating over elements provided by an implementation of
11634// ParamGeneratorInterface<T>. It wraps ParamIteratorInterface<T>
11635// and implements the const forward iterator concept.
11636template <typename T>
11637class ParamIterator {
11638 public:
11639 typedef T value_type;
11640 typedef const T& reference;
11641 typedef ptrdiff_t difference_type;
11642
11643 // ParamIterator assumes ownership of the impl_ pointer.
11644 ParamIterator(const ParamIterator& other) : impl_(other.impl_->Clone()) {}
11645 ParamIterator& operator=(const ParamIterator& other) {
11646 if (this != &other)
11647 impl_.reset(other.impl_->Clone());
11648 return *this;
11649 }
11650
11651 const T& operator*() const { return *impl_->Current(); }
11652 const T* operator->() const { return impl_->Current(); }
11653 // Prefix version of operator++.
11654 ParamIterator& operator++() {
11655 impl_->Advance();
11656 return *this;
11657 }
11658 // Postfix version of operator++.
11659 ParamIterator operator++(int /*unused*/) {
11660 ParamIteratorInterface<T>* clone = impl_->Clone();
11661 impl_->Advance();
11662 return ParamIterator(clone);
11663 }
11664 bool operator==(const ParamIterator& other) const {
11665 return impl_.get() == other.impl_.get() || impl_->Equals(*other.impl_);
11666 }
11667 bool operator!=(const ParamIterator& other) const {
11668 return !(*this == other);
11669 }
11670
11671 private:
11672 friend class ParamGenerator<T>;
11673 explicit ParamIterator(ParamIteratorInterface<T>* impl) : impl_(impl) {}
11674 scoped_ptr<ParamIteratorInterface<T> > impl_;
11675};
11676
11677// ParamGeneratorInterface<T> is the binary interface to access generators
11678// defined in other translation units.
11679template <typename T>
11680class ParamGeneratorInterface {
11681 public:
11682 typedef T ParamType;
11683
11684 virtual ~ParamGeneratorInterface() {}
11685
11686 // Generator interface definition
11687 virtual ParamIteratorInterface<T>* Begin() const = 0;
11688 virtual ParamIteratorInterface<T>* End() const = 0;
11689};
11690
11691// Wraps ParamGeneratorInterface<T> and provides general generator syntax
11692// compatible with the STL Container concept.
11693// This class implements copy initialization semantics and the contained
11694// ParamGeneratorInterface<T> instance is shared among all copies
11695// of the original object. This is possible because that instance is immutable.
11696template<typename T>
11697class ParamGenerator {
11698 public:
11699 typedef ParamIterator<T> iterator;
11700
11701 explicit ParamGenerator(ParamGeneratorInterface<T>* impl) : impl_(impl) {}
11702 ParamGenerator(const ParamGenerator& other) : impl_(other.impl_) {}
11703
11704 ParamGenerator& operator=(const ParamGenerator& other) {
11705 impl_ = other.impl_;
11706 return *this;
11707 }
11708
11709 iterator begin() const { return iterator(impl_->Begin()); }
11710 iterator end() const { return iterator(impl_->End()); }
11711
11712 private:
11713 linked_ptr<const ParamGeneratorInterface<T> > impl_;
11714};
11715
11716// Generates values from a range of two comparable values. Can be used to
11717// generate sequences of user-defined types that implement operator+() and
11718// operator<().
11719// This class is used in the Range() function.
11720template <typename T, typename IncrementT>
11721class RangeGenerator : public ParamGeneratorInterface<T> {
11722 public:
11723 RangeGenerator(T begin, T end, IncrementT step)
11724 : begin_(begin), end_(end),
11725 step_(step), end_index_(CalculateEndIndex(begin, end, step)) {}
11726 virtual ~RangeGenerator() {}
11727
11728 virtual ParamIteratorInterface<T>* Begin() const {
11729 return new Iterator(this, begin_, 0, step_);
11730 }
11731 virtual ParamIteratorInterface<T>* End() const {
11732 return new Iterator(this, end_, end_index_, step_);
11733 }
11734
11735 private:
11736 class Iterator : public ParamIteratorInterface<T> {
11737 public:
11738 Iterator(const ParamGeneratorInterface<T>* base, T value, int index,
11739 IncrementT step)
11740 : base_(base), value_(value), index_(index), step_(step) {}
11741 virtual ~Iterator() {}
11742
11743 virtual const ParamGeneratorInterface<T>* BaseGenerator() const {
11744 return base_;
11745 }
11746 virtual void Advance() {
11747 value_ = static_cast<T>(value_ + step_);
11748 index_++;
11749 }
11750 virtual ParamIteratorInterface<T>* Clone() const {
11751 return new Iterator(*this);
11752 }
11753 virtual const T* Current() const { return &value_; }
11754 virtual bool Equals(const ParamIteratorInterface<T>& other) const {
11755 // Having the same base generator guarantees that the other
11756 // iterator is of the same type and we can downcast.
11757 GTEST_CHECK_(BaseGenerator() == other.BaseGenerator())
11758 << "The program attempted to compare iterators "
11759 << "from different generators." << std::endl;
11760 const int other_index =
11761 CheckedDowncastToActualType<const Iterator>(&other)->index_;
11762 return index_ == other_index;
11763 }
11764
11765 private:
11766 Iterator(const Iterator& other)
11767 : ParamIteratorInterface<T>(),
11768 base_(other.base_), value_(other.value_), index_(other.index_),
11769 step_(other.step_) {}
11770
11771 // No implementation - assignment is unsupported.
11772 void operator=(const Iterator& other) = delete;
11773
11774 const ParamGeneratorInterface<T>* const base_;
11775 T value_;
11776 int index_;
11777 const IncrementT step_;
11778 }; // class RangeGenerator::Iterator
11779
11780 static int CalculateEndIndex(const T& begin,
11781 const T& end,
11782 const IncrementT& step) {
11783 int end_index = 0;
11784 for (T i = begin; i < end; i = static_cast<T>(i + step))
11785 end_index++;
11786 return end_index;
11787 }
11788
11789 // No implementation - assignment is unsupported.
11790 void operator=(const RangeGenerator& other) = delete;
11791
11792 const T begin_;
11793 const T end_;
11794 const IncrementT step_;
11795 // The index for the end() iterator. All the elements in the generated
11796 // sequence are indexed (0-based) to aid iterator comparison.
11797 const int end_index_;
11798}; // class RangeGenerator
11799
11800
11801// Generates values from a pair of STL-style iterators. Used in the
11802// ValuesIn() function. The elements are copied from the source range
11803// since the source can be located on the stack, and the generator
11804// is likely to persist beyond that stack frame.
11805template <typename T>
11806class ValuesInIteratorRangeGenerator : public ParamGeneratorInterface<T> {
11807 public:
11808 template <typename ForwardIterator>
11809 ValuesInIteratorRangeGenerator(ForwardIterator begin, ForwardIterator end)
11810 : container_(begin, end) {}
11811 virtual ~ValuesInIteratorRangeGenerator() {}
11812
11813 virtual ParamIteratorInterface<T>* Begin() const {
11814 return new Iterator(this, container_.begin());
11815 }
11816 virtual ParamIteratorInterface<T>* End() const {
11817 return new Iterator(this, container_.end());
11818 }
11819
11820 private:
11821 typedef typename ::std::vector<T> ContainerType;
11822
11823 class Iterator : public ParamIteratorInterface<T> {
11824 public:
11825 Iterator(const ParamGeneratorInterface<T>* base,
11826 typename ContainerType::const_iterator iterator)
11827 : base_(base), iterator_(iterator) {}
11828 virtual ~Iterator() {}
11829
11830 virtual const ParamGeneratorInterface<T>* BaseGenerator() const {
11831 return base_;
11832 }
11833 virtual void Advance() {
11834 ++iterator_;
11835 value_.reset();
11836 }
11837 virtual ParamIteratorInterface<T>* Clone() const {
11838 return new Iterator(*this);
11839 }
11840 // We need to use cached value referenced by iterator_ because *iterator_
11841 // can return a temporary object (and of type other then T), so just
11842 // having "return &*iterator_;" doesn't work.
11843 // value_ is updated here and not in Advance() because Advance()
11844 // can advance iterator_ beyond the end of the range, and we cannot
11845 // detect that fact. The client code, on the other hand, is
11846 // responsible for not calling Current() on an out-of-range iterator.
11847 virtual const T* Current() const {
11848 if (value_.get() == NULL)
11849 value_.reset(new T(*iterator_));
11850 return value_.get();
11851 }
11852 virtual bool Equals(const ParamIteratorInterface<T>& other) const {
11853 // Having the same base generator guarantees that the other
11854 // iterator is of the same type and we can downcast.
11855 GTEST_CHECK_(BaseGenerator() == other.BaseGenerator())
11856 << "The program attempted to compare iterators "
11857 << "from different generators." << std::endl;
11858 return iterator_ ==
11859 CheckedDowncastToActualType<const Iterator>(&other)->iterator_;
11860 }
11861
11862 private:
11863 Iterator(const Iterator& other)
11864 // The explicit constructor call suppresses a false warning
11865 // emitted by gcc when supplied with the -Wextra option.
11866 : ParamIteratorInterface<T>(),
11867 base_(other.base_),
11868 iterator_(other.iterator_) {}
11869
11870 const ParamGeneratorInterface<T>* const base_;
11871 typename ContainerType::const_iterator iterator_;
11872 // A cached value of *iterator_. We keep it here to allow access by
11873 // pointer in the wrapping iterator's operator->().
11874 // value_ needs to be mutable to be accessed in Current().
11875 // Use of scoped_ptr helps manage cached value's lifetime,
11876 // which is bound by the lifespan of the iterator itself.
11877 mutable scoped_ptr<const T> value_;
11878 }; // class ValuesInIteratorRangeGenerator::Iterator
11879
11880 // No implementation - assignment is unsupported.
11881 void operator=(const ValuesInIteratorRangeGenerator& other) = delete;
11882
11883 const ContainerType container_;
11884}; // class ValuesInIteratorRangeGenerator

11920// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN USER CODE.
11921//
11922// Stores a parameter value and later creates tests parameterized with that
11923// value.
11924template <class TestClass>
11925class ParameterizedTestFactory : public internal::TestFactoryBase {

12010// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN USER CODE.
12011//
12012// ParameterizedTestCaseInfo accumulates tests obtained from TEST_P
12013// macro invocations for a particular test case and generators
12014// obtained from INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P macro invocations for that
12015// test case. It registers tests with all values generated by all
12016// generators when asked.
12017template <class TestCase>
12018class ParameterizedTestCaseInfo : public ParameterizedTestCaseInfoBase {
12019 public:
12020 // ParamType and GeneratorCreationFunc are private types but are required
12021 // for declarations of public methods AddTestPattern() and
12022 // AddTestCaseInstantiation().
12023 typedef typename TestCase::ParamType ParamType;
12024 // A function that returns an instance of appropriate generator type.
12025 typedef ParamGenerator<ParamType>(GeneratorCreationFunc)();
12026 typedef typename ParamNameGenFunc<ParamType>::Type ParamNameGeneratorFunc;
12027
12028 explicit ParameterizedTestCaseInfo(
12029 const char* name, CodeLocation code_location)
12030 : test_case_name_(name), code_location_(code_location) {}
12031
12032 // Test case base name for display purposes.
12033 virtual const std::string& GetTestCaseName() const override { return test_case_name_; }
12034 // Test case id to verify identity.
12035 virtual TypeId GetTestCaseTypeId() const override { return GetTypeId<TestCase>(); }
12036 // TEST_P macro uses AddTestPattern() to record information
12037 // about a single test in a LocalTestInfo structure.
12038 // test_case_name is the base name of the test case (without invocation
12039 // prefix). test_base_name is the name of an individual test without
12040 // parameter index. For the test SequenceA/FooTest.DoBar/1 FooTest is
12041 // test case base name and DoBar is test base name.
12042 void AddTestPattern(const char* test_case_name,
12043 const char* test_base_name,
12044 TestMetaFactoryBase<ParamType>* meta_factory) {
12045 tests_.push_back(linked_ptr<TestInfo>(new TestInfo(test_case_name,
12046 test_base_name,
12047 meta_factory)));
12048 }
12049 // INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P macro uses AddGenerator() to record information
12050 // about a generator.
12051 int AddTestCaseInstantiation(const std::string& instantiation_name,
12052 GeneratorCreationFunc* func,
12053 ParamNameGeneratorFunc* name_func,
12054 const char* file, int line) {
12055 instantiations_.push_back(
12056 InstantiationInfo(instantiation_name, func, name_func, file, line));
12057 return 0; // Return value used only to run this method in namespace scope.
12058 }
12059 // UnitTest class invokes this method to register tests in this test case
12060 // test cases right before running tests in RUN_ALL_TESTS macro.
12061 // This method should not be called more then once on any single
12062 // instance of a ParameterizedTestCaseInfoBase derived class.
12063 // UnitTest has a guard to prevent from calling this method more then once.
12064 virtual void RegisterTests() override {
12065 for (typename TestInfoContainer::iterator test_it = tests_.begin();
12066 test_it != tests_.end(); ++test_it) {
12067 linked_ptr<TestInfo> test_info = *test_it;
12068 for (typename InstantiationContainer::iterator gen_it =
12069 instantiations_.begin(); gen_it != instantiations_.end();
12070 ++gen_it) {
12071 const std::string& instantiation_name = gen_it->name;
12072 ParamGenerator<ParamType> generator((*gen_it->generator)());
12073 ParamNameGeneratorFunc* name_func = gen_it->name_func;
12074 const char* file = gen_it->file;
12075 int line = gen_it->line;
12076
12077 std::string test_case_name;
12078 if ( !instantiation_name.empty() )
12079 test_case_name = instantiation_name + "/";
12080 test_case_name += test_info->test_case_base_name;
12081
12082 size_t i = 0;
12083 std::set<std::string> test_param_names;
12084 for (typename ParamGenerator<ParamType>::iterator param_it =
12085 generator.begin();
12086 param_it != generator.end(); ++param_it, ++i) {
12087 Message test_name_stream;
12088
12089 std::string param_name = name_func(
12090 TestParamInfo<ParamType>(*param_it, i));
12091
12092 GTEST_CHECK_(IsValidParamName(param_name))
12093 << "Parameterized test name '" << param_name
12094 << "' is invalid, in " << file
12095 << " line " << line << std::endl;
12096
12097 GTEST_CHECK_(test_param_names.count(param_name) == 0)
12098 << "Duplicate parameterized test name '" << param_name
12099 << "', in " << file << " line " << line << std::endl;
12100
12101 test_param_names.insert(param_name);
12102
12103 test_name_stream << test_info->test_base_name << "/" << param_name;
12104 MakeAndRegisterTestInfo(
12105 test_case_name.c_str(),
12106 test_name_stream.GetString().c_str(),
12107 NULL, // No type parameter.
12108 PrintToString(*param_it).c_str(),
12109 code_location_,
12110 GetTestCaseTypeId(),
12111 TestCase::SetUpTestCase,
12112 TestCase::TearDownTestCase,
12113 test_info->test_meta_factory->CreateTestFactory(*param_it));
12114 } // for param_it
12115 } // for gen_it
12116 } // for test_it
12117 } // RegisterTests
12118
12119 private:
12120 // LocalTestInfo structure keeps information about a single test registered
12121 // with TEST_P macro.
12122 struct TestInfo {
12123 TestInfo(const char* a_test_case_base_name,
12124 const char* a_test_base_name,
12125 TestMetaFactoryBase<ParamType>* a_test_meta_factory) :
12126 test_case_base_name(a_test_case_base_name),
12127 test_base_name(a_test_base_name),
12128 test_meta_factory(a_test_meta_factory) {}
12129
12130 const std::string test_case_base_name;
12131 const std::string test_base_name;
12132 const scoped_ptr<TestMetaFactoryBase<ParamType> > test_meta_factory;
12133 };
12134 typedef ::std::vector<linked_ptr<TestInfo> > TestInfoContainer;
12135 // Records data received from INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P macros:
12136 // <Instantiation name, Sequence generator creation function,
12137 // Name generator function, Source file, Source line>
12138 struct InstantiationInfo {
12139 InstantiationInfo(const std::string &name_in,
12140 GeneratorCreationFunc* generator_in,
12141 ParamNameGeneratorFunc* name_func_in,
12142 const char* file_in,
12143 int line_in)
12144 : name(name_in),
12145 generator(generator_in),
12146 name_func(name_func_in),
12147 file(file_in),
12148 line(line_in) {}
12149
12150 std::string name;
12151 GeneratorCreationFunc* generator;
12152 ParamNameGeneratorFunc* name_func;
12153 const char* file;
12154 int line;
12155 };
12156 typedef ::std::vector<InstantiationInfo> InstantiationContainer;
12157
12158 static bool IsValidParamName(const std::string& name) {
12159 // Check for empty string
12160 if (name.empty())
12161 return false;
12162
12163 // Check for invalid characters
12164 for (std::string::size_type index = 0; index < name.size(); ++index) {
12165 if (!isalnum(name[index]) && name[index] != '_')
12166 return false;
12167 }
12168
12169 return true;
12170 }
12171
12172 const std::string test_case_name_;
12173 CodeLocation code_location_;
12174 TestInfoContainer tests_;
12175 InstantiationContainer instantiations_;
12176
12177 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ParameterizedTestCaseInfo);
12178}; // class ParameterizedTestCaseInfo

12180// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN USER CODE.
12181//
12182// ParameterizedTestCaseRegistry contains a map of ParameterizedTestCaseInfoBase
12183// classes accessed by test case names. TEST_P and INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P
12184// macros use it to locate their corresponding ParameterizedTestCaseInfo
12185// descriptors.
12186class ParameterizedTestCaseRegistry {
12187 public:
12188 ParameterizedTestCaseRegistry() {}
12189 ~ParameterizedTestCaseRegistry() {
12190 for (TestCaseInfoContainer::iterator it = test_case_infos_.begin();
12191 it != test_case_infos_.end(); ++it) {
12192 delete *it;
12193 }
12194 }
12195
12196 // Looks up or creates and returns a structure containing information about
12197 // tests and instantiations of a particular test case.
12198 template <class TestCase>
12199 ParameterizedTestCaseInfo<TestCase>* GetTestCasePatternHolder(
12200 const char* test_case_name,
12201 CodeLocation code_location) {
12202 ParameterizedTestCaseInfo<TestCase>* typed_test_info = NULL;
12203 for (TestCaseInfoContainer::iterator it = test_case_infos_.begin();
12204 it != test_case_infos_.end(); ++it) {
12205 if ((*it)->GetTestCaseName() == test_case_name) {
12206 if ((*it)->GetTestCaseTypeId() != GetTypeId<TestCase>()) {
12207 // Complain about incorrect usage of Google Test facilities
12208 // and terminate the program since we cannot guaranty correct
12209 // test case setup and tear-down in this case.
12210 ReportInvalidTestCaseType(test_case_name, code_location);
12211 posix::Abort();
12212 } else {
12213 // At this point we are sure that the object we found is of the same
12214 // type we are looking for, so we downcast it to that type
12215 // without further checks.
12216 typed_test_info = CheckedDowncastToActualType<
12217 ParameterizedTestCaseInfo<TestCase> >(*it);
12218 }
12219 break;
12220 }
12221 }
12222 if (typed_test_info == NULL) {
12223 typed_test_info = new ParameterizedTestCaseInfo<TestCase>(
12224 test_case_name, code_location);
12225 test_case_infos_.push_back(typed_test_info);
12226 }
12227 return typed_test_info;
12228 }
12229 void RegisterTests() {
12230 for (TestCaseInfoContainer::iterator it = test_case_infos_.begin();
12231 it != test_case_infos_.end(); ++it) {
12232 (*it)->RegisterTests();
12233 }
12234 }
12235
12236 private:
12237 typedef ::std::vector<ParameterizedTestCaseInfoBase*> TestCaseInfoContainer;
12238
12239 TestCaseInfoContainer test_case_infos_;
12240
12241 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ParameterizedTestCaseRegistry);
12242};

17800namespace testing {
17801
17802// Functions producing parameter generators.
17803//
17804// Google Test uses these generators to produce parameters for value-
17805// parameterized tests. When a parameterized test case is instantiated
17806// with a particular generator, Google Test creates and runs tests
17807// for each element in the sequence produced by the generator.
17808//
17809// In the following sample, tests from test case FooTest are instantiated
17810// each three times with parameter values 3, 5, and 8:
17811//
17812// class FooTest : public TestWithParam<int> { ... };
17813//
17814// TEST_P(FooTest, TestThis) {
17815// }
17816// TEST_P(FooTest, TestThat) {
17817// }
17818// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(TestSequence, FooTest, Values(3, 5, 8));
17819//
17820
17821// Range() returns generators providing sequences of values in a range.
17822//
17823// Synopsis:
17824// Range(start, end)
17825// - returns a generator producing a sequence of values {start, start+1,
17826// start+2, ..., }.
17827// Range(start, end, step)
17828// - returns a generator producing a sequence of values {start, start+step,
17829// start+step+step, ..., }.
17830// Notes:
17831// * The generated sequences never include end. For example, Range(1, 5)
17832// returns a generator producing a sequence {1, 2, 3, 4}. Range(1, 9, 2)
17833// returns a generator producing {1, 3, 5, 7}.
17834// * start and end must have the same type. That type may be any integral or
17835// floating-point type or a user defined type satisfying these conditions:
17836// * It must be assignable (have operator=() defined).
17837// * It must have operator+() (operator+(int-compatible type) for
17838// two-operand version).
17839// * It must have operator<() defined.
17840// Elements in the resulting sequences will also have that type.
17841// * Condition start < end must be satisfied in order for resulting sequences
17842// to contain any elements.
17843//
17844template <typename T, typename IncrementT>
17845internal::ParamGenerator<T> Range(T start, T end, IncrementT step) {
17846 return internal::ParamGenerator<T>(
17847 new internal::RangeGenerator<T, IncrementT>(start, end, step));
17848}
17849
17850template <typename T>
17851internal::ParamGenerator<T> Range(T start, T end) {
17852 return Range(start, end, 1);
17853}
17854
17855// ValuesIn() function allows generation of tests with parameters coming from
17856// a container.
17857//
17858// Synopsis:
17859// ValuesIn(const T (&array)[N])
17860// - returns a generator producing sequences with elements from
17861// a C-style array.
17862// ValuesIn(const Container& container)
17863// - returns a generator producing sequences with elements from
17864// an STL-style container.
17865// ValuesIn(Iterator begin, Iterator end)
17866// - returns a generator producing sequences with elements from
17867// a range [begin, end) defined by a pair of STL-style iterators. These
17868// iterators can also be plain C pointers.
17869//
17870// Please note that ValuesIn copies the values from the containers
17871// passed in and keeps them to generate tests in RUN_ALL_TESTS().
17872//
17873// Examples:
17874//
17875// This instantiates tests from test case StringTest
17876// each with C-string values of "foo", "bar", and "baz":
17877//
17878// const char* strings[] = {"foo", "bar", "baz"};
17879// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(StringSequence, StringTest, ValuesIn(strings));
17880//
17881// This instantiates tests from test case StlStringTest
17882// each with STL strings with values "a" and "b":
17883//
17884// ::std::vector< ::std::string> GetParameterStrings() {
17885// ::std::vector< ::std::string> v;
17886// v.push_back("a");
17887// v.push_back("b");
17888// return v;
17889// }
17890//
17891// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(CharSequence,
17892// StlStringTest,
17893// ValuesIn(GetParameterStrings()));
17894//
17895//
17896// This will also instantiate tests from CharTest
17897// each with parameter values 'a' and 'b':
17898//
17899// ::std::list<char> GetParameterChars() {
17900// ::std::list<char> list;
17901// list.push_back('a');
17902// list.push_back('b');
17903// return list;
17904// }
17905// ::std::list<char> l = GetParameterChars();
17906// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(CharSequence2,
17907// CharTest,
17908// ValuesIn(l.begin(), l.end()));
17909//
17910template <typename ForwardIterator>
17911internal::ParamGenerator<
17912 typename ::testing::internal::IteratorTraits<ForwardIterator>::value_type>
17913ValuesIn(ForwardIterator begin, ForwardIterator end) {
17914 typedef typename ::testing::internal::IteratorTraits<ForwardIterator>
17915 ::value_type ParamType;
17916 return internal::ParamGenerator<ParamType>(
17917 new internal::ValuesInIteratorRangeGenerator<ParamType>(begin, end));
17918}
17919
17920template <typename T, size_t N>
17921internal::ParamGenerator<T> ValuesIn(const T (&array)[N]) {
17922 return ValuesIn(array, array + N);
17923}
17924
17925template <class Container>
17926internal::ParamGenerator<typename Container::value_type> ValuesIn(
17927 const Container& container) {
17928 return ValuesIn(container.begin(), container.end());
17929}
17930
17931// Values() allows generating tests from explicitly specified list of
17932// parameters.
17933//
17934// Synopsis:
17935// Values(T v1, T v2, ..., T vN)
17936// - returns a generator producing sequences with elements v1, v2, ..., vN.
17937//
17938// For example, this instantiates tests from test case BarTest each
17939// with values "one", "two", and "three":
17940//
17941// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(NumSequence, BarTest, Values("one", "two", "three"));
17942//
17943// This instantiates tests from test case BazTest each with values 1, 2, 3.5.
17944// The exact type of values will depend on the type of parameter in BazTest.
17945//
17946// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(FloatingNumbers, BazTest, Values(1, 2, 3.5));
17947//
17948// Currently, Values() supports from 1 to 50 parameters.
17949//
17950template <typename T1>
17951internal::ValueArray1<T1> Values(T1 v1) {
17952 return internal::ValueArray1<T1>(v1);
17953}
17954
17955template <typename T1, typename T2>
17956internal::ValueArray2<T1, T2> Values(T1 v1, T2 v2) {
17957 return internal::ValueArray2<T1, T2>(v1, v2);
17958}
17959

17961internal::ValueArray3<T1, T2, T3> Values(T1 v1, T2 v2, T3 v3) {
17962 return internal::ValueArray3<T1, T2, T3>(v1, v2, v3);
17963}

17967 return internal::ValueArray4<T1, T2, T3, T4>(v1, v2, v3, v4);
17968}

17991template <typename T1, typename T2, typename T3, typename T4, typename T5,
17992 typename T6, typename T7, typename T8>
17993internal::ValueArray8<T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8> Values(T1 v1, T2 v2,

17999template <typename T1, typename T2, typename T3, typename T4, typename T5,
18000 typename T6, typename T7, typename T8, typename T9>

18803// Bool() allows generating tests with parameters in a set of (false, true).
18804//
18805// Synopsis:
18806// Bool()
18807// - returns a generator producing sequences with elements {false, true}.
18808//
18809// It is useful when testing code that depends on Boolean flags. Combinations
18810// of multiple flags can be tested when several Bool()'s are combined using
18811// Combine() function.
18812//
18813// In the following example all tests in the test case FlagDependentTest
18814// will be instantiated twice with parameters false and true.
18815//
18816// class FlagDependentTest : public testing::TestWithParam<bool> {
18817// virtual void SetUp() {
18818// external_flag = GetParam();
18819// }
18820// }
18821// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(BoolSequence, FlagDependentTest, Bool());
18822//
18823inline internal::ParamGenerator<bool> Bool() {
18824 return Values(false, true);
18825}
18826
18827# if GTEST_HAS_COMBINE
18828// Combine() allows the user to combine two or more sequences to produce
18829// values of a Cartesian product of those sequences' elements.
18830//
18831// Synopsis:
18832// Combine(gen1, gen2, ..., genN)
18833// - returns a generator producing sequences with elements coming from
18834// the Cartesian product of elements from the sequences generated by
18835// gen1, gen2, ..., genN. The sequence elements will have a type of
18836// tuple<T1, T2, ..., TN> where T1, T2, ..., TN are the types
18837// of elements from sequences produces by gen1, gen2, ..., genN.
18838//
18839// Combine can have up to 10 arguments. This number is currently limited
18840// by the maximum number of elements in the tuple implementation used by Google
18841// Test.
18842//
18843// Example:
18844//
18845// This will instantiate tests in test case AnimalTest each one with
18846// the parameter values tuple("cat", BLACK), tuple("cat", WHITE),
18847// tuple("dog", BLACK), and tuple("dog", WHITE):
18848//
18849// enum Color { BLACK, GRAY, WHITE };
18850// class AnimalTest
18851// : public testing::TestWithParam<tuple<const char*, Color> > {...};
18852//
18853// TEST_P(AnimalTest, AnimalLooksNice) {...}
18854//
18855// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(AnimalVariations, AnimalTest,
18856// Combine(Values("cat", "dog"),
18857// Values(BLACK, WHITE)));
18858//
18859// This will instantiate tests in FlagDependentTest with all variations of two
18860// Boolean flags:
18861//
18862// class FlagDependentTest
18863// : public testing::TestWithParam<tuple<bool, bool> > {
18864// virtual void SetUp() {
18865// // Assigns external_flag_1 and external_flag_2 values from the tuple.
18866// tie(external_flag_1, external_flag_2) = GetParam();
18867// }
18868// };
18869//
18870// TEST_P(FlagDependentTest, TestFeature1) {
18871// // Test your code using external_flag_1 and external_flag_2 here.
18872// }
18873// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(TwoBoolSequence, FlagDependentTest,
18874// Combine(Bool(), Bool()));
18875//
18876template <typename Generator1, typename Generator2>
18877internal::CartesianProductHolder2<Generator1, Generator2> Combine(
18878 const Generator1& g1, const Generator2& g2) {
18879 return internal::CartesianProductHolder2<Generator1, Generator2>(
18880 g1, g2);
18881}

18886 return internal::CartesianProductHolder3<Generator1, Generator2, Generator3>(
18887 g1, g2, g3);
18888}

18981# define TEST_P(test_case_name, test_name) \
18982 class GTEST_TEST_CLASS_NAME_(test_case_name, test_name) \
18983 : public test_case_name { \
18984 public: \
18985 GTEST_TEST_CLASS_NAME_(test_case_name, test_name)() {} \
18986 virtual void TestBody(); \
18987 private: \
18988 static int AddToRegistry() { \
18989 ::testing::UnitTest::GetInstance()->parameterized_test_registry(). \
18990 GetTestCasePatternHolder<test_case_name>(\
18991 #test_case_name, \
18992 ::testing::internal::CodeLocation(\
18993 __FILE__, __LINE__))->AddTestPattern(\
18994 GTEST_STRINGIFY_(test_case_name), \
18995 GTEST_STRINGIFY_(test_name), \
18996 new ::testing::internal::TestMetaFactory< \
18997 GTEST_TEST_CLASS_NAME_(\
18998 test_case_name, test_name)>()); \
18999 return 0; \
19000 } \
19001 static int gtest_registering_dummy_ GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_; \
19002 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(\
19003 GTEST_TEST_CLASS_NAME_(test_case_name, test_name)); \
19004 }; \
19005 int GTEST_TEST_CLASS_NAME_(test_case_name, \
19006 test_name)::gtest_registering_dummy_ = \
19007 GTEST_TEST_CLASS_NAME_(test_case_name, test_name)::AddToRegistry(); \
19008 void GTEST_TEST_CLASS_NAME_(test_case_name, test_name)::TestBody()
19009
19010// The optional last argument to INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P allows the user
19011// to specify a function or functor that generates custom test name suffixes
19012// based on the test parameters. The function should accept one argument of
19013// type testing::TestParamInfo<class ParamType>, and return std::string.
19014//
19015// testing::PrintToStringParamName is a builtin test suffix generator that
19016// returns the value of testing::PrintToString(GetParam()).
19017//
19018// Note: test names must be non-empty, unique, and may only contain ASCII
19019// alphanumeric characters or underscore. Because PrintToString adds quotes
19020// to std::string and C strings, it won't work for these types.
19021
19022# define INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(prefix, test_case_name, generator, ...) \
19023 static ::testing::internal::ParamGenerator<test_case_name::ParamType> \
19024 gtest_##prefix##test_case_name##_EvalGenerator_() { return generator; } \
19025 static ::std::string gtest_##prefix##test_case_name##_EvalGenerateName_( \
19026 const ::testing::TestParamInfo<test_case_name::ParamType>& info) { \
19027 return ::testing::internal::GetParamNameGen<test_case_name::ParamType> \
19028 (__VA_ARGS__)(info); \
19029 } \
19030 static int gtest_##prefix##test_case_name##_dummy_ GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_ = \
19031 ::testing::UnitTest::GetInstance()->parameterized_test_registry(). \
19032 GetTestCasePatternHolder<test_case_name>(\
19033 #test_case_name, \
19034 ::testing::internal::CodeLocation(\
19035 __FILE__, __LINE__))->AddTestCaseInstantiation(\
19036 #prefix, \
19037 &gtest_##prefix##test_case_name##_EvalGenerator_, \
19038 &gtest_##prefix##test_case_name##_EvalGenerateName_, \
19039 __FILE__, __LINE__)
19040

19080// When you need to test the private or protected members of a class,
19081// use the FRIEND_TEST macro to declare your tests as friends of the
19082// class. For example:
19083//
19084// class MyClass {
19085// private:
19086// void PrivateMethod();
19087// FRIEND_TEST(MyClassTest, PrivateMethodWorks);
19088// };
19089//
19090// class MyClassTest : public testing::Test {
19091// // ...
19092// };
19093//
19094// TEST_F(MyClassTest, PrivateMethodWorks) {
19095// // Can call MyClass::PrivateMethod() here.
19096// }
19097//
19098// Note: The test class must be in the same namespace as the class being tested.
19099// For example, putting MyClassTest in an anonymous namespace will not work.
19100
19101#define FRIEND_TEST(test_case_name, test_name)\
19102friend class test_case_name##_##test_name##_Test
19103

19145namespace testing {
19146
19147// A copyable object representing the result of a test part (i.e. an
19148// assertion or an explicit FAIL(), ADD_FAILURE(), or SUCCESS()).
19149//
19150// Don't inherit from TestPartResult as its destructor is not virtual.
19151class GTEST_API_ TestPartResult {
19152 public:
19153 // The possible outcomes of a test part (i.e. an assertion or an
19154 // explicit SUCCEED(), FAIL(), or ADD_FAILURE()).
19155 enum Type {
19156 kSuccess, // Succeeded.
19157 kNonFatalFailure, // Failed but the test can continue.
19158 kFatalFailure // Failed and the test should be terminated.
19159 };
19160
19161 // C'tor. TestPartResult does NOT have a default constructor.
19162 // Always use this constructor (with parameters) to create a
19163 // TestPartResult object.
19164 TestPartResult(Type a_type,
19165 const char* a_file_name,
19166 int a_line_number,
19167 const char* a_message)
19168 : type_(a_type),
19169 file_name_(a_file_name == NULL ? "" : a_file_name),
19170 line_number_(a_line_number),
19171 summary_(ExtractSummary(a_message)),
19172 message_(a_message) {
19173 }
19174
19175 // Gets the outcome of the test part.
19176 Type type() const { return type_; }
19177
19178 // Gets the name of the source file where the test part took place, or
19179 // NULL if it's unknown.
19180 const char* file_name() const {
19181 return file_name_.empty() ? NULL : file_name_.c_str();
19182 }
19183
19184 // Gets the line in the source file where the test part took place,
19185 // or -1 if it's unknown.
19186 int line_number() const { return line_number_; }
19187
19188 // Gets the summary of the failure message.
19189 const char* summary() const { return summary_.c_str(); }
19190
19191 // Gets the message associated with the test part.
19192 const char* message() const { return message_.c_str(); }
19193
19194 // Returns true iff the test part passed.
19195 bool passed() const { return type_ == kSuccess; }
19196
19197 // Returns true iff the test part failed.
19198 bool failed() const { return type_ != kSuccess; }
19199
19200 // Returns true iff the test part non-fatally failed.
19201 bool nonfatally_failed() const { return type_ == kNonFatalFailure; }
19202
19203 // Returns true iff the test part fatally failed.
19204 bool fatally_failed() const { return type_ == kFatalFailure; }
19205
19206 private:
19207 Type type_;
19208
19209 // Gets the summary of the failure message by omitting the stack
19210 // trace in it.
19211 static std::string ExtractSummary(const char* message);
19212
19213 // The name of the source file where the test part took place, or
19214 // "" if the source file is unknown.
19215 std::string file_name_;
19216 // The line in the source file where the test part took place, or -1
19217 // if the line number is unknown.
19218 int line_number_;
19219 std::string summary_; // The test failure summary.

19321// This header implements typed tests and type-parameterized tests.
19322
19323// Typed (aka type-driven) tests repeat the same test for types in a
19324// list. You must know which types you want to test with when writing
19325// typed tests. Here's how you do it:
19326
19327#if 0
19328
19329// First, define a fixture class template. It should be parameterized
19330// by a type. Remember to derive it from testing::Test.
19331template <typename T>
19332class FooTest : public testing::Test {
19333 public:
19334 ...
19335 typedef std::list<T> List;
19336 static T shared_;
19337 T value_;
19338};
19339
19340// Next, associate a list of types with the test case, which will be
19341// repeated for each type in the list. The typedef is necessary for
19342// the macro to parse correctly.
19343typedef testing::Types<char, int, unsigned int> MyTypes;
19344TYPED_TEST_CASE(FooTest, MyTypes);
19345
19346// If the type list contains only one type, you can write that type
19347// directly without Types<...>:
19348// TYPED_TEST_CASE(FooTest, int);
19349
19350// Then, use TYPED_TEST() instead of TEST_F() to define as many typed
19351// tests for this test case as you want.
19352TYPED_TEST(FooTest, DoesBlah) {
19353 // Inside a test, refer to TypeParam to get the type parameter.
19354 // Since we are inside a derived class template, C++ requires use to
19355 // visit the members of FooTest via 'this'.
19356 TypeParam n = this->value_;
19357
19358 // To visit static members of the fixture, add the TestFixture::
19359 // prefix.
19360 n += TestFixture::shared_;
19361
19362 // To refer to typedefs in the fixture, add the "typename
19363 // TestFixture::" prefix.
19364 typename TestFixture::List values;
19365 values.push_back(n);
19366 ...
19367}
19368
19369TYPED_TEST(FooTest, HasPropertyA) { ... }
19370
19371// TYPED_TEST_CASE takes an optional third argument which allows to specify a
19372// class that generates custom test name suffixes based on the type. This should
19373// be a class which has a static template function GetName(int index) returning
19374// a string for each type. The provided integer index equals the index of the
19375// type in the provided type list. In many cases the index can be ignored.
19376//
19377// For example:
19378// class MyTypeNames {
19379// public:
19380// template <typename T>
19381// static std::string GetName(int) {
19382// if (std::is_same<T, char>()) return "char";
19383// if (std::is_same<T, int>()) return "int";
19384// if (std::is_same<T, unsigned int>()) return "unsignedInt";
19385// }
19386// };
19387// TYPED_TEST_CASE(FooTest, MyTypes, MyTypeNames);
19388
19389#endif // 0
19390
19391// Type-parameterized tests are abstract test patterns parameterized
19392// by a type. Compared with typed tests, type-parameterized tests
19393// allow you to define the test pattern without knowing what the type
19394// parameters are. The defined pattern can be instantiated with
19395// different types any number of times, in any number of translation
19396// units.
19397//
19398// If you are designing an interface or concept, you can define a
19399// suite of type-parameterized tests to verify properties that any
19400// valid implementation of the interface/concept should have. Then,
19401// each implementation can easily instantiate the test suite to verify
19402// that it conforms to the requirements, without having to write
19403// similar tests repeatedly. Here's an example:
19404
19405#if 0
19406
19407// First, define a fixture class template. It should be parameterized
19408// by a type. Remember to derive it from testing::Test.
19409template <typename T>
19410class FooTest : public testing::Test {
19411 ...
19412};
19413
19414// Next, declare that you will define a type-parameterized test case
19415// (the _P suffix is for "parameterized" or "pattern", whichever you
19416// prefer):
19417TYPED_TEST_CASE_P(FooTest);
19418
19419// Then, use TYPED_TEST_P() to define as many type-parameterized tests
19420// for this type-parameterized test case as you want.
19421TYPED_TEST_P(FooTest, DoesBlah) {
19422 // Inside a test, refer to TypeParam to get the type parameter.
19423 TypeParam n = 0;
19424 ...
19425}
19426
19427TYPED_TEST_P(FooTest, HasPropertyA) { ... }
19428
19429// Now the tricky part: you need to register all test patterns before
19430// you can instantiate them. The first argument of the macro is the
19431// test case name; the rest are the names of the tests in this test
19432// case.
19433REGISTER_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P(FooTest,
19434 DoesBlah, HasPropertyA);
19435
19436// Finally, you are free to instantiate the pattern with the types you
19437// want. If you put the above code in a header file, you can #include
19438// it in multiple C++ source files and instantiate it multiple times.
19439//
19440// To distinguish different instances of the pattern, the first
19441// argument to the INSTANTIATE_* macro is a prefix that will be added
19442// to the actual test case name. Remember to pick unique prefixes for
19443// different instances.
19444typedef testing::Types<char, int, unsigned int> MyTypes;
19445INSTANTIATE_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P(My, FooTest, MyTypes);
19446
19447// If the type list contains only one type, you can write that type
19448// directly without Types<...>:
19449// INSTANTIATE_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P(My, FooTest, int);
19450//
19451// Similar to the optional argument of TYPED_TEST_CASE above,
19452// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P takes an optional fourth argument which allows to
19453// generate custom names.
19454// INSTANTIATE_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P(My, FooTest, MyTypes, MyTypeNames);
19455
19456#endif // 0
19457
19458
19459// Implements typed tests.
19460
19461#if GTEST_HAS_TYPED_TEST
19462
19463// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN USER CODE.
19464//
19465// Expands to the name of the typedef for the type parameters of the
19466// given test case.
19467# define GTEST_TYPE_PARAMS_(TestCaseName) gtest_type_params_##TestCaseName##_
19468
19469// Expands to the name of the typedef for the NameGenerator, responsible for
19470// creating the suffixes of the name.
19471#define GTEST_NAME_GENERATOR_(TestCaseName) \
19472 gtest_type_params_##TestCaseName##_NameGenerator
19473
19474// The 'Types' template argument below must have spaces around it
19475// since some compilers may choke on '>>' when passing a template
19476// instance (e.g. Types<int>)
19477# define TYPED_TEST_CASE(CaseName, Types, ...) \
19478 typedef ::testing::internal::TypeList< Types >::type GTEST_TYPE_PARAMS_( \
19479 CaseName); \
19480 typedef ::testing::internal::NameGeneratorSelector<__VA_ARGS__>::type \
19481 GTEST_NAME_GENERATOR_(CaseName)
19482
19483# define TYPED_TEST(CaseName, TestName) \
19484 template <typename gtest_TypeParam_> \
19485 class GTEST_TEST_CLASS_NAME_(CaseName, TestName) \
19486 : public CaseName<gtest_TypeParam_> { \
19487 private: \
19488 typedef CaseName<gtest_TypeParam_> TestFixture; \
19489 typedef gtest_TypeParam_ TypeParam; \
19490 virtual void TestBody(); \
19491 }; \
19492 static bool gtest_##CaseName##_##TestName##_registered_ \
19493 GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_ = \
19494 ::testing::internal::TypeParameterizedTest< \
19495 CaseName, \
19496 ::testing::internal::TemplateSel<GTEST_TEST_CLASS_NAME_(CaseName, \
19497 TestName)>, \
19498 GTEST_TYPE_PARAMS_( \
19499 CaseName)>::Register("", \
19500 ::testing::internal::CodeLocation( \
19501 __FILE__, __LINE__), \
19502 #CaseName, #TestName, 0, \
19503 ::testing::internal::GenerateNames< \
19504 GTEST_NAME_GENERATOR_(CaseName), \
19505 GTEST_TYPE_PARAMS_(CaseName)>()); \
19506 template <typename gtest_TypeParam_> \
19507 void GTEST_TEST_CLASS_NAME_(CaseName, \
19508 TestName)<gtest_TypeParam_>::TestBody()
19509
19510#endif // GTEST_HAS_TYPED_TEST
19511
19512// Implements type-parameterized tests.
19513
19514#if GTEST_HAS_TYPED_TEST_P
19515
19516// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN USER CODE.
19517//
19518// Expands to the namespace name that the type-parameterized tests for
19519// the given type-parameterized test case are defined in. The exact
19520// name of the namespace is subject to change without notice.
19521# define GTEST_CASE_NAMESPACE_(TestCaseName) \
19522 gtest_case_##TestCaseName##_
19523
19524// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN USER CODE.
19525//
19526// Expands to the name of the variable used to remember the names of
19527// the defined tests in the given test case.
19528# define GTEST_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P_STATE_(TestCaseName) \
19529 gtest_typed_test_case_p_state_##TestCaseName##_
19530
19531// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN USER CODE DIRECTLY.
19532//
19533// Expands to the name of the variable used to remember the names of
19534// the registered tests in the given test case.
19535# define GTEST_REGISTERED_TEST_NAMES_(TestCaseName) \
19536 gtest_registered_test_names_##TestCaseName##_
19537
19538// The variables defined in the type-parameterized test macros are
19539// static as typically these macros are used in a .h file that can be
19540// #included in multiple translation units linked together.
19541# define TYPED_TEST_CASE_P(CaseName) \
19542 static ::testing::internal::TypedTestCasePState \
19543 GTEST_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P_STATE_(CaseName)
19544
19545# define TYPED_TEST_P(CaseName, TestName) \
19546 namespace GTEST_CASE_NAMESPACE_(CaseName) { \
19547 template <typename gtest_TypeParam_> \
19548 class TestName : public CaseName<gtest_TypeParam_> { \
19549 private: \
19550 typedef CaseName<gtest_TypeParam_> TestFixture; \
19551 typedef gtest_TypeParam_ TypeParam; \
19552 virtual void TestBody(); \
19553 }; \
19554 static bool gtest_##TestName##_defined_ GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_ = \
19555 GTEST_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P_STATE_(CaseName).AddTestName(\
19556 __FILE__, __LINE__, #CaseName, #TestName); \
19557 } \
19558 template <typename gtest_TypeParam_> \
19559 void GTEST_CASE_NAMESPACE_(CaseName)::TestName<gtest_TypeParam_>::TestBody()
19560
19561# define REGISTER_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P(CaseName, ...) \
19562 namespace GTEST_CASE_NAMESPACE_(CaseName) { \
19563 typedef ::testing::internal::Templates<__VA_ARGS__>::type gtest_AllTests_; \
19564 } \
19565 static const char* const GTEST_REGISTERED_TEST_NAMES_(CaseName) \
19566 GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_ = \
19567 GTEST_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P_STATE_(CaseName).VerifyRegisteredTestNames( \
19568 __FILE__, __LINE__, #__VA_ARGS__)
19569
19570// The 'Types' template argument below must have spaces around it
19571// since some compilers may choke on '>>' when passing a template
19572// instance (e.g. Types<int>)
19573# define INSTANTIATE_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P(Prefix, CaseName, Types, ...) \
19574 static bool gtest_##Prefix##_##CaseName GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_ = \
19575 ::testing::internal::TypeParameterizedTestCase< \
19576 CaseName, GTEST_CASE_NAMESPACE_(CaseName)::gtest_AllTests_, \
19577 ::testing::internal::TypeList< Types >::type>:: \
19578 Register(#Prefix, \
19579 ::testing::internal::CodeLocation(__FILE__, __LINE__), \
19580 &GTEST_TYPED_TEST_CASE_P_STATE_(CaseName), #CaseName, \
19581 GTEST_REGISTERED_TEST_NAMES_(CaseName), \
19582 ::testing::internal::GenerateNames< \
19583 ::testing::internal::NameGeneratorSelector< \
19584 __VA_ARGS__>::type, \
19585 ::testing::internal::TypeList< Types >::type>())
19586
19587#endif // GTEST_HAS_TYPED_TEST_P
19588
19589#endif // GTEST_INCLUDE_GTEST_GTEST_TYPED_TEST_H_
