19727// A class for indicating whether an assertion was successful. When
19728// the assertion wasn't successful, the AssertionResult object
19729// remembers a non-empty message that describes how it failed.
19730//
19731// To create an instance of this class, use one of the factory functions
19732// (AssertionSuccess() and AssertionFailure()).
19733//
19734// This class is useful for two purposes:
19735// 1. Defining predicate functions to be used with Boolean test assertions
19736// EXPECT_TRUE/EXPECT_FALSE and their ASSERT_ counterparts
19737// 2. Defining predicate-format functions to be
19738// used with predicate assertions (ASSERT_PRED_FORMAT*, etc).
19739//
19740// For example, if you define IsEven predicate:
19741//
19742// testing::AssertionResult IsEven(int n) {
19743// if ((n % 2) == 0)
19744// return testing::AssertionSuccess();
19745// else
19746// return testing::AssertionFailure() << n << " is odd";
19747// }
19748//
19749// Then the failed expectation EXPECT_TRUE(IsEven(Fib(5)))
19750// will print the message
19751//
19752// Value of: IsEven(Fib(5))
19753// Actual: false (5 is odd)
19754// Expected: true
19755//
19756// instead of a more opaque
19757//
19758// Value of: IsEven(Fib(5))
19759// Actual: false
19760// Expected: true
19761//
19762// in case IsEven is a simple Boolean predicate.
19763//
19764// If you expect your predicate to be reused and want to support informative
19765// messages in EXPECT_FALSE and ASSERT_FALSE (negative assertions show up
19766// about half as often as positive ones in our tests), supply messages for
19767// both success and failure cases:
19768//
19769// testing::AssertionResult IsEven(int n) {
19770// if ((n % 2) == 0)
19771// return testing::AssertionSuccess() << n << " is even";
19772// else
19773// return testing::AssertionFailure() << n << " is odd";
19774// }
19775//
19776// Then a statement EXPECT_FALSE(IsEven(Fib(6))) will print
19777//
19778// Value of: IsEven(Fib(6))
19779// Actual: true (8 is even)
19780// Expected: false
19781//
19782// NB: Predicates that support negative Boolean assertions have reduced
19783// performance in positive ones so be careful not to use them in tests
19784// that have lots (tens of thousands) of positive Boolean assertions.
19785//
19786// To use this class with EXPECT_PRED_FORMAT assertions such as:
19787//
19788// // Verifies that Foo() returns an even number.
19789// EXPECT_PRED_FORMAT1(IsEven, Foo());
19790//
19791// you need to define:
19792//
19793// testing::AssertionResult IsEven(const char* expr, int n) {
19794// if ((n % 2) == 0)
19795// return testing::AssertionSuccess();
19796// else
19797// return testing::AssertionFailure()
19798// << "Expected: " << expr << " is even\n Actual: it's " << n;
19799// }
19800//
19801// If Foo() returns 5, you will see the following message:
19802//
19803// Expected: Foo() is even
19804// Actual: it's 5
19805//
19806class GTEST_API_ AssertionResult {
19807 public:
19808 // Copy constructor.
19809 // Used in EXPECT_TRUE/FALSE(assertion_result).
19810 AssertionResult(const AssertionResult& other);
19811
19812#if defined(_MSC_VER) && _MSC_VER < 1910
19813 GTEST_DISABLE_MSC_WARNINGS_PUSH_(4800 /* forcing value to bool */)
19814#endif
19815
19816 // Used in the EXPECT_TRUE/FALSE(bool_expression).
19817 //
19818 // T must be contextually convertible to bool.
19819 //
19820 // The second parameter prevents this overload from being considered if
19821 // the argument is implicitly convertible to AssertionResult. In that case
19822 // we want AssertionResult's copy constructor to be used.
19823 template <typename T>
19824 explicit AssertionResult(
19825 const T& success,
19826 typename internal::EnableIf<
19827 !internal::ImplicitlyConvertible<T, AssertionResult>::value>::type*
19828 /*enabler*/ = NULL)
19829 : success_(success) {}
19830
19831#if defined(_MSC_VER) && _MSC_VER < 1910
19832 GTEST_DISABLE_MSC_WARNINGS_POP_()
19833#endif
19834
19835 // Assignment operator.
19836 AssertionResult& operator=(AssertionResult other) {
19837 swap(other);
19838 return *this;
19839 }
19840
19841 // Returns true iff the assertion succeeded.
19842 operator bool() const { return success_; } // NOLINT
19843
19844 // Returns the assertion's negation. Used with EXPECT/ASSERT_FALSE.
19845 AssertionResult operator!() const;
19846
19847 // Returns the text streamed into this AssertionResult. Test assertions
19848 // use it when they fail (i.e., the predicate's outcome doesn't match the
19849 // assertion's expectation). When nothing has been streamed into the
19850 // object, returns an empty string.
19851 const char* message() const {
19852 return message_.get() != NULL ? message_->c_str() : "";
19853 }
19854 // FIXME: Remove this after making sure no clients use it.
19855 // Deprecated; please use message() instead.
19856 const char* failure_message() const { return message(); }
19857
19858 // Streams a custom failure message into this object.
19859 template <typename T> AssertionResult& operator<<(const T& value) {
19860 AppendMessage(Message() << value);
19861 return *this;
19862 }
19863
19864 // Allows streaming basic output manipulators such as endl or flush into
19865 // this object.
19866 AssertionResult& operator<<(
19867 ::std::ostream& (*basic_manipulator)(::std::ostream& stream)) {
19868 AppendMessage(Message() << basic_manipulator);
19869 return *this;
19870 }
19871
19872 private:
19873 // Appends the contents of message to message_.
19874 void AppendMessage(const Message& a_message) {
19875 if (message_.get() == NULL)
19876 message_.reset(new ::std::string);
19877 message_->append(a_message.GetString().c_str());
19878 }
19879
19880 // Swap the contents of this AssertionResult with other.
19881 void swap(AssertionResult& other);
19882
19883 // Stores result of the assertion predicate.
19884 bool success_;
19885 // Stores the message describing the condition in case the expectation
19886 // construct is not satisfied with the predicate's outcome.
19887 // Referenced via a pointer to avoid taking too much stack frame space
19888 // with test assertions.
19889 internal::scoped_ptr< ::std::string> message_;
19890};

20268// The abstract class that all tests inherit from.
20269//
20270// In Google Test, a unit test program contains one or many TestCases, and
20271// each TestCase contains one or many Tests.
20272//
20273// When you define a test using the TEST macro, you don't need to
20274// explicitly derive from Test - the TEST macro automatically does
20275// this for you.
20276//
20277// The only time you derive from Test is when defining a test fixture
20278// to be used in a TEST_F. For example:
20279//
20280// class FooTest : public testing::Test {
20281// protected:
20282// void SetUp() override { ... }
20283// void TearDown() override { ... }
20284// ...
20285// };
20286//
20287// TEST_F(FooTest, Bar) { ... }
20288// TEST_F(FooTest, Baz) { ... }
20289//
20290// Test is not copyable.
20291class GTEST_API_ Test {
20292 public:
20293 friend class TestInfo;
20294
20295 // Defines types for pointers to functions that set up and tear down
20296 // a test case.
20297 typedef internal::SetUpTestCaseFunc SetUpTestCaseFunc;
20298 typedef internal::TearDownTestCaseFunc TearDownTestCaseFunc;
20299
20300 // The d'tor is virtual as we intend to inherit from Test.
20301 virtual ~Test();
20302
20303 // Sets up the stuff shared by all tests in this test case.
20304 //
20305 // Google Test will call Foo::SetUpTestCase() before running the first
20306 // test in test case Foo. Hence a sub-class can define its own
20307 // SetUpTestCase() method to shadow the one defined in the super
20308 // class.
20309 static void SetUpTestCase() {}
20310
20311 // Tears down the stuff shared by all tests in this test case.
20312 //
20313 // Google Test will call Foo::TearDownTestCase() after running the last
20314 // test in test case Foo. Hence a sub-class can define its own
20315 // TearDownTestCase() method to shadow the one defined in the super
20316 // class.
20317 static void TearDownTestCase() {}
20318
20319 // Returns true iff the current test has a fatal failure.
20320 static bool HasFatalFailure();
20321
20322 // Returns true iff the current test has a non-fatal failure.
20323 static bool HasNonfatalFailure();
20324
20325 // Returns true iff the current test has a (either fatal or
20326 // non-fatal) failure.
20327 static bool HasFailure() { return HasFatalFailure() || HasNonfatalFailure(); }
20328
20329 // Logs a property for the current test, test case, or for the entire
20330 // invocation of the test program when used outside of the context of a
20331 // test case. Only the last value for a given key is remembered. These
20332 // are public static so they can be called from utility functions that are
20333 // not members of the test fixture. Calls to RecordProperty made during
20334 // lifespan of the test (from the moment its constructor starts to the
20335 // moment its destructor finishes) will be output in XML as attributes of
20336 // the <testcase> element. Properties recorded from fixture's
20337 // SetUpTestCase or TearDownTestCase are logged as attributes of the
20338 // corresponding <testsuite> element. Calls to RecordProperty made in the
20339 // global context (before or after invocation of RUN_ALL_TESTS and from
20340 // SetUp/TearDown method of Environment objects registered with Google
20341 // Test) will be output as attributes of the <testsuites> element.
20342 static void RecordProperty(const std::string& key, const std::string& value);
20343 static void RecordProperty(const std::string& key, int value);
20344
20345 protected:
20346 // Creates a Test object.
20347 Test();
20348
20349 // Sets up the test fixture.
20350 virtual void SetUp();
20351
20352 // Tears down the test fixture.
20353 virtual void TearDown();
20354
20355 private:
20356 // Returns true iff the current test has the same fixture class as
20357 // the first test in the current test case.
20358 static bool HasSameFixtureClass();
20359
20360 // Runs the test after the test fixture has been set up.
20361 //
20362 // A sub-class must implement this to define the test logic.
20363 //
20364 // DO NOT OVERRIDE THIS FUNCTION DIRECTLY IN A USER PROGRAM.
20365 // Instead, use the TEST or TEST_F macro.
20366 virtual void TestBody() = 0;
20367
20368 // Sets up, executes, and tears down the test.
20369 void Run();
20370
20371 // Deletes self. We deliberately pick an unusual name for this
20372 // internal method to avoid clashing with names used in user TESTs.
20373 void DeleteSelf_() { delete this; }
20374
20375 const internal::scoped_ptr< GTEST_FLAG_SAVER_ > gtest_flag_saver_;
20376
20377 // Often a user misspells SetUp() as Setup() and spends a long time
20378 // wondering why it is never called by Google Test. The declaration of
20379 // the following method is solely for catching such an error at
20380 // compile time:
20381 //
20382 // - The return type is deliberately chosen to be not void, so it
20383 // will be a conflict if void Setup() is declared in the user's
20384 // test fixture.
20385 //
20386 // - This method is private, so it will be another compiler error
20387 // if the method is called from the user's test fixture.
20388 //
20389 // DO NOT OVERRIDE THIS FUNCTION.
20390 //
20391 // If you see an error about overriding the following function or
20392 // about it being private, you have mis-spelled SetUp() as Setup().
20393 struct Setup_should_be_spelled_SetUp {};
20394 virtual Setup_should_be_spelled_SetUp* Setup() { return NULL; }
20395
20396 // We disallow copying Tests.
20397 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(Test);
20398};
20399
20400typedef internal::TimeInMillis TimeInMillis;
20401
20402// A copyable object representing a user specified test property which can be
20403// output as a key/value string pair.
20404//
20405// Don't inherit from TestProperty as its destructor is not virtual.
20406class TestProperty {
20407 public:
20408 // C'tor. TestProperty does NOT have a default constructor.
20409 // Always use this constructor (with parameters) to create a
20410 // TestProperty object.
20411 TestProperty(const std::string& a_key, const std::string& a_value) :
20412 key_(a_key), value_(a_value) {
20413 }
20414
20415 // Gets the user supplied key.
20416 const char* key() const {
20417 return key_.c_str();
20418 }
20419
20420 // Gets the user supplied value.
20421 const char* value() const {
20422 return value_.c_str();
20423 }
20424
20425 // Sets a new value, overriding the one supplied in the constructor.
20426 void SetValue(const std::string& new_value) {
20427 value_ = new_value;
20428 }
20429
20430 private:
20431 // The key supplied by the user.
20432 std::string key_;
20433 // The value supplied by the user.
20434 std::string value_;
20435};

20437// The result of a single Test. This includes a list of
20438// TestPartResults, a list of TestProperties, a count of how many
20439// death tests there are in the Test, and how much time it took to run
20440// the Test.
20441//
20442// TestResult is not copyable.
20443class GTEST_API_ TestResult {
20444 public:
20445 // Creates an empty TestResult.
20446 TestResult();
20447
20448 // D'tor. Do not inherit from TestResult.
20449 ~TestResult();
20450

20553// A TestInfo object stores the following information about a test:
20554//
20555// Test case name
20556// Test name
20557// Whether the test should be run
20558// A function pointer that creates the test object when invoked
20559// Test result
20560//
20561// The constructor of TestInfo registers itself with the UnitTest
20562// singleton such that the RUN_ALL_TESTS() macro knows which tests to
20563// run.
20564class GTEST_API_ TestInfo {
20565 public:
20566 // Destructs a TestInfo object. This function is not virtual, so
20567 // don't inherit from TestInfo.
20568 ~TestInfo();
20569
20570 // Returns the test case name.
20571 const char* test_case_name() const { return test_case_name_.c_str(); }
20572
20573 // Returns the test name.
20574 const char* name() const { return name_.c_str(); }
20575
20576 // Returns the name of the parameter type, or NULL if this is not a typed
20577 // or a type-parameterized test.
20578 const char* type_param() const {
20579 if (type_param_.get() != NULL)
20580 return type_param_->c_str();
20581 return NULL;
20582 }
20583
20584 // Returns the text representation of the value parameter, or NULL if this
20585 // is not a value-parameterized test.
20586 const char* value_param() const {
20587 if (value_param_.get() != NULL)
20588 return value_param_->c_str();
20589 return NULL;
20590 }
20591
20592 // Returns the file name where this test is defined.
20593 const char* file() const { return location_.file.c_str(); }
20594
20595 // Returns the line where this test is defined.
20596 int line() const { return location_.line; }
20597
20598 // Return true if this test should not be run because it's in another shard.
20599 bool is_in_another_shard() const { return is_in_another_shard_; }
20600
20601 // Returns true if this test should run, that is if the test is not
20602 // disabled (or it is disabled but the also_run_disabled_tests flag has
20603 // been specified) and its full name matches the user-specified filter.
20604 //
20605 // Google Test allows the user to filter the tests by their full names.
20606 // The full name of a test Bar in test case Foo is defined as
20607 // "Foo.Bar". Only the tests that match the filter will run.
20608 //
20609 // A filter is a colon-separated list of glob (not regex) patterns,
20610 // optionally followed by a '-' and a colon-separated list of
20611 // negative patterns (tests to exclude). A test is run if it
20612 // matches one of the positive patterns and does not match any of
20613 // the negative patterns.
20614 //
20615 // For example, *A*:Foo.* is a filter that matches any string that
20616 // contains the character 'A' or starts with "Foo.".
20617 bool should_run() const { return should_run_; }
20618
20619 // Returns true iff this test will appear in the XML report.
20620 bool is_reportable() const {
20621 // The XML report includes tests matching the filter, excluding those
20622 // run in other shards.
20623 return matches_filter_ && !is_in_another_shard_;
20624 }
20625
20626 // Returns the result of the test.
20627 const TestResult* result() const { return &result_; }
20628
20629 private:
20630#if GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
20631 friend class internal::DefaultDeathTestFactory;
20632#endif // GTEST_HAS_DEATH_TEST
20633 friend class Test;
20634 friend class TestCase;
20635 friend class internal::UnitTestImpl;
20636 friend class internal::StreamingListenerTest;
20637 friend TestInfo* internal::MakeAndRegisterTestInfo(
20638 const char* test_case_name,
20639 const char* name,
20640 const char* type_param,
20641 const char* value_param,
20642 internal::CodeLocation code_location,
20643 internal::TypeId fixture_class_id,
20644 Test::SetUpTestCaseFunc set_up_tc,
20645 Test::TearDownTestCaseFunc tear_down_tc,
20646 internal::TestFactoryBase* factory);
20647
20648 // Constructs a TestInfo object. The newly constructed instance assumes
20649 // ownership of the factory object.
20650 TestInfo(const std::string& test_case_name,
20651 const std::string& name,
20652 const char* a_type_param, // NULL if not a type-parameterized test
20653 const char* a_value_param, // NULL if not a value-parameterized test
20654 internal::CodeLocation a_code_location,
20655 internal::TypeId fixture_class_id,
20656 internal::TestFactoryBase* factory);
20657
20658 // Increments the number of death tests encountered in this test so
20659 // far.
20660 int increment_death_test_count() {
20661 return result_.increment_death_test_count();
20662 }
20663
20664 // Creates the test object, runs it, records its result, and then
20665 // deletes it.
20666 void Run();
20667
20668 static void ClearTestResult(TestInfo* test_info) {
20669 test_info->result_.Clear();
20670 }
20671
20672 // These fields are immutable properties of the test.
20673 const std::string test_case_name_; // Test case name
20674 const std::string name_; // Test name
20675 // Name of the parameter type, or NULL if this is not a typed or a
20676 // type-parameterized test.
20677 const internal::scoped_ptr<const ::std::string> type_param_;
20678 // Text representation of the value parameter, or NULL if this is not a
20679 // value-parameterized test.
20680 const internal::scoped_ptr<const ::std::string> value_param_;
20681 internal::CodeLocation location_;
20682 const internal::TypeId fixture_class_id_; // ID of the test fixture class
20683 bool should_run_; // True iff this test should run
20684 bool is_disabled_; // True iff this test is disabled
20685 bool matches_filter_; // True if this test matches the
20686 // user-specified filter.
20687 bool is_in_another_shard_; // Will be run in another shard.
20688 internal::TestFactoryBase* const factory_; // The factory that creates
20689 // the test object
20690
20691 // This field is mutable and needs to be reset before running the
20692 // test for the second time.
20693 TestResult result_;
20694
20695 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(TestInfo);
20696};

20698// A test case, which consists of a vector of TestInfos.
20699//
20700// TestCase is not copyable.
20701class GTEST_API_ TestCase {
20702 public:
20703 // Creates a TestCase with the given name.
20704 //
20705 // TestCase does NOT have a default constructor. Always use this
20706 // constructor to create a TestCase object.
20707 //
20708 // Arguments:
20709 //
20710 // name: name of the test case
20711 // a_type_param: the name of the test's type parameter, or NULL if
20712 // this is not a type-parameterized test.
20713 // set_up_tc: pointer to the function that sets up the test case
20714 // tear_down_tc: pointer to the function that tears down the test case
20715 TestCase(const char* name, const char* a_type_param,
20716 Test::SetUpTestCaseFunc set_up_tc,
20717 Test::TearDownTestCaseFunc tear_down_tc);
20718
20719 // Destructor of TestCase.
20720 virtual ~TestCase();
20721
20722 // Gets the name of the TestCase.
20723 const char* name() const { return name_.c_str(); }
20724
20725 // Returns the name of the parameter type, or NULL if this is not a
20726 // type-parameterized test case.
20727 const char* type_param() const {
20728 if (type_param_.get() != NULL)
20729 return type_param_->c_str();
20730 return NULL;
20731 }
20732
20733 // Returns true if any test in this test case should run.
20734 bool should_run() const { return should_run_; }
20735
20736 // Gets the number of successful tests in this test case.
20737 int successful_test_count() const;
20738
20739 // Gets the number of failed tests in this test case.
20740 int failed_test_count() const;
20741
20742 // Gets the number of disabled tests that will be reported in the XML report.
20743 int reportable_disabled_test_count() const;
20744
20745 // Gets the number of disabled tests in this test case.
20746 int disabled_test_count() const;
20747
20748 // Gets the number of tests to be printed in the XML report.
20749 int reportable_test_count() const;
20750
20751 // Get the number of tests in this test case that should run.
20752 int test_to_run_count() const;
20753
20754 // Gets the number of all tests in this test case.
20755 int total_test_count() const;
20756
20757 // Returns true iff the test case passed.
20758 bool Passed() const { return !Failed(); }
20759
20760 // Returns true iff the test case failed.
20761 bool Failed() const { return failed_test_count() > 0; }
20762
20763 // Returns the elapsed time, in milliseconds.
20764 TimeInMillis elapsed_time() const { return elapsed_time_; }
20765
20766 // Returns the i-th test among all the tests. i can range from 0 to
20767 // total_test_count() - 1. If i is not in that range, returns NULL.
20768 const TestInfo* GetTestInfo(int i) const;
20769
20770 // Returns the TestResult that holds test properties recorded during
20771 // execution of SetUpTestCase and TearDownTestCase.
20772 const TestResult& ad_hoc_test_result() const { return ad_hoc_test_result_; }
20773
20774 private:
20775 friend class Test;
20776 friend class internal::UnitTestImpl;
20777
20778 // Gets the (mutable) vector of TestInfos in this TestCase.
20779 std::vector<TestInfo*>& test_info_list() { return test_info_list_; }
20780
20781 // Gets the (immutable) vector of TestInfos in this TestCase.
20782 const std::vector<TestInfo*>& test_info_list() const {
20783 return test_info_list_;
20784 }
20785
20786 // Returns the i-th test among all the tests. i can range from 0 to
20787 // total_test_count() - 1. If i is not in that range, returns NULL.
20788 TestInfo* GetMutableTestInfo(int i);
20789
20790 // Sets the should_run member.
20791 void set_should_run(bool should) { should_run_ = should; }
20792
20793 // Adds a TestInfo to this test case. Will delete the TestInfo upon
20794 // destruction of the TestCase object.
20795 void AddTestInfo(TestInfo * test_info);
20796
20797 // Clears the results of all tests in this test case.
20798 void ClearResult();
20799
20800 // Clears the results of all tests in the given test case.
20801 static void ClearTestCaseResult(TestCase* test_case) {
20802 test_case->ClearResult();
20803 }
20804
20805 // Runs every test in this TestCase.
20806 void Run();
20807
20808 // Runs SetUpTestCase() for this TestCase. This wrapper is needed
20809 // for catching exceptions thrown from SetUpTestCase().
20810 void RunSetUpTestCase() { (*set_up_tc_)(); }
20811
20812 // Runs TearDownTestCase() for this TestCase. This wrapper is
20813 // needed for catching exceptions thrown from TearDownTestCase().
20814 void RunTearDownTestCase() { (*tear_down_tc_)(); }
20815
20816 // Returns true iff test passed.
20817 static bool TestPassed(const TestInfo* test_info) {
20818 return test_info->should_run() && test_info->result()->Passed();
20819 }
20820
20821 // Returns true iff test failed.
20822 static bool TestFailed(const TestInfo* test_info) {
20823 return test_info->should_run() && test_info->result()->Failed();
20824 }
20825
20826 // Returns true iff the test is disabled and will be reported in the XML
20827 // report.
20828 static bool TestReportableDisabled(const TestInfo* test_info) {
20829 return test_info->is_reportable() && test_info->is_disabled_;
20830 }
20831
20832 // Returns true iff test is disabled.
20833 static bool TestDisabled(const TestInfo* test_info) {
20834 return test_info->is_disabled_;
20835 }
20836
20837 // Returns true iff this test will appear in the XML report.
20838 static bool TestReportable(const TestInfo* test_info) {
20839 return test_info->is_reportable();
20840 }
20841
20842 // Returns true if the given test should run.
20843 static bool ShouldRunTest(const TestInfo* test_info) {
20844 return test_info->should_run();
20845 }
20846
20847 // Shuffles the tests in this test case.
20848 void ShuffleTests(internal::Random* random);
20849
20850 // Restores the test order to before the first shuffle.
20851 void UnshuffleTests();
20852
20853 // Name of the test case.
20854 std::string name_;
20855 // Name of the parameter type, or NULL if this is not a typed or a
20856 // type-parameterized test.
20857 const internal::scoped_ptr<const ::std::string> type_param_;
20858 // The vector of TestInfos in their original order. It owns the
20859 // elements in the vector.
20860 std::vector<TestInfo*> test_info_list_;
20861 // Provides a level of indirection for the test list to allow easy
20862 // shuffling and restoring the test order. The i-th element in this
20863 // vector is the index of the i-th test in the shuffled test list.
20864 std::vector<int> test_indices_;
20865 // Pointer to the function that sets up the test case.
20866 Test::SetUpTestCaseFunc set_up_tc_;
20867 // Pointer to the function that tears down the test case.
20868 Test::TearDownTestCaseFunc tear_down_tc_;
20869 // True iff any test in this test case should run.
20870 bool should_run_;
20871 // Elapsed time, in milliseconds.
20872 TimeInMillis elapsed_time_;
20873 // Holds test properties recorded during execution of SetUpTestCase and
20874 // TearDownTestCase.
20875 TestResult ad_hoc_test_result_;
20876
20877 // We disallow copying TestCases.
20878 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(TestCase);
20879};

20881// An Environment object is capable of setting up and tearing down an
20882// environment. You should subclass this to define your own
20883// environment(s).
20884//
20885// An Environment object does the set-up and tear-down in virtual
20886// methods SetUp() and TearDown() instead of the constructor and the
20887// destructor, as:
20888//
20889// 1. You cannot safely throw from a destructor. This is a problem
20890// as in some cases Google Test is used where exceptions are enabled, and
20891// we may want to implement ASSERT_* using exceptions where they are
20892// available.
20893// 2. You cannot use ASSERT_* directly in a constructor or
20894// destructor.
20895class Environment {
20896 public:
20897 // The d'tor is virtual as we need to subclass Environment.
20898 virtual ~Environment() {}
20899
20900 // Override this to define how to set up the environment.
20901 virtual void SetUp() {}
20902
20903 // Override this to define how to tear down the environment.
20904 virtual void TearDown() {}
20905 private:
20906 // If you see an error about overriding the following function or
20907 // about it being private, you have mis-spelled SetUp() as Setup().
20908 struct Setup_should_be_spelled_SetUp {};
20909 virtual Setup_should_be_spelled_SetUp* Setup() { return NULL; }
20910};

20918 explicit AssertionException(const TestPartResult& result)
20919 : GoogleTestFailureException(result) {}

20924// The interface for tracing execution of tests. The methods are organized in
20925// the order the corresponding events are fired.
20926class TestEventListener {
20927 public:
20928 virtual ~TestEventListener() {}
20929
20930 // Fired before any test activity starts.
20931 virtual void OnTestProgramStart(const UnitTest& unit_test) = 0;
20932
20933 // Fired before each iteration of tests starts. There may be more than
20934 // one iteration if GTEST_FLAG(repeat) is set. iteration is the iteration
20935 // index, starting from 0.
20936 virtual void OnTestIterationStart(const UnitTest& unit_test,
20937 int iteration) = 0;
20938
20939 // Fired before environment set-up for each iteration of tests starts.
20940 virtual void OnEnvironmentsSetUpStart(const UnitTest& unit_test) = 0;
20941
20942 // Fired after environment set-up for each iteration of tests ends.
20943 virtual void OnEnvironmentsSetUpEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test) = 0;
20944
20945 // Fired before the test case starts.
20946 virtual void OnTestCaseStart(const TestCase& test_case) = 0;
20947
20948 // Fired before the test starts.
20949 virtual void OnTestStart(const TestInfo& test_info) = 0;
20950
20951 // Fired after a failed assertion or a SUCCEED() invocation.
20952 // If you want to throw an exception from this function to skip to the next
20953 // TEST, it must be AssertionException defined above, or inherited from it.
20954 virtual void OnTestPartResult(const TestPartResult& test_part_result) = 0;
20955
20956 // Fired after the test ends.
20957 virtual void OnTestEnd(const TestInfo& test_info) = 0;
20958
20959 // Fired after the test case ends.
20960 virtual void OnTestCaseEnd(const TestCase& test_case) = 0;
20961
20962 // Fired before environment tear-down for each iteration of tests starts.
20963 virtual void OnEnvironmentsTearDownStart(const UnitTest& unit_test) = 0;
20964
20965 // Fired after environment tear-down for each iteration of tests ends.
20966 virtual void OnEnvironmentsTearDownEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test) = 0;
20967
20968 // Fired after each iteration of tests finishes.
20969 virtual void OnTestIterationEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test,
20970 int iteration) = 0;
20971
20972 // Fired after all test activities have ended.
20973 virtual void OnTestProgramEnd(const UnitTest& unit_test) = 0;
20974};
20975
20976// The convenience class for users who need to override just one or two
20977// methods and are not concerned that a possible change to a signature of
20978// the methods they override will not be caught during the build. For
20979// comments about each method please see the definition of TestEventListener
20980// above.
20981class EmptyTestEventListener : public TestEventListener {
20982 public:
20983 virtual void OnTestProgramStart(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {}
20984 virtual void OnTestIterationStart(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/,
20985 int /*iteration*/) {}
20986 virtual void OnEnvironmentsSetUpStart(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {}
20987 virtual void OnEnvironmentsSetUpEnd(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {}
20988 virtual void OnTestCaseStart(const TestCase& /*test_case*/) {}
20989 virtual void OnTestStart(const TestInfo& /*test_info*/) {}
20990 virtual void OnTestPartResult(const TestPartResult& /*test_part_result*/) {}
20991 virtual void OnTestEnd(const TestInfo& /*test_info*/) {}
20992 virtual void OnTestCaseEnd(const TestCase& /*test_case*/) {}
20993 virtual void OnEnvironmentsTearDownStart(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {}
20994 virtual void OnEnvironmentsTearDownEnd(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {}
20995 virtual void OnTestIterationEnd(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/,
20996 int /*iteration*/) {}
20997 virtual void OnTestProgramEnd(const UnitTest& /*unit_test*/) {}
20998};

21000// TestEventListeners lets users add listeners to track events in Google Test.
21001class GTEST_API_ TestEventListeners {
21002 public:
21003 TestEventListeners();
21004 ~TestEventListeners();
21005
21006 // Appends an event listener to the end of the list. Google Test assumes
21007 // the ownership of the listener (i.e. it will delete the listener when
21008 // the test program finishes).
21009 void Append(TestEventListener* listener);
21010
21011 // Removes the given event listener from the list and returns it. It then
21012 // becomes the caller's responsibility to delete the listener. Returns
21013 // NULL if the listener is not found in the list.
21014 TestEventListener* Release(TestEventListener* listener);
21015
21016 // Returns the standard listener responsible for the default console
21017 // output. Can be removed from the listeners list to shut down default
21018 // console output. Note that removing this object from the listener list
21019 // with Release transfers its ownership to the caller and makes this
21020 // function return NULL the next time.
21021 TestEventListener* default_result_printer() const {
21022 return default_result_printer_;
21023 }
21024
21025 // Returns the standard listener responsible for the default XML output
21026 // controlled by the --gtest_output=xml flag. Can be removed from the
21027 // listeners list by users who want to shut down the default XML output
21028 // controlled by this flag and substitute it with custom one. Note that
21029 // removing this object from the listener list with Release transfers its
21030 // ownership to the caller and makes this function return NULL the next
21031 // time.
21032 TestEventListener* default_xml_generator() const {
21033 return default_xml_generator_;
21034 }
21035
21036 private:
21037 friend class TestCase;
21038 friend class TestInfo;
21039 friend class internal::DefaultGlobalTestPartResultReporter;
21040 friend class internal::NoExecDeathTest;
21041 friend class internal::TestEventListenersAccessor;
21042 friend class internal::UnitTestImpl;
21043
21044 // Returns repeater that broadcasts the TestEventListener events to all
21045 // subscribers.
21046 TestEventListener* repeater();
21047
21048 // Sets the default_result_printer attribute to the provided listener.
21049 // The listener is also added to the listener list and previous
21050 // default_result_printer is removed from it and deleted. The listener can
21051 // also be NULL in which case it will not be added to the list. Does
21052 // nothing if the previous and the current listener objects are the same.
21053 void SetDefaultResultPrinter(TestEventListener* listener);
21054
21055 // Sets the default_xml_generator attribute to the provided listener. The
21056 // listener is also added to the listener list and previous
21057 // default_xml_generator is removed from it and deleted. The listener can
21058 // also be NULL in which case it will not be added to the list. Does
21059 // nothing if the previous and the current listener objects are the same.
21060 void SetDefaultXmlGenerator(TestEventListener* listener);
21061
21062 // Controls whether events will be forwarded by the repeater to the
21063 // listeners in the list.
21064 bool EventForwardingEnabled() const;
21065 void SuppressEventForwarding();
21066
21067 // The actual list of listeners.
21068 internal::TestEventRepeater* repeater_;
21069 // Listener responsible for the standard result output.
21070 TestEventListener* default_result_printer_;
21071 // Listener responsible for the creation of the XML output file.
21072 TestEventListener* default_xml_generator_;
21073
21074 // We disallow copying TestEventListeners.
21075 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(TestEventListeners);
21076};

21078// A UnitTest consists of a vector of TestCases.
21079//
21080// This is a singleton class. The only instance of UnitTest is
21081// created when UnitTest::GetInstance() is first called. This
21082// instance is never deleted.
21083//
21084// UnitTest is not copyable.
21085//
21086// This class is thread-safe as long as the methods are called
21087// according to their specification.
21088class GTEST_API_ UnitTest {
21089 public:

21190 // the order they were registered. After all tests in the program
21191 // have finished, all global test environments will be torn-down in
21192 // the *reverse* order they were registered.

21194 // The UnitTest object takes ownership of the given environment.

21249 // Pops a trace from the per-thread Google Test trace stack.

21252

21254 // methods need to lock it too.
21255 mutable internal::Mutex mutex_;
21256

21258 // the object is constructed. We don't mark it as const here, as
21259 // doing so will cause a warning in the constructor of UnitTest.

21261 internal::UnitTestImpl* impl_;

21264 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(UnitTest);

21267// A convenient wrapper for adding an environment for the test
21268// program.
21269//
21270// You should call this before RUN_ALL_TESTS() is called, probably in
21271// main(). If you use gtest_main, you need to call this before main()
21272// starts for it to take effect. For example, you can define a global
21273// variable like this:
21274//
21275// testing::Environment* const foo_env =
21276// testing::AddGlobalTestEnvironment(new FooEnvironment);
21277//
21278// However, we strongly recommend you to write your own main() and
21279// call AddGlobalTestEnvironment() there, as relying on initialization
21280// of global variables makes the code harder to read and may cause
21281// problems when you register multiple environments from different
21282// translation units and the environments have dependencies among them
21283// (remember that the compiler doesn't guarantee the order in which
21284// global variables from different translation units are initialized).
21285inline Environment* AddGlobalTestEnvironment(Environment* env) {
21286 return UnitTest::GetInstance()->AddEnvironment(env);
21287}

21289// Initializes Google Test. This must be called before calling
21290// RUN_ALL_TESTS(). In particular, it parses a command line for the
21291// flags that Google Test recognizes. Whenever a Google Test flag is
21292// seen, it is removed from argv, and *argc is decremented.
21293//
21294// No value is returned. Instead, the Google Test flag variables are
21295// updated.
21296//
21297// Calling the function for the second time has no user-visible effect.
21298GTEST_API_ void InitGoogleTest(int* argc, char** argv);

21300// This overloaded version can be used in Windows programs compiled in
21301// UNICODE mode.
21302GTEST_API_ void InitGoogleTest(int* argc, wchar_t** argv);

21306// Separate the error generating code from the code path to reduce the stack
21307// frame size of CmpHelperEQ. This helps reduce the overhead of some sanitizers
21308// when calling EXPECT_* in a tight loop.
21309template <typename T1, typename T2>
21310AssertionResult CmpHelperEQFailure(const char* lhs_expression,
21311 const char* rhs_expression,
21312 const T1& lhs, const T2& rhs) {
21313 return EqFailure(lhs_expression,
21314 rhs_expression,
21315 FormatForComparisonFailureMessage(lhs, rhs),
21316 FormatForComparisonFailureMessage(rhs, lhs),
21317 false);
21318}

21322#if defined(__GNUC__) && (__GNUC__ == 14)
21323#pragma GCC push_options
21324#pragma GCC optimize ("O0")
21325#endif

21327// The helper function for {ASSERT|EXPECT}_EQ.
21328template <typename T1, typename T2>
21329AssertionResult CmpHelperEQ(const char* lhs_expression,
21330 const char* rhs_expression,
21331 const T1& lhs,
21332 const T2& rhs) {
21333 if (lhs == rhs) {
21334 return AssertionSuccess();
21335 }
21336
21337 return CmpHelperEQFailure(lhs_expression, rhs_expression, lhs, rhs);
21338}
21339
21340#if defined(__GNUC__) && (__GNUC__ == 14)
21341#pragma GCC pop_options
21342#endif

21344// With this overloaded version, we allow anonymous enums to be used
21345// in {ASSERT|EXPECT}_EQ when compiled with gcc 4, as anonymous enums
21346// can be implicitly cast to BiggestInt.
21347GTEST_API_ AssertionResult CmpHelperEQ(const char* lhs_expression,
21348 const char* rhs_expression,
21349 BiggestInt lhs,
21350 BiggestInt rhs);
21351
21352// The helper class for {ASSERT|EXPECT}_EQ. The template argument
21353// lhs_is_null_literal is true iff the first argument to ASSERT_EQ()
21354// is a null pointer literal. The following default implementation is
21355// for lhs_is_null_literal being false.
21356template <bool lhs_is_null_literal>
21357class EqHelper {
21358 public:
21359 // This templatized version is for the general case.
21360 template <typename T1, typename T2>
21361 static AssertionResult Compare(const char* lhs_expression,
21362 const char* rhs_expression,
21363 const T1& lhs,
21364 const T2& rhs) {
21365 return CmpHelperEQ(lhs_expression, rhs_expression, lhs, rhs);
21366 }
21367
21368 // With this overloaded version, we allow anonymous enums to be used
21369 // in {ASSERT|EXPECT}_EQ when compiled with gcc 4, as anonymous
21370 // enums can be implicitly cast to BiggestInt.
21371 //
21372 // Even though its body looks the same as the above version, we
21373 // cannot merge the two, as it will make anonymous enums unhappy.
21374 static AssertionResult Compare(const char* lhs_expression,
21375 const char* rhs_expression,
21376 BiggestInt lhs,
21377 BiggestInt rhs) {
21378 return CmpHelperEQ(lhs_expression, rhs_expression, lhs, rhs);
21379 }
21380};
21381
21382// This specialization is used when the first argument to ASSERT_EQ()
21383// is a null pointer literal, like NULL, false, or 0.
21384template <>
21385class EqHelper<true> {
21386 public:
21387 // We define two overloaded versions of Compare(). The first
21388 // version will be picked when the second argument to ASSERT_EQ() is
21389 // NOT a pointer, e.g. ASSERT_EQ(0, AnIntFunction()) or
21390 // EXPECT_EQ(false, a_bool).
21391 template <typename T1, typename T2>
21392 static AssertionResult Compare(
21393 const char* lhs_expression,
21394 const char* rhs_expression,
21395 const T1& lhs,
21396 const T2& rhs,
21397 // The following line prevents this overload from being considered if T2
21398 // is not a pointer type. We need this because ASSERT_EQ(NULL, my_ptr)
21399 // expands to Compare("", "", NULL, my_ptr), which requires a conversion
21400 // to match the Secret* in the other overload, which would otherwise make
21401 // this template match better.
21402 typename EnableIf<!is_pointer<T2>::value>::type* = 0) {
21403 return CmpHelperEQ(lhs_expression, rhs_expression, lhs, rhs);
21404 }
21405
21406 // This version will be picked when the second argument to ASSERT_EQ() is a
21407 // pointer, e.g. ASSERT_EQ(NULL, a_pointer).
21408 template <typename T>
21409 static AssertionResult Compare(
21410 const char* lhs_expression,
21411 const char* rhs_expression,
21412 // We used to have a second template parameter instead of Secret*. That
21413 // template parameter would deduce to 'long', making this a better match
21414 // than the first overload even without the first overload's EnableIf.
21415 // Unfortunately, gcc with -Wconversion-null warns when "passing NULL to
21416 // non-pointer argument" (even a deduced integral argument), so the old
21417 // implementation caused warnings in user code.
21418 Secret* /* lhs (NULL) */,
21419 T* rhs) {
21420 // We already know that 'lhs' is a null pointer.
21421 return CmpHelperEQ(lhs_expression, rhs_expression,
21422 static_cast<T*>(NULL), rhs);
21423 }
21424};

21426// Separate the error generating code from the code path to reduce the stack
21427// frame size of CmpHelperOP. This helps reduce the overhead of some sanitizers
21428// when calling EXPECT_OP in a tight loop.
21429template <typename T1, typename T2>
21430AssertionResult CmpHelperOpFailure(const char* expr1, const char* expr2,
21431 const T1& val1, const T2& val2,
21432 const char* op) {
21433 return AssertionFailure()
21434 << "Expected: (" << expr1 << ") " << op << " (" << expr2
21435 << "), actual: " << FormatForComparisonFailureMessage(val1, val2)
21436 << " vs " << FormatForComparisonFailureMessage(val2, val1);
21437}

21439// A macro for implementing the helper functions needed to implement
21440// ASSERT_?? and EXPECT_??. It is here just to avoid copy-and-paste
21441// of similar code.
21442//
21443// For each templatized helper function, we also define an overloaded
21444// version for BiggestInt in order to reduce code bloat and allow
21445// anonymous enums to be used with {ASSERT|EXPECT}_?? when compiled
21446// with gcc 4.
21447//
21448// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN A USER PROGRAM.
21449
21450#define GTEST_IMPL_CMP_HELPER_(op_name, op)\
21451template <typename T1, typename T2>\
21452AssertionResult CmpHelper##op_name(const char* expr1, const char* expr2, \
21453 const T1& val1, const T2& val2) {\
21454 if (val1 op val2) {\
21455 return AssertionSuccess();\
21456 } else {\
21457 return CmpHelperOpFailure(expr1, expr2, val1, val2, #op);\
21458 }\
21459}\
21460GTEST_API_ AssertionResult CmpHelper##op_name(\
21461 const char* expr1, const char* expr2, BiggestInt val1, BiggestInt val2)
21462
21463// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN A USER PROGRAM.
21464
21465// Implements the helper function for {ASSERT|EXPECT}_NE
21466GTEST_IMPL_CMP_HELPER_(NE, !=);
21467// Implements the helper function for {ASSERT|EXPECT}_LE
21468GTEST_IMPL_CMP_HELPER_(LE, <=);
21469// Implements the helper function for {ASSERT|EXPECT}_LT
21470GTEST_IMPL_CMP_HELPER_(LT, <);
21471// Implements the helper function for {ASSERT|EXPECT}_GE
21472GTEST_IMPL_CMP_HELPER_(GE, >=);
21473// Implements the helper function for {ASSERT|EXPECT}_GT
21474GTEST_IMPL_CMP_HELPER_(GT, >);
21475
21476#undef GTEST_IMPL_CMP_HELPER_
21477

21567// Helper template function for comparing floating-points.
21568//
21569// Template parameter:
21570//
21571// RawType: the raw floating-point type (either float or double)
21572//
21573// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN A USER PROGRAM.
21574template <typename RawType>
21575AssertionResult CmpHelperFloatingPointEQ(const char* lhs_expression,
21576 const char* rhs_expression,
21577 RawType lhs_value,
21578 RawType rhs_value) {
21579 const FloatingPoint<RawType> lhs(lhs_value), rhs(rhs_value);
21580
21581 if (lhs.AlmostEquals(rhs)) {
21582 return AssertionSuccess();
21583 }
21584
21585 ::std::stringstream lhs_ss;
21586 lhs_ss << std::setprecision(std::numeric_limits<RawType>::digits10 + 2)
21587 << lhs_value;
21588
21589 ::std::stringstream rhs_ss;
21590 rhs_ss << std::setprecision(std::numeric_limits<RawType>::digits10 + 2)
21591 << rhs_value;
21592
21593 return EqFailure(lhs_expression,
21594 rhs_expression,
21595 StringStreamToString(&lhs_ss),
21596 StringStreamToString(&rhs_ss),
21597 false);
21598}

21610// INTERNAL IMPLEMENTATION - DO NOT USE IN USER CODE.
21611// A class that enables one to stream messages to assertion macros
21612class GTEST_API_ AssertHelper {
21613 public:
21614 // Constructor.
21615 AssertHelper(TestPartResult::Type type,
21616 const char* file,
21617 int line,
21618 const char* message);
21619 ~AssertHelper();
21620
21621 // Message assignment is a semantic trick to enable assertion
21622 // streaming; see the GTEST_MESSAGE_ macro below.
21623 void operator=(const Message& message) const;
21624
21625 private:
21626 // We put our data in a struct so that the size of the AssertHelper class can
21627 // be as small as possible. This is important because gcc is incapable of
21628 // re-using stack space even for temporary variables, so every EXPECT_EQ
21629 // reserves stack space for another AssertHelper.
21630 struct AssertHelperData {
21631 AssertHelperData(TestPartResult::Type t,
21632 const char* srcfile,
21633 int line_num,
21634 const char* msg)
21635 : type(t), file(srcfile), line(line_num), message(msg) { }
21636
21637 TestPartResult::Type const type;
21638 const char* const file;
21639 int const line;
21640 std::string const message;
21641
21642 private:
21643 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(AssertHelperData);
21644 };
21645
21646 AssertHelperData* const data_;
21647
21648 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(AssertHelper);
21649};

21658// The pure interface class that all value-parameterized tests inherit from.
21659// A value-parameterized class must inherit from both ::testing::Test and
21660// ::testing::WithParamInterface. In most cases that just means inheriting
21661// from ::testing::TestWithParam, but more complicated test hierarchies
21662// may need to inherit from Test and WithParamInterface at different levels.
21663//
21664// This interface has support for accessing the test parameter value via
21665// the GetParam() method.
21666//
21667// Use it with one of the parameter generator defining functions, like Range(),
21668// Values(), ValuesIn(), Bool(), and Combine().
21669//
21670// class FooTest : public ::testing::TestWithParam<int> {
21671// protected:
21672// FooTest() {
21673// // Can use GetParam() here.
21674// }
21675// virtual ~FooTest() {
21676// // Can use GetParam() here.
21677// }
21678// virtual void SetUp() {
21679// // Can use GetParam() here.
21680// }
21681// virtual void TearDown {
21682// // Can use GetParam() here.
21683// }
21684// };
21685// TEST_P(FooTest, DoesBar) {
21686// // Can use GetParam() method here.
21687// Foo foo;
21688// ASSERT_TRUE(foo.DoesBar(GetParam()));
21689// }
21690// INSTANTIATE_TEST_CASE_P(OneToTenRange, FooTest, ::testing::Range(1, 10));
21691
21692template <typename T>
21693class WithParamInterface {
21694 public:
21695 typedef T ParamType;
21696 virtual ~WithParamInterface() {}
21697
21698 // The current parameter value. Is also available in the test fixture's
21699 // constructor. This member function is non-static, even though it only
21700 // references static data, to reduce the opportunity for incorrect uses
21701 // like writing 'WithParamInterface<bool>::GetParam()' for a test that
21702 // uses a fixture whose parameter type is int.
21703 const ParamType& GetParam() const {
21704 GTEST_CHECK_(GetParameterPtrRef_() != NULL)
21705 << "GetParam() can only be called inside a value-parameterized test "
21706 << "-- did you intend to write TEST_P instead of TEST_F?";
21707 return *GetParameterPtrRef_();
21708 }

21735// Macros for indicating success/failure in test code.
21736
21737// ADD_FAILURE unconditionally adds a failure to the current test.
21738// SUCCEED generates a success - it doesn't automatically make the
21739// current test successful, as a test is only successful when it has
21740// no failure.
21741//
21742// EXPECT_* verifies that a certain condition is satisfied. If not,
21743// it behaves like ADD_FAILURE. In particular:
21744//
21745// EXPECT_TRUE verifies that a Boolean condition is true.
21746// EXPECT_FALSE verifies that a Boolean condition is false.
21747//
21748// FAIL and ASSERT_* are similar to ADD_FAILURE and EXPECT_*, except
21749// that they will also abort the current function on failure. People
21750// usually want the fail-fast behavior of FAIL and ASSERT_*, but those
21751// writing data-driven tests often find themselves using ADD_FAILURE
21752// and EXPECT_* more.

21761 ::testing::TestPartResult::kNonFatalFailure)

21763// Generates a fatal failure with a generic message.

21767// generic name and clashes with some other libraries.

21769# define FAIL() GTEST_FAIL()
21770#endif
21771
21772// Generates a success with a generic message.

21776// is a generic name and clashes with some other libraries.

21819// Macros for testing equalities and inequalities.
21820//
21821// * {ASSERT|EXPECT}_EQ(v1, v2): Tests that v1 == v2
21822// * {ASSERT|EXPECT}_NE(v1, v2): Tests that v1 != v2
21823// * {ASSERT|EXPECT}_LT(v1, v2): Tests that v1 < v2
21824// * {ASSERT|EXPECT}_LE(v1, v2): Tests that v1 <= v2
21825// * {ASSERT|EXPECT}_GT(v1, v2): Tests that v1 > v2
21826// * {ASSERT|EXPECT}_GE(v1, v2): Tests that v1 >= v2
21827//
21828// When they are not, Google Test prints both the tested expressions and
21829// their actual values. The values must be compatible built-in types,
21830// or you will get a compiler error. By "compatible" we mean that the
21831// values can be compared by the respective operator.
21832//
21833// Note:
21834//
21835// 1. It is possible to make a user-defined type work with
21836// {ASSERT|EXPECT}_??(), but that requires overloading the
21837// comparison operators and is thus discouraged by the Google C++
21838// Usage Guide. Therefore, you are advised to use the
21839// {ASSERT|EXPECT}_TRUE() macro to assert that two objects are
21840// equal.
21841//
21842// 2. The {ASSERT|EXPECT}_??() macros do pointer comparisons on
21843// pointers (in particular, C strings). Therefore, if you use it
21844// with two C strings, you are testing how their locations in memory
21845// are related, not how their content is related. To compare two C
21846// strings by content, use {ASSERT|EXPECT}_STR*().
21847//
21848// 3. {ASSERT|EXPECT}_EQ(v1, v2) is preferred to
21849// {ASSERT|EXPECT}_TRUE(v1 == v2), as the former tells you
21850// what the actual value is when it fails, and similarly for the
21851// other comparisons.
21852//
21853// 4. Do not depend on the order in which {ASSERT|EXPECT}_??()
21854// evaluate their arguments, which is undefined.
21855//
21856// 5. These macros evaluate their arguments exactly once.
21857//
21858// Examples:
21859//
21860// EXPECT_NE(Foo(), 5);
21861// EXPECT_EQ(a_pointer, NULL);
21862// ASSERT_LT(i, array_size);
21863// ASSERT_GT(records.size(), 0) << "There is no record left.";
21864
21865#define EXPECT_EQ(val1, val2) \
21866 EXPECT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal:: \
21867 EqHelper<GTEST_IS_NULL_LITERAL_(val1)>::Compare, \
21868 val1, val2)
21869#define EXPECT_NE(val1, val2) \
21870 EXPECT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal::CmpHelperNE, val1, val2)
21871#define EXPECT_LE(val1, val2) \
21872 EXPECT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal::CmpHelperLE, val1, val2)
21873#define EXPECT_LT(val1, val2) \
21874 EXPECT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal::CmpHelperLT, val1, val2)
21875#define EXPECT_GE(val1, val2) \
21876 EXPECT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal::CmpHelperGE, val1, val2)
21877#define EXPECT_GT(val1, val2) \
21878 EXPECT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal::CmpHelperGT, val1, val2)
21879
21880#define GTEST_ASSERT_EQ(val1, val2) \
21881 ASSERT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal:: \
21882 EqHelper<GTEST_IS_NULL_LITERAL_(val1)>::Compare, \
21883 val1, val2)
21884#define GTEST_ASSERT_NE(val1, val2) \
21885 ASSERT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal::CmpHelperNE, val1, val2)
21886#define GTEST_ASSERT_LE(val1, val2) \
21887 ASSERT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal::CmpHelperLE, val1, val2)
21888#define GTEST_ASSERT_LT(val1, val2) \
21889 ASSERT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal::CmpHelperLT, val1, val2)
21890#define GTEST_ASSERT_GE(val1, val2) \
21891 ASSERT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal::CmpHelperGE, val1, val2)
21892#define GTEST_ASSERT_GT(val1, val2) \
21893 ASSERT_PRED_FORMAT2(::testing::internal::CmpHelperGT, val1, val2)

21898#if !GTEST_DONT_DEFINE_ASSERT_EQ

21900#endif

22047// Causes a trace (including the given source file path and line number,
22048// and the given message) to be included in every test failure message generated
22049// by code in the scope of the lifetime of an instance of this class. The effect
22050// is undone with the destruction of the instance.
22051//
22052// The message argument can be anything streamable to std::ostream.
22053//
22054// Example:
22055// testing::ScopedTrace trace("file.cc", 123, "message");
22056//
22057class GTEST_API_ ScopedTrace {
22058 public:
22059 // The c'tor pushes the given source file location and message onto
22060 // a trace stack maintained by Google Test.
22061
22062 // Template version. Uses Message() to convert the values into strings.
22063 // Slow, but flexible.
22064 template <typename T>
22065 ScopedTrace(const char* file, int line, const T& message) {
22066 PushTrace(file, line, (Message() << message).GetString());
22067 }
22068
22069 // Optimize for some known types.
22070 ScopedTrace(const char* file, int line, const char* message) {
22071 PushTrace(file, line, message ? message : "(null)");
22072 }
22073
22074#if GTEST_HAS_GLOBAL_STRING
22075 ScopedTrace(const char* file, int line, const ::string& message) {
22076 PushTrace(file, line, message);
22077 }
22078#endif
22079
22080 ScopedTrace(const char* file, int line, const std::string& message) {
22081 PushTrace(file, line, message);
22082 }
22083
22084 // The d'tor pops the info pushed by the c'tor.
22085 //
22086 // Note that the d'tor is not virtual in order to be efficient.
22087 // Don't inherit from ScopedTrace!
22088 ~ScopedTrace();
22089
22090 private:
22091 void PushTrace(const char* file, int line, std::string message);
22092
22093 GTEST_DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN_(ScopedTrace);
22094} GTEST_ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_; // A ScopedTrace object does its job in its
22095 // c'tor and d'tor. Therefore it doesn't
22096 // need to be used otherwise.
22097
22098// Causes a trace (including the source file path, the current line
22099// number, and the given message) to be included in every test failure
22100// message generated by code in the current scope. The effect is
22101// undone when the control leaves the current scope.
22102//
22103// The message argument can be anything streamable to std::ostream.
22104//
22105// In the implementation, we include the current line number as part
22106// of the dummy variable name, thus allowing multiple SCOPED_TRACE()s
22107// to appear in the same block - as long as they are on different
22108// lines.
22109//
22110// Assuming that each thread maintains its own stack of traces.
22111// Therefore, a SCOPED_TRACE() would (correctly) only affect the
22112// assertions in its own thread.
22113#define SCOPED_TRACE(message) \
22114 ::testing::ScopedTrace GTEST_CONCAT_TOKEN_(gtest_trace_, __LINE__)(\
22115 __FILE__, __LINE__, (message))

22118// Compile-time assertion for type equality.
22119// StaticAssertTypeEq<type1, type2>() compiles iff type1 and type2 are
22120// the same type. The value it returns is not interesting.
22121//
22122// Instead of making StaticAssertTypeEq a class template, we make it a
22123// function template that invokes a helper class template. This
22124// prevents a user from misusing StaticAssertTypeEq<T1, T2> by
22125// defining objects of that type.
22126//
22127// CAVEAT:
22128//
22129// When used inside a method of a class template,
22130// StaticAssertTypeEq<T1, T2>() is effective ONLY IF the method is
22131// instantiated. For example, given:
22132//
22133// template <typename T> class Foo {
22134// public:
22135// void Bar() { testing::StaticAssertTypeEq<int, T>(); }
22136// };
22137//
22138// the code:
22139//
22140// void Test1() { Foo<bool> foo; }
22141//
22142// will NOT generate a compiler error, as Foo<bool>::Bar() is never
22143// actually instantiated. Instead, you need:
22144//
22145// void Test2() { Foo<bool> foo; foo.Bar(); }
22146//
22147// to cause a compiler error.
22148template <typename T1, typename T2>
22149bool StaticAssertTypeEq() {
22150 (void)internal::StaticAssertTypeEqHelper<T1, T2>();
22151 return true;
22152}

22154// Defines a test.
22155//
22156// The first parameter is the name of the test case, and the second
22157// parameter is the name of the test within the test case.
22158//
22159// The convention is to end the test case name with "Test". For
22160// example, a test case for the Foo class can be named FooTest.
22161//
22162// Test code should appear between braces after an invocation of
22163// this macro. Example:
22164//
22165// TEST(FooTest, InitializesCorrectly) {
22166// Foo foo;
22167// EXPECT_TRUE(foo.StatusIsOK());
22168// }
22169
22170// Note that we call GetTestTypeId() instead of GetTypeId<
22171// ::testing::Test>() here to get the type ID of testing::Test. This
22172// is to work around a suspected linker bug when using Google Test as
22173// a framework on Mac OS X. The bug causes GetTypeId<
22174// ::testing::Test>() to return different values depending on whether
22175// the call is from the Google Test framework itself or from user test
22176// code. GetTestTypeId() is guaranteed to always return the same
22177// value, as it always calls GetTypeId<>() from the Google Test
22178// framework.
22179#define GTEST_TEST(test_case_name, test_name)\
22180 GTEST_TEST_(test_case_name, test_name, \
22181 ::testing::Test, ::testing::internal::GetTestTypeId())
22182
22183// Define this macro to 1 to omit the definition of TEST(), which
22184// is a generic name and clashes with some other libraries.
22185#if !GTEST_DONT_DEFINE_TEST
22186# define TEST(test_case_name, test_name) GTEST_TEST(test_case_name, test_name)
22187#endif
22188
22189// Defines a test that uses a test fixture.
22190//
22191// The first parameter is the name of the test fixture class, which
22192// also doubles as the test case name. The second parameter is the
22193// name of the test within the test case.
22194//
22195// A test fixture class must be declared earlier. The user should put
22196// the test code between braces after using this macro. Example:
22197//
22198// class FooTest : public testing::Test {
22199// protected:
22200// virtual void SetUp() { b_.AddElement(3); }
22201//
22202// Foo a_;
22203// Foo b_;
22204// };
22205//
22206// TEST_F(FooTest, InitializesCorrectly) {
22207// EXPECT_TRUE(a_.StatusIsOK());
22208// }
22209//
22210// TEST_F(FooTest, ReturnsElementCountCorrectly) {
22211// EXPECT_EQ(a_.size(), 0);
22212// EXPECT_EQ(b_.size(), 1);
22213// }
22214
22215#define TEST_F(test_fixture, test_name)\
22216 GTEST_TEST_(test_fixture, test_name, test_fixture, \
22217 ::testing::internal::GetTypeId<test_fixture>())
